items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Pakistan’s National Cyber Emergency Response Team has issued a high-level cybersecurity advisory ahead of Defence Day, directing critical institutions to strengthen monitoring, maintain round-the-clock technical readiness, and prepare for possible cyberattacks between September 5 and 7.
The advisory calls on key public-sector bodies, critical information infrastructure operators, and sectoral and provincial CERTs to remain on heightened alert during the period. Institutions have been asked to establish dedicated cybersecurity control rooms and ensure that technical teams and designated focal persons remain available for immediate response.
The National Security Operations Centre, or NSOC, will serve as the country’s central cyber coordination point during Defence Day. It is expected to operate continuously, monitor the national cyber situation, facilitate the exchange of threat intelligence, and support a coordinated response to major incidents affecting digital infrastructure.
Authorities have also directed organizations to continuously monitor critical networks, systems, websites, and digital services and to immediately report suspicious activity, attempted intrusions, or confirmed security breaches.
Critical Systems Placed on Heightened Security
The advisory places particular emphasis on government and other sensitive digital platforms, including websites, online portals, APIs, and email services.
Institutions have been advised to activate web application firewalls and DDoS protection, ensure web-facing systems are fully updated, and apply stronger controls to administrative accounts. Multi-factor authentication has also been recommended for privileged access.
The National CERT has further instructed organizations to update operating systems, disable unnecessary services, and keep firewalls, intrusion detection systems, and intrusion prevention systems active on critical servers.
Sensitive databases should not be directly exposed through public IP addresses, while security logs should be continuously reviewed for signs of unauthorized access or unusual activity.
Officials have also stressed the need for uninterrupted coordination with the NSOC so that threat intelligence and incident information can be shared quickly across institutions.
Backup, Recovery, and Connectivity Plans Put on Standby
The advisory also focuses on operational resilience in the event of a serious cyber incident.
Critical organizations have been instructed to keep disaster recovery sites ready for immediate use and maintain offline or air-gapped backups of important systems, configurations, and data. Recovery mechanisms should also be tested in advance rather than relied upon without verification.
Data centers and security operations centers have been advised to ensure backup internet connectivity and uninterrupted power arrangements, including UPS and generator support.
Technical teams have also been told to remain prepared for rapid escalation, communication and incident response if an attack is detected.
The measures reflect growing concern over coordinated cyber threats against public-facing and critical digital systems during high-profile national events. With multiple institutions expected to operate under heightened vigilance, authorities are aiming to reduce the risk of service disruption, data compromise, and wider impact on Pakistan’s digital infrastructure.

items.title: Simple Energy Catches The Mass-Market Wave
items.summary:
After years of chasing premium and performance-focused buyers, EV startups are now setting their sights on the mass market. While EV startups initially built their propositions around consumers willing to pay a premium for longer range, connected features and differentiated riding experiences, that playbook has started to change.
With electric two-wheelers moving deeper into the mainstream, manufacturers are increasingly looking beyond the early-adopter customer to the much larger pool of family and commuter buyers. Ola Electric and Ather Energy recently introduced more affordable, family-oriented scooters. Now, Bengaluru-based Simple Energy is joining the race with its new Wave range.
Earlier this month, the union government halved the incentive for registered electric two-wheelers (E2Ws) to ₹2,500 per kWh of battery capacity, capped at ₹5,000 per vehicle from April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2028, compared to ₹5,000 per kWh, capped at ₹10,000 per vehicle, under the FY25 scheme.
With policy
items.author: Gargi Sarkar
items.content:
After years of chasing premium and performance-focused buyers, EV startups are now setting their sights on the mass market. While EV startups initially built their propositions around consumers willing to pay a premium for longer range, connected features and differentiated riding experiences, that playbook has started to change.
With electric two-wheelers moving deeper into the mainstream, manufacturers are increasingly looking beyond the early-adopter customer to the much larger pool of family and commuter buyers. Ola Electric and Ather Energy recently introduced more affordable, family-oriented scooters. Now, Bengaluru-based Simple Energy is joining the race with its new Wave range.
Earlier this month, the union government halved the incentive for registered electric two-wheelers (E2Ws) to ₹2,500 per kWh of battery capacity, capped at ₹5,000 per vehicle from April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2028, compared to ₹5,000 per kWh, capped at ₹10,000 per vehicle, under the FY25 scheme.
With policy support becoming more modest, affordability is emerging as an increasingly important lever for adoption, particularly as manufacturers look to expand beyond premium early adopters and tap the much larger commuter segment in India’s $30 Bn two-wheeler market. This is the segment that Simple is also going after.
Launched at an introductory starting price of ₹1.10 Lakh (ex-showroom), the Simple Wave marks a significant expansion of the startup’s portfolio, which was previously anchored by the performance-oriented Simple One. The new lineup comprises six models across three variants. Bookings have opened across Simple Energy’s stores and website, with deliveries scheduled to begin in the last week of September.
But the Wave is about more than adding another scooter to Simple Energy’s portfolio. For the startup, it is a bet that the next leg of India’s EV adoption will come from the mass market.
From Performance To Family Scooters
Simple Energy was founded in 2019 by Suhas Rajkumar and Shreshth Mishra, with Ankit Gupta later joining as a cofounder. Its first product, the Simple One, positioned the company around performance and long-range electric mobility. The Wave represents a deliberate broadening of that proposition.
“We definitely want to scale up and become a part of the top five clubs. Hopefully, in the top three very soon, depending on how we scale from here,” founder and CEO Rajkumar said.
According to him, the family scooter is primarily about expanding Simple Energy’s presence across India by giving consumers a more affordable entry point into its portfolio. “When you make an affordable offering, it scales up your production; it scales up your volumes.”
The Wave models are intended to serve as an entry point for a larger mass audience. The shift comes at a time when the broader electric two-wheeler industry is also moving in the same direction. EV manufacturers are increasingly trying to compete for customers who would otherwise buy a conventional petrol scooter.
Ola Electric recently launched the S1Z in two variants priced at ₹79,999 and ₹99,999, with IDC-certified ranges of 179 km and 301 km. The S1Z is also the company’s first scooter range powered by its locally developed 46-series LFP Bharat Cell technology.
Ather Energy, meanwhile, launched the Konarc family scooter at a starting price of ₹99,999. Built on the company’s new EL platform, the Konarc is available in six variants across the S and Z product lines, with range options spanning 100 km to 200 km.
For these players, as well as for Simple Energy, the new launches mean competing not just against each other and fellow EV startups but against the entrenched two-wheeler industry.
Rajkumar explicitly spelt this out: “ICE products are definitely a competition. Our objective is to change the way people move from petrol to EVs. The competition is not about how we can price better or undercut the competition. It’s more to do with how much more value we can give to the consumer at that price point.”
From 1,500 Scooters To 10,000 A Month
The larger challenge for Simple Energy is not necessarily finding demand, but building enough capacity and distribution to capture the natural demand in the market for EVs.
The company currently has manufacturing capacity of around 3,000 scooters a month and says it is selling roughly 1,500 units a month. It wants to take monthly sales and manufacturing to 10,000 units by March 2027.
That would represent more than a six-fold increase from its current monthly sales run rate. Rajkumar believes the Wave can help unlock that growth, particularly as an affordable family scooter can tap into demand beyond the company’s existing customer base.
“The current tailwind of the industry kind of takes up a definite demand that is already there. And when you add a family scooter with a more affordable price tag, I think it only escalates that current demand as well,” he said.
Simple Energy also plans to substantially expand its retail footprint. The company currently has around 90 stores across 61 cities, and is targeting 160-170 outlets by March 2027.
Importantly, these are dealer-operated outlets, rather than company-owned stores. This allows Simple Energy to expand its physical presence without taking on the entire capital burden of establishing and operating each outlet.
While the company believes its existing network could potentially absorb significant additional demand, Rajkumar said the expansion is being undertaken conservatively to ensure that the retail network keeps pace with production and manufacturing capacity.
At the moment, that is the bottleneck. Rajkumar said the company’s 1,500-unit monthly sales are not primarily a result of weak demand or distribution constraints, but supply limitations.
“It’s more supply constraint, not distribution or demand. It’s the manufacturing side of it. That’s the most problematic piece for us today,” the CEO said.
This makes capacity expansion particularly important if Simple Energy is to deliver on its 10,000-unit monthly target on sales and manufacturing. The startup expects manufacturing capacity to reach 75-80% of this target by the end of the next financial year, from around 30% currently.
The company also claims that around 95% of its components are localised, an important factor as EV manufacturers increasingly seek greater control over their supply chains and costs.
Betting On Scale, While Costs Remain A Challenge
The Wave’s ₹1.10 Lakh introductory price is another important part of Simple Energy’s strategy.
The company has positioned the price as an introductory offer rather than necessarily a permanent price point. Yet despite the lower entry price, Rajkumar expects the Wave portfolio to generate a contribution margin of around 20-25% over the next eight to 12 months.
That makes the economics of the mass-market push particularly important. Affordable scooters can potentially unlock significantly higher volumes, but they also leave less room for cost inefficiencies.
And commodity inflation is already putting pressure on the sector. Rajkumar said commodity prices have increased sharply, with costs rising roughly 25-30% over the past two quarters, impacting margins across the industry.
Achieving the contribution margin in this atmosphere will be a challenge, and it’s one that Simple has dealt with throughout its existence, as Rajkumar acknowledged. “Supply chain has always been a problem since 2020. Today, the margins have dropped significantly because of the commodity price increase,” he said.
This pressure can persist for at least another 12 months, although the company anticipates some easing after 18-24 months.
In June, the startup raised ₹250 Cr through a mix of debt and equity. The capital is being deployed primarily towards manufacturing capacity and production expansion, with the balance earmarked for sales, marketing and R&D.
The fundraise is also part of the company’s broader ambition to transition into a full-stack electric vehicle OEM and eventually prepare for an IPO.
The company reported revenue of around ₹171 Cr in FY26, as the founder claimed, up sharply from roughly ₹44 Cr in FY25. Rajkumar attributed the growth largely to the underlying demand for its products rather than any single growth lever.
“For us, the demand is there. We just have to multiply our production,” he said.
That, in many ways, captures Simple Energy’s immediate challenge.
India’s electric two-wheeler market is growing rapidly, but competition is becoming considerably broader. Vahan data showed electric two-wheeler registrations falling 16.2% month-on-month to 1.72 Lakh units in August, although registrations were still up 64% year-on-year.
As Ola, Ather, Simple Energy and traditional automakers such as TVS Motor, Bajaj Auto and Hero MotoCorp push further into affordable EVs, the next phase of the market is likely to be less about convincing affluent early adopters and more about winning the everyday commuter.
For Simple Energy, the Wave is therefore both a product launch and a scale test. If the company succeeds, it could move closer to the top-five in the market and eventually the top-three position that it is eyeing.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Signify menggelar Signify Innovation Day Light the Future di Jakarta pada 2 September 2026. Acara ini mempertemukan sejumlah pemangku kepentingan dari sektor pemerintahan, properti, hingga industri untuk membahas pemanfaatan teknologi pencahayaan dalam pengembangan kota pintar dan layak huni serta bangunan yang lebih adaptif terhadap kebutuhan masa depan.
Pembahasan tersebut turut dikaitkan dengan agenda pembangunan berkelanjutan di Indonesia, termasuk target Net Zero Emission (NZE) pada 2060 atau lebih cepat. Dalam konteks ini, pencahayaan tidak lagi sekadar diposisikan sebagai fasilitas penerangan, tetapi juga bagian dari infrastruktur yang dapat memengaruhi efisiensi energi, keamanan, kenyamanan, dan operasional sebuah kawasan atau bangunan.
Meski demikian, penerapan teknologi pencahayaan pintar tetap membutuhkan dukungan dari sisi kebijakan, investasi, serta kesiapan infrastruktur. Efisiensi yang ditawarkan teknologi tidak otomatis menghasilkan penghematan apabila implementasinya tidak disesuaikan dengan kebutuhan di lapangan. Karena itu, Signify Innovation Day juga membahas aspek kebijakan, pembiayaan, dan penerapan teknologi secara lebih luas.
Baca Juga: WiZ Smart Lighting Hadir, Hias Rumah Jadi dengan Ragam Warna
Pencahayaan untuk Kota yang Lebih Cerdas
Salah satu produk Signify yang sudah dipakai untuk berbagai keperluan stadion olahraga di indonesia (Foto: Louis/Gizmologi)
Salah satu sesi bertajuk “Future of Smart & Liveable Cities: Driving Sustainability Through Innovation and Circularity” membahas strategi pembangunan kota berbasis data serta penerapan prinsip sirkularitas. Diskusi melibatkan perwakilan Kementerian Dalam Negeri, Kementerian PPN/Bappenas, Dinas Bina Marga Provinsi DKI Jakarta, dan Signify Indonesia.
Salah satu contoh yang dibahas adalah transisi menuju lampu LED dan sistem pencahayaan pintar pada Penerangan Jalan Umum (PJU) di Jakarta. Teknologi semacam ini berpotensi membantu pengelolaan energi dan operasional secara lebih efisien. Namun, penerapannya juga perlu mempertimbangkan investasi awal, pemeliharaan, serta kompatibilitas dengan infrastruktur yang sudah tersedia.
Bangunan Future-Ready Tak Hanya Soal Efisiensi
Produk Signify yang sudah dipergunakan untuk beberapa layanan publik di Indonesia (Foto: Louis/Gizmologi)
Sesi kedua mengangkat tema “Achieving Sustainability Goals and Business Growth Through Future-Ready Buildings”. Forum ini mempertemukan praktisi dari sektor properti, hospitality, fasilitas gedung, ESG, dan green building untuk membahas hubungan antara keberlanjutan dan kebutuhan bisnis.
Dalam pembahasan tersebut, teknologi pencahayaan ditempatkan sebagai salah satu komponen dalam pengelolaan bangunan yang lebih efisien. Sistem pencahayaan pintar dapat membantu mengatur penggunaan energi sekaligus mendukung kenyamanan penghuni. Meski begitu, pencahayaan hanya menjadi salah satu bagian dari strategi bangunan berkelanjutan yang juga mencakup sistem energi, tata kelola, material, dan operasional.
Selain diskusi, Signify turut menampilkan demo sejumlah solusi pencahayaan untuk berbagai kebutuhan profesional, termasuk perkantoran, industri, data center, hotel, stadion, fasad, lanskap, dan penerangan jalan. Acara ini menunjukkan bahwa arah pengembangan pencahayaan kini semakin terintegrasi dengan isu efisiensi energi dan pengelolaan infrastruktur, meski keberhasilan implementasinya tetap bergantung pada kebutuhan serta kondisi masing-masing sektor.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Qualcomm Technologies dan HUMAIN memperkenalkan Horizon Ultra, perangkat PC generasi baru yang dirancang dengan fokus pada pemrosesan artificial intelligence (AI) langsung di perangkat. Produk tersebut diperkenalkan dalam ajang LEAP 2026 dan menjadi hasil pengembangan bersama selama lebih dari 12 bulan, dengan Snapdragon X2 Elite sebagai platform komputasi utamanya.
Horizon Ultra menjadi bagian dari upaya HUMAIN membawa kemampuan AI lebih dekat ke pengguna, alih-alih sepenuhnya bergantung pada pusat data atau layanan cloud. Generasi pertama perangkat ini akan menjalankan Microsoft Windows, sehingga secara penggunaan masih berada dalam lingkungan PC yang sudah umum digunakan, terutama untuk kebutuhan perusahaan.
Namun, HUMAIN sudah menyiapkan arah berbeda untuk generasi berikutnya. Perusahaan berencana menghadirkan HUMAIN OS pada lini Horizon Ultra mulai 2027. Sistem operasi tersebut ditujukan untuk memberikan integrasi yang lebih dalam antara perangkat, kemampuan AI, dan ekosistem teknologi HUMAIN.
Baca Juga: Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Punya Dua Varian, Qualcomm Konfirmasi Meluncur September
Snapdragon X2 Elite Jadi Otak Horizon Ultra
Horizon Ultra menggunakan Snapdragon X2 Elite yang memiliki CPU Qualcomm Oryon 18-core, GPU Qualcomm Adreno, serta NPU Qualcomm Hexagon. Ketiganya memungkinkan beban kerja dibagi ke komponen yang berbeda, termasuk pemrosesan AI yang dapat dijalankan secara lokal melalui NPU.
Pendekatan tersebut memungkinkan sebagian model dan fitur AI berjalan tanpa harus terus-menerus mengirimkan data ke cloud. Secara teori, pemrosesan lokal dapat membantu responsivitas dan memungkinkan data tertentu tetap berada di perangkat. Namun, kemampuan tersebut tetap bergantung pada model AI, optimasi software, serta jenis beban kerja yang dijalankan.
Menargetkan Penggunaan Enterprise
HUMAIN juga memosisikan Horizon Ultra sebagai perangkat untuk kebutuhan enterprise. Pemrosesan AI di endpoint dapat menjadi pilihan untuk skenario yang membutuhkan respons cepat, konektivitas yang terbatas, atau pengelolaan data tertentu secara lokal. Pada saat yang sama, perangkat tetap dapat terhubung ke layanan cloud ketika membutuhkan kapasitas komputasi lebih besar.
Untuk penjualan dan distribusi enterprise, HUMAIN menunjuk AlFalak sebagai mitra. Horizon Ultra yang menjalankan Windows dijadwalkan tersedia untuk pembelian perusahaan mulai 20 September 2026.
Peluncuran ini menunjukkan arah pengembangan PC yang mulai menempatkan AI sebagai bagian dari arsitektur perangkat, bukan sekadar fitur tambahan di dalam aplikasi. Meski demikian, seberapa besar manfaat pendekatan tersebut dalam penggunaan nyata masih perlu dilihat melalui pengujian performa, efisiensi, kompatibilitas aplikasi, serta pengalaman pengguna setelah perangkat tersedia di pasar.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
D2C smart crib brand Cradlewise has raised $12 Mn (about ₹xx Cr) in a Series A funding round led by 3one4 Capital and Prudent Investment Management.
The San Francisco-headquartered startup plans to deploy the fresh capital towards growth, channel expansion, product R&D, and entry into new international markets.
Cradlewise, which currently sells its products through its own website and ecommerce marketplaces, plans to widen its distribution through offline retail stores, partnerships, and other channels. The startup said the strategy would help it reach parents across multiple touchpoints without relying on a single route to market.
Founded in 2019 by husband-wife duo Radhika and Bharath Patil, Cradlewise manufactures an AI-enabled smart crib that uses sensors and an integrated monitor to detect when a baby begins stirring. It then automatically bounces the crib to help soothe the baby back to sleep.
The crib connects to an app that allows parents to monitor their baby remotely, track sleep patterns, and access sleep-related insights. The system also learns a baby’s individual sleep patterns over time to personalise its response.
Cradlewise’s products currently cater to children aged up to 24 months.
The startup said its technology is backed by patents covering its hardware and sensing systems. Its connected products have generated more than 75 Mn hours of sleep data, which it uses to improve sleep detection, predict when a baby may stir, and personalise the experience.
With the fresh funding, the D2C startup plans to expand its portfolio beyond cribs and develop sleep products for older children.
Its roadmap includes software-led sleep routines, other child sleep hardware products, lower-priced entry points, and reusable sensing and electronics modules that could shorten future product development cycles.
The latest round takes Cradlewise’s total funding raised to $26 Mn. Its investors include Sean O’Sullivan Ventures, Footwork VC, Charles River Ventures, 3one4 Capital, and Prudent Investment Management.
Prior to this, Cradlewise raised $7 Mn in its seed funding round in 2021.
Sleeptech Opportunity Expands
The development comes at a time when India’s sleeptech market is moving beyond its traditional mattress-led playbook.
While new-age brands initially disrupted the category by making mattresses and other sleep essentials more accessible through the D2C model, the opportunity is now expanding into a broader ecosystem of technology-led sleep products.
DUSQ, initially launched as InnerGize, raised ₹24 Cr in February to develop wearables designed to regulate sleep using vagus nerve stimulation and smart sensors, instead of merely tracking sleep metrics.
The shift is also visible among established consumer brands.
In 2024, mattress brand Wakefit entered the sleep technology segment with its Zense platform, which uses connected technology to track sleep patterns and offer insights into sleep quality, movement, and other physiological parameters. It also allows users to optimise their sleeping environment.

items.title: The Ayurveda Co Shuts Down After Overexpansion Derails Business
items.summary:
D2C ayurvedic beauty and personal care brand The Ayurveda Co (T.A.C) has shut down, more than a year after it ceased operations, cofounder Param Bhargava said in a LinkedIn post.
Bhargava announced the closure of both T.A.C and its sister brand Khadi Essentials, adding that the startups stopped operations in July 2025. Their assets have since been liquidated, and the entities are now undergoing a formal winding-up process.

items.author: Palak Sharma
items.content:
D2C ayurvedic beauty and personal care brand The Ayurveda Co (T.A.C) has shut down, more than a year after it ceased operations, cofounder Param Bhargava said in a LinkedIn post.
Bhargava announced the closure of both T.A.C and its sister brand Khadi Essentials, adding that the startups stopped operations in July 2025. Their assets have since been liquidated, and the entities are now undergoing a formal winding-up process.
“Taking the hardest pill for now and shutting down my second love, The Ayurveda Co and Khadi Essentials,” Bhargava wrote.
He attributed the failure to the startup expanding faster than its systems and business could support.
“We expanded too fast, too wide, and (hired) way too many senior folks too early, before the system was ready,” Bhargava said, adding that the startup’s ambitions ran ahead of what the business could sustainably support.
The cofounder said the team tried to keep the business afloat by mortgaging parental property, while the cofounders did not withdraw salaries for more than a year. He added that the pressure of trying to turn around the business led to physical and mental breakdowns.
Bhargava took responsibility for the failure, saying there were several decisions he would make differently today.
Founded in 2021 by Bhargava and Shreedha Singh, T.A.C sold ayurvedic products across skincare, haircare, natural makeup, wellness, and supplements. The founders had earlier launched Khadi Essentials in 2019.
The startup sold its products through its website, ecommerce marketplaces, exclusive outlets, and multibrand stores.
As per Bhargava, the startup owned 20 retail stores and had more than 800 beauty advisor counters and a network of 110 operational distributors. He said the brand scaled to ₹250 Cr in net revenue and had 20 Lakh consumers.
T.A.C. raised a total of $15 Mn in funding to date from Sixth Sense Ventures, Wipro Consumer Care Venture, and a host of angel investors, including actor Kajal Aggarwal.
The startup last raised ₹100 Cr in its Series A funding round in 2023.
T.A.C’s FY24 revenue grew 67% YoY to ₹59.6 Cr, while loss tripled to ₹68 Cr on the back of expenses that nearly doubled to ₹109.5 Cr.
With the closure, T.A.C has joined a growing list of Indian startups that have shut down operations in 2026. Earlier this week, Savtacart shut shop after failed funding and acquisition discussions. Last month, social networking platform Medial announced its closure after failing to raise fresh funding amid a cash crunch.
Koo cofounder Mayank Bidawatka also shut down his AI-powered photo-sharing startup PicSee after it failed to achieve the scale required to sustain operations. The list also includes quick commerce startup Klydo and online matchmaking platform Juleo.

items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
vivo is preparing to expand its flagship smartphone lineup with the upcoming vivo X500 series, and the company has now officially revealed key camera specifications for the standard X500 ahead of its expected China launch this month.
The series is expected to include the vivo X500, X500 Pro, and X500 Pro Max, with vivo gradually disclosing specifications as the launch approaches. The latest details suggest the standard X500 will carry significantly more capable camera hardware than a typical base flagship.
According to vivo, the X500 will feature a 50MP Sony LYT-828 primary sensor measuring 1/1.28 inches. The same sensor is used in the current vivo X300 Pro, indicating that the company is bringing premium imaging hardware to the standard model rather than reserving it entirely for the Pro variants.
The main camera will also feature ZEISS gimbal-level stabilization and carry a CIPA 5.5 professional stabilization rating, which should help improve handheld photography, low-light shooting, and video stability.
For zoom photography, the vivo X500 will use a 64MP Sony LYT-610 telephoto sensor, the same sensor confirmed for the X500 Pro. The telephoto camera will also receive a CIPA 5.5 stabilization rating and support 4K slow-motion video recording at 120 fps.
The device is additionally confirmed to support a 200 mm teleconverter, potentially giving users significantly greater reach for distant subjects, portraits, and travel photography.
Reports also suggest that the X500 could feature a 50MP ultrawide camera, alongside a 6.37-inch display and a 3nm MediaTek Dimensity 9000-series chipset, although vivo has yet to officially confirm these specifications.
vivo X500 Expected Price in Pakistan
vivo has not announced official Pakistani pricing for the X500 series, and any figure circulating at this stage should therefore be treated as an estimate.
The previous vivo X300 Pro launched in Pakistan at around Rs. 349,999, providing some indication of how vivo positions its premium X-series devices locally. The standard X500, however, is expected to sit below the Pro variants and could therefore arrive at a considerably lower price point.
Based on its expected positioning and current unofficial estimates, the vivo X500 could be priced somewhere between Rs. 170,000 and Rs. 220,000 in Pakistan, depending on the storage configuration, taxes, and exchange-rate conditions at the time of launch.
The X500 Pro and Pro Max, if introduced locally, would likely command significantly higher prices.
Pricing could also vary depending on whether vivo launches the devices officially through its Pakistani distribution network or whether initial units reach the market through unofficial import channels.
vivo X500 Pakistan Release Timeline
The vivo X500 series is scheduled to debut in China during September 2026, but vivo has not yet confirmed an international or Pakistani launch date.
Pakistan typically receives selected X-series models after their initial Chinese or global release rather than simultaneously. If vivo follows a similar rollout strategy this year, the X500 could reach Pakistan towards the end of 2026 or during the opening months of 2027.
A local launch would also depend on which X500 variants vivo chooses to introduce. The company may bring only selected models from the lineup rather than the entire X500 family.
For Pakistani buyers, the standard X500 could be particularly interesting if vivo maintains its premium camera hardware while keeping the price below the Pro models. The combination of a 50MP Sony flagship sensor, ZEISS stabilization, 64MP telephoto camera and 200mm teleconverter support could make it one of the strongest camera-focused options in its segment.
For now, the China launch will provide the clearest picture of the X500’s complete specifications, pricing and configurations, after which more concrete details about its global and Pakistani availability are expected to emerge.

Acer Project DualPlay Mini memiliki dua mode penggunaan
items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Acer Project DualPlay Mini baru saja dipamerkan di ajang tahunan IFA 2026 di Berlin. Tampil sebagai konsep handheld gaming 8 inci, perangkat ini dapat berubah bentuk menjadi mini-laptop dengan keyboard fisik bawaan.
Perusahaan asal Taiwan ini memamerkan handheld gaming berdampingan dengan Predator Atlas 7. Walau tampil di secara langsung di Berlin, Acer menegaskan Project DualPlay Mini ini masih berstatus konsep, alias belum ada harga atau jadwal rilis.
Acer menyebutkan, mekanisme transformasi perangkat ini sebagai flip-and-swivel design. Saat ditutup, perangkat ini tampil seperti handheld gaming pada umumnya, lengkap dengan analog stick, D-pad, tombol ABXY, dan tombol bahu.
Namun saat layar dibuka dan diputar, terlihat keyboard backlit tersembunyi di bagian dalam. Lalu apa fungsi mode keyboard di Project DualPlay Mini ini?
Apa Fungsi Mode Keyboard di Acer Project DualPlay Mini?
Acer Project DualPlay Mini di IFA 2026. (Doc: Acer)
Acer Project DualPlay Mini memiliki dua mode penggunaan berbeda dalam satu perangkat, dengan mode handheld layaknya perangkat gaming portablet pada umumnya.
Ketika dibuka, layar bisa diputar dan memperlihatkan keyboard backlit. Acer menjelaskan, mode ini ditujukan untuk gamer yang ingin melakukan pekerjaan ringan atau game PC lebih nyaman saat bermain dengan keyboard dan mouse, seperti game first-person shooter.
Seperti handheld gaming PC lainnya, perusahaan menyediakan mode eksternal di mana Acer Project DualMini ini dapat dihubungkan ke monitor eksternal agar bisa main dengan tampilan lebih besar.
Spesifikasi Project DualPlay Mini
Sayang, raksasa teknologi asal Taiwan ini belum memberikan informasi lebih detail tentang spesifikasi Acer Project DualPlay Mini. Hanya saja, perangkat ini berjalan menggunakan chipset Intel.
Perusahaan juga menyebutkan, Acer Project DualPlay Mini ini sudah mengadopsi arsitektur dual-fan yang serupa dengan Predator Atlas 8 — satu kipas Predator AeroBlade berbahan metal dengan bilah lebih tipis, satu kipas plastik.
Dengan status tersebut, Acer Project DualPlay Mini belum memiliki jadwal penjualan global maupun informasi mengenai kemungkinan ketersediaannya di Indonesia.
Apakah Konsep Handheld dengan Keyboard Ini Hal Baru?
Acer DualPlay Mini di IFA 2026. (Doc: Acer)
Tidak. Ayaneo sempat merilis FLIP KB pada 2024 dengan desain clamshell dan keyboard fisik terintegrasi, sementara GPD memiliki seri WIN Mini menggabungkan layar 7 inci, kontrol gaming, keyboard, dan Windows dalam satu desain clamshell.
Perbedaan utama Acer Project DualPlay Mini terletak pada mekanismenya: perangkat tetap berbentuk handheld konvensional saat tertutup, lalu layar dibuka dan diputar untuk mengekspos keyboard di dalamnya, bukan desain clamshell dari awal seperti kompetitornya.
Acer Perkenalkan Lini Laptop 3D dan PC AIO di IFA 2026
Acer memperluas lini perangkat Aspire dengan memperkenalkan sejumlah produk baru untuk kebutuhan komputasi yang berbeda. Dalam ajang Next@Acer di Berlin, perusahaan memperkenalkan Aspire G 3D 16 sebagai laptop yang mengandalkan teknologi layar 3D tanpa kacamata, serta Aspire S 27 dan Aspire S 24 sebagai PC all-in-one (AIO) untuk kebutuhan rumahan.
Aspire G 3D 16 menjadi produk yang paling berbeda di antara perangkat baru tersebut. Laptop ini membawa layar IPS 16 inci dengan resolusi WQXGA+ 3840 x 2400 piksel dan refresh rate 120Hz. Ketika digunakan dalam mode 3D, resolusinya menjadi 1920 x 2400 piksel. Acer juga menyematkan teknologi SpatialLabs yang memungkinkan konten 2D dikonversi menjadi tampilan 3D.
Di sisi performa, Acer Aspire G 3D 16 menggunakan AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 dengan grafis Radeon 8060S, RAM LPDDR5x-8000 hingga 128GB, serta SSD hingga 2TB. Laptop ini juga membawa baterai 99,9 Wh, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4, dua port USB 4 Type-C, serta keyboard RGB dengan tombol WASD berwarna merah.
Aspire G 3D 16 Andalkan Teknologi SpatialLabs
Teknologi 3D pada Acer Aspire G 3D 16 menggunakan dua kamera pelacak untuk menyesuaikan tampilan dengan posisi pengguna. Sistem tersebut memungkinkan konten 2D seperti foto dan video dikonversi menjadi visual 3D melalui SpatialLabs 3D Hub.
Namun, pengalaman 3D tetap bergantung pada konten, aplikasi, dan konfigurasi perangkat. Acer sendiri mencatat bahwa kualitas konversi 2D ke 3D dapat berbeda tergantung sumbernya. Artinya, fitur tersebut memang menarik untuk kreator dan pengguna yang sering bekerja dengan konten visual, tetapi belum tentu menjadi kebutuhan utama bagi semua pengguna laptop.
Aspire S 27 dan S 24 Fokus untuk Keluarga
Untuk segmen penggunaan rumahan, Acer memperbarui Aspire S 27 dan Aspire S 24. Keduanya menggunakan prosesor Intel Core 7 350 dan menjalankan Windows 11. Acer Aspire S 27 memiliki layar 27 inci dengan pilihan panel QHD 120Hz atau FHD 144Hz, sedangkan Aspire S 24 menggunakan panel FHD 144Hz.
Kedua AIO tersebut mempertahankan desain minimalis dengan bezel tipis dan rasio layar terhadap bodi 90 persen. Acer juga menyediakan opsi layar sentuh yang mendukung stylus, RAM hingga 16GB, SSD hingga 1TB, webcam FHD dengan privacy shutter, serta konektivitas Wi-Fi 6E.
Acer belum mengungkapkan harga dan ketersediaan masing-masing produk untuk pasar Indonesia. Perusahaan menyebut spesifikasi, harga, serta ketersediaan dapat berbeda di setiap wilayah, sehingga informasi lokal masih perlu menunggu pengumuman resmi Acer Indonesia.

items.author: Inc42 BrandLabs
items.content:
Despite growing demand for non-invasive aesthetic treatments such as laser hair reduction, skin resurfacing, pigmentation removal and chemical peels, access remains a challenge.
For many, the biggest hurdle isn’t the treatment but everything that comes before it. Booking an appointment, travelling to a clinic, waiting despite having a confirmed slot, paying a random consultation fee and filling out lengthy forms can make a 30-minute procedure a half-day job.
As convenience becomes a bigger part of everyday life, people now expect aesthetic treatments to be as easy to access as salon services or grocery deliveries.
This has paved the way for a new model: bringing advanced aesthetic treatments straight to people’s homes. And Yes Madam is betting on this shift.
The scale of this demand is reflected in India’s growing adoption of non-surgical aesthetics. According to the International Society of Aesthetic Plastic Surgery (ISAPS), 611,800 non-surgical aesthetic procedures were performed in India in 2024, with hair removal alone accounting for 208,880 procedures, making it the most common non-surgical aesthetic procedure in the country.
Yet unlike conventional salon services, treatments involving lasers, radio frequency or other specialised technologies require trained professionals, calibrated equipment and tighter hygiene protocols. These requirements have traditionally kept advanced aesthetics within specialised clinical settings.
Advanced Aesthetic Treatments Available At Home
Taking these treatments into the home isn’t as simple as replacing a salon chair with a living room sofa. It requires a fundamentally different operating model.
To bridge that gap, Yes Madam has expanded its at-home salon model to include protocol-driven, dermatologist-designed aesthetic treatments delivered by certified professionals using professional-grade equipment.
Instead of customer-facing clinics, it relies on backend equipment hubs, reducing infrastructure costs and offering treatments that are typically 35-55% cheaper than conventional clinics.
However, affordability alone isn’t enough for procedures traditionally associated with skin clinics. For at-home treatments to work, consumers need confidence that safety, equipment quality and clinical oversight are not being compromised.
To build trust, Yes Madam has standardised every part of the treatment process — from the equipment used to the way every procedure is performed. To maintain consistent quality and safety, the company:
Trains professionals using dermatologist-designed protocols
Uses fresh, single-use consumables for every session
Centrally monitors equipment across its service hubs
Limits its portfolio to non-invasive procedures that do not require continuous medical supervision
 
Inside Yes Madam’s New Home Stack
With that operational framework in place, Yes Madam’s advanced aesthetics portfolio addresses a range of common skin and body concerns through non-invasive treatments delivered at home.
Laser Hair Reduction: Multi-wavelength diode laser technology with ice-cooling targets unwanted hair across different skin tones, with treatments ranging from underarms to full-body sessions priced between approximately ₹1,150 and ₹7,500 per session. According to data shared by Yes Madam, customers completing a full course of 6 sessions typically achieve a 70-80% permanent reduction that is consistent with clinical outcomes.
Q-Switched Nd:YAG Laser: Combines laser, carbon peel and LED technologies to reduce pigmentation, tanning, acne marks and uneven skin tone while improving skin texture. According to Yes Madam’s data, its customers report a visible reduction in acne marks within the first 3-4 sessions.
Body Toning: Combines radio frequency (RF), electrical muscle stimulation (EMS), cavitation and controlled heating to contour stubborn fat deposits without invasive procedures. The brand claims to deliver the service in under 60 mins with a safe and protocol-driven procedure.
HydraGlo Facials: Combine abrasion, radio frequency and oxygen infusion to hydrate and rejuvenate the skin through variants such as Korean HydraGlo, Insta Collagen Boost, Hydration Boost, De-Tan and Intensive Pore Clean-Up. This procedure has become Yes Madam’s fastest-growing treatment (by bookings) and is increasingly popular among male consumers aged 28-40. Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru and Pune remain the cities with maximum traction from women customers.
Expanding The TAM: What Lies Ahead
As advanced aesthetic procedures become part of routine self-care, growing demand for convenience, privacy and transparent pricing is expanding the market for at-home treatments.
Yes Madam has its eyes on first-time users, while expanding into Hyderabad, Kolkata, Chennai and Ahmedabad. It targets building a ₹500 Cr advanced aesthetics business in the next five years.
The startup is sure that the future of advanced aesthetics may not be defined by larger clinics or more premium retail spaces, but by making clinical-grade treatments more accessible to everyday consumers.
Just as convenience has transformed food delivery, mobility and even healthcare, companies like Yes Madam are helping redefine where and how professional aesthetic care can be delivered by bringing dermatologist-supervised, non-invasive technologies directly into people’s homes.

items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Ride-hailing major Uber is laying off around 200-250 employees in India as part of a broader global restructuring that will see the company eliminate about 3,300 roles.
The India layoffs, which are expected to impact both individual contributors and managers, come barely six months after Uber cut around 80 jobs in the country. The latest exercise is expected to primarily affect the company’s technology and operations teams, with its AI solutions team slashed by half, according to an ET report citing sources.
Responding to Inc42’s queries, an Uber spokesperson said, “Globally, we are making organisational changes to remove layers so we can move faster. As part of these changes, we will be saying goodbye to some valued team members in India, whom we will support through this transition. Our commitment to India as a key market, and our ambition to innovate locally for riders and drivers, remain unchanged – in fact, we are expanding India’s strategic footprint by strengthening our regional operations here to drive our mobility business across Asia-Pacific.”
Globally, Uber is cutting about 10% of its workforce as it looks to simplify its organisational structure, reduce management layers, and redirect resources towards its core mobility and delivery businesses as well as its autonomous vehicle ambitions.
Uber CEO Dara Khosrowshahi, in a note to employees, said the company has become increasingly complex following years of rapid expansion, with additional layers of management, greater coordination requirements and fragmented ownership slowing down decision-making.
The company plans to reduce by around 20% the number of employees who sit seven or more organisational layers below the CEO. It will also nearly halve the number of “micro-teams” with only one or two direct reports and consolidate several functions, the company said in a blog post.
Uber is also merging its separate delivery operations teams covering restaurants, retail and direct delivery, while bringing together its core services engineering and science teams.
The company said the savings generated from the organisational reset would be redirected towards growth, innovation and capabilities that will be important to its future. It also plans to invest more than $10 Bn in autonomous vehicle technology over the coming years as robotaxis threaten to reshape the traditional ride-hailing model.
Uber said the restructuring followed a period of strong business performance, with its top line tripling over the past five years as it added products, expanded into new businesses, and reached more consumers and earners.
As part of the restructuring, Uber will also ask the vast majority of its remote employees to return to the office. Going forward, only around 1% of its employees will work remotely, while the company will continue enforcing its hybrid policy requiring employees to work from the office three days a week.
Uber India Cuts Come Amid Broader Reset
The layoffs come at a time when Uber is stepping up its investments in India, particularly in technology and AI.
In February this year, the company infused nearly ₹3,000 Cr into its India arm, Uber India Systems. The parent company invested ₹2,921 Cr through two tranches, as competition intensified in India’s ride-hailing market, especially from Rapido.
Khosrowshahi previously acknowledged Rapido as the company’s biggest competitor in India.
Notably, Uber and Rapido reportedly held talks earlier this year to potentially combine their India ride-hailing operations. The discussions broke down over the structure of the proposed deal. Rapido subsequently denied that it was exploring a merger.
Uber India’s net loss surged nearly 15X to ₹1,511 Cr in FY25 from ₹89 Cr in FY24, while its gross revenue remained largely flat at ₹2,604 Cr.
In March, Uber shut its shuttle service in Delhi NCR, following similar shutdowns in Mumbai and Hyderabad, as it shifted its focus towards employee transportation services for businesses. The company is looking to tap India’s growing corporate commute and GCC ecosystem through its B2B mobility offering.
At the same time, it announced plans to open two new technology centres in Bengaluru and Hyderabad, along with its first data centre in India, being set up with the Adani Group.
In June, Prabhjeet Singh stepped down as Uber’s India and South Asia head after more than a decade with the company to join OpenAI as its India MD.
The post Uber To Lay Off 200-250 Employees In India Amid Global Restructuring appeared first on Inc42 Media.

items.title: Port of Jumanah Karya Agate Rilis 7 September, Cek Spesifikasi PC Lengkap

Agate, developer game asal Indonesia, dijadwalkan akan merilis Port of Jumanah pada 7 September 2026 bersama Red Dunes Games sebagai publisher.
Menariknya, game action adventure dengan elemen roguelite ini tidak hanya meluncur di PC lewat Steam dan Epic Game Store, tetapi juga untuk PlayStation 5 (PS5).
Kehadiran Port of Jumanah di platform konsol PS5 terbilang sangat menarik, karena tidak banyak game-game buatan studio asal Indonesia bisa tembus di konsol milik Sony tersebut.
Walau masih baru akan dirilis secara global empat hari mendatang, gamer yang penasaran dengan game besutan Agate International ini bisa mainkan versi demo di Steam.

Port of Jumanah rilis di PC hingga PS5
Dari sisi gameplay, Port of Jumanah adalah action 2.5D memadukan combat, elemen roguelite, dan eksplorasi bawah laut. Pemain akan mengendalikan Mansour, pemuda yang terseret ke dalam serangkaian peristiwa hingga harus menyelamatkan dunia.
Selain menyelam di laut, Mansour
items.author: Yus Lianson
items.content:
Agate, developer game asal Indonesia, dijadwalkan akan merilis Port of Jumanah pada 7 September 2026 bersama Red Dunes Games sebagai publisher.
Menariknya, game action adventure dengan elemen roguelite ini tidak hanya meluncur di PC lewat Steam dan Epic Game Store, tetapi juga untuk PlayStation 5 (PS5).
Kehadiran Port of Jumanah di platform konsol PS5 terbilang sangat menarik, karena tidak banyak game-game buatan studio asal Indonesia bisa tembus di konsol milik Sony tersebut.
Walau masih baru akan dirilis secara global empat hari mendatang, gamer yang penasaran dengan game besutan Agate International ini bisa mainkan versi demo di Steam.
Gameplay Port of Jumanah di PC hingga PS5
Port of Jumanah rilis di PC hingga PS5
Dari sisi gameplay, Port of Jumanah adalah action 2.5D memadukan combat, elemen roguelite, dan eksplorasi bawah laut. Pemain akan mengendalikan Mansour, pemuda yang terseret ke dalam serangkaian peristiwa hingga harus menyelamatkan dunia.
Selain menyelam di laut, Mansour bisa merekrut karakter lain untuk bergabung dengan kru, menjelajahi lautan, menghadapi monster, dan meningkatkan perlengkapan.
Progression menjadi bagian penting di dalam game, di mana pemain bisa membuka upgrade kemampuan dan gear setiap kali menyelesaikan misi.
Adapun latar game, hingga desain lingkungan dan karakter di Port of Jumanah terinspirasi dari budaya Arab, sebagaimana dikutip dari situs resminya, Kamis (3/9/2026).
Tampil sebagai game lokal, pengembang juga sudah mendukung bahasa Indonesia, termasuk yang lainnya seperti Inggris, Arab, Jepang, Mandarin, dan Prancis.
Spesifikasi Port of Jumanah
Port of Jumanah, game buatan Agate dan Red Dunes
Untuk versi PC, spesifikasi minimum yang tercantum adalah Intel Core i5-9400F, RAM 8GB, dan GPU GTX 1050 Ti 4GB atau Radeon RX 570 4GB. Ruang penyimpanan yang dibutuhkan sekitar 8GB.
Port of Jumanah dijadwalkan rilis 7 September 2026 di PS5, Steam, dan Epic Games Store. Harga belum diumumkan, tapi game ini sudah bisa ditambahkan ke wishlist di Steam dan Epic Games Store.
Agate Academy Dukung Pelaksanaan Global Game Jam 2025
Di sisi lain, Agate lewat Agate Academy, kembali menunjukkan komitmennya dalam mendukung pengembangan ekosistem game nasional dengan mendukung pelaksanaan Global Game Jam (GGJ) 2025. Acara ini akan digelar serentak di 12 kota di Indonesia, termasuk Bandung, Yogyakarta, Jakarta, Surabaya, dan Makassar. GGJ 2025 akan berlangsung selama tiga hari, mulai 24 hingga 26 Januari 2025, dengan pendaftaran peserta yang dibuka hingga 23 Januari 2025.
Sebagai salah satu acara pengembangan game berskala internasional, GGJ menjadi ajang bagi para pengembang game untuk berkolaborasi dan menciptakan game dalam waktu 48 jam. Hingga saat ini, GGJ telah melibatkan lebih dari 439.000 peserta dari 132 negara dan menghasilkan lebih dari 89.000 game. Dengan dukungan dari Agate Academy, GGJ diharapkan dapat menjadi ruang bagi talenta lokal untuk meningkatkan kreativitas dan inovasi di tingkat global.
Kolaborasi yang dilakukan Agate Academy dalam acara ini juga melibatkan berbagai komunitas dan asosiasi, seperti Asosiasi Game Indonesia (AGI) serta komunitas lokal di setiap kota penyelenggara. Hal ini tidak hanya memperkuat ekosistem pengembangan game nasional tetapi juga membuka peluang kolaborasi lintas komunitas yang lebih luas.
Meningkatkan Ekosistem Game Nasional
Agate ungkap strategi di 2024
Salah satu fokus utama Agate Academy adalah pengembangan talenta pengembang game di Indonesia. Sejak didirikan pada 2019, Agate Academy telah melatih lebih dari 7.500 peserta melalui berbagai program unggulan, seperti Agate Game Course dan Agate Game Course for Teachers. Dengan jaringan yang mencakup lebih dari 345 sekolah dan universitas serta 20 mentor berpengalaman, Agate Academy terus berupaya mempercepat pertumbuhan ekosistem game di Indonesia.
Dukungan Agate Academy dalam GGJ 2025 tidak hanya terbatas pada penyediaan tempat atau fasilitas, tetapi juga pada penyelenggaraan sesi mentoring dan pelatihan selama acara berlangsung. Peserta dari berbagai latar belakang, baik pemula, pelajar, hingga profesional, diundang untuk bergabung dan berkolaborasi dalam menciptakan game inovatif.
Menurut CEO Agate Academy, Restya Winda Astari, GGJ 2025 merupakan peluang besar bagi pengembang game lokal untuk menunjukkan kemampuan mereka. “Melalui acara ini, kami berharap dapat menciptakan ruang inspiratif bagi para talenta lokal untuk belajar, berinovasi, dan memperluas jaringan mereka,” ungkapnya. Dengan semangat kolaborasi dan kreativitas, Agate Academy berharap acara ini dapat memberikan dampak positif yang berkelanjutan bagi industri game nasional.

items.author: Onsa Mustafa
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Google has introduced two new AI models, Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber. The company says the new models bring better reasoning, coding, and agentic capabilities while keeping the speed and lower cost associated with the Flash series.
Gemini 3.8 Flash is designed as a general-purpose model for developers, businesses and consumers. Google says it delivers major improvements over Gemini 3.7 Flash, particularly when handling complex software engineering tasks, autonomous agents and multi-step reasoning.
Despite these improvements, Google is keeping the introductory pricing at the same level as Gemini 3.7 Flash. The model costs $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens.
Google Introduces Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber With Stronger AI and Security Skills
A major focus of Gemini 3.8 Flash is long-running coding work. Google says the model can independently work through complex software engineering problems and complete tasks from start to finish. On the DeepSWE v1.1 benchmark, the company says Gemini 3.8 Flash can outperform several larger and more expensive frontier models.
The model also targets professional workloads that require detailed analysis. Google reports strong results on finance and legal agent benchmarks, along with a 54.9% score on HLE-Verified. This shows the model’s ability to work through difficult questions across areas such as science, humanities, and professional fields.
Google says Gemini 3.8 Flash achieves these results by spending more effort on complicated tasks. It can perform additional reasoning steps and repeatedly use tools when needed. This approach can improve results, although it may also increase token usage.
Developers who want to reduce computing costs can select lower effort levels. Google will also continue supporting Gemini 3.7 Flash for workloads where efficiency is more important than maximum performance.
The second model, Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber, focuses specifically on cybersecurity. Google describes it as its most capable cybersecurity model yet, with a focus on finding vulnerabilities and automatically fixing security problems.
The model has demonstrated strong results on CyberGym, a benchmark designed to test autonomous vulnerability discovery. Google says Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber outperformed its previous 3.5 Flash Cyber model as well as several much larger frontier models.
Google also tested the model on an internal benchmark covering complex software projects written in 20 programming languages. The company says the model achieved a success rate of more than 70% when identifying vulnerabilities across these codebases.
Automated vulnerability repair is another key feature. On the CWE-Bench benchmark, Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber recorded a 47.2% pass@1 score. Google says this is close to the 47.8% result achieved by a leading frontier model, while Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber costs significantly less to operate.
Google is already using the cybersecurity model internally. The company says its Chrome Security team found that Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber generated 2.6 times more correct vulnerability patches than the best commercial models tested, despite those models being much larger.
Google also says its Cloud Vulnerability Research team used the model to identify a critical vulnerability in less than two hours. According to the company, research of this type can normally take months.
See Also: Google Gemini May Let Users Turn Off Visible Watermarks on AI-Generated Content
Security remains a major part of the new models. Gemini 3.8 Flash includes safeguards designed to limit harmful use involving cyber offense and CBRN-related areas. Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber has more permissive cybersecurity protections because it is intended for trusted defenders.
For this reason, Google is making Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber available through its Fairwind Program to selected government authorities, critical infrastructure operators, and software maintainers.
Gemini 3.8 Flash is already available through several Google products and developer platforms. Developers can access it through the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, Android Studio and Google Antigravity. Enterprises can use it through Gemini Enterprise, while eligible consumers can access it through the Gemini app, Google Search’s AI Mode, and Gemini in Google Sheets.
With the two new models, Google is expanding Gemini’s focus beyond traditional chatbot use. Gemini 3.8 Flash is aimed at demanding coding, reasoning, and agent-based tasks, while the Cyber version targets organizations that need advanced tools for discovering and fixing software vulnerabilities.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
HUAWEI nova 16s dan nova 16s Pro resmi dikenalkan ke pasar global. Keduanya merupakan versi global dari nova 16 dan nova 16 Pro yang sebelumnya diperkenalkan di China pada Juni 2026. Seperti pola Huawei dalam beberapa generasi terakhir, model global kali ini mendapatkan tambahan “s” pada penamaannya.
HUAWEI nova 16s Pro menjadi model yang paling tinggi dengan mengandalkan konfigurasi kamera yang cukup agresif. Smartphone ini membawa kamera utama 200MP RYYB dengan aperture f/1.8 dan OIS, ditemani sensor multispektral 1,5MP untuk membantu kalibrasi warna berdasarkan kondisi adegan. Kamera tersebut dipadukan dengan periskop 50MP RYYB 3,7x OIS dan ultrawide 50MP dengan bidang pandang 118 derajat yang juga mendukung mode makro hingga jarak 2,5 cm.
Di sisi lain, nova 16s menawarkan spesifikasi yang lebih sederhana, tetapi tetap membawa baterai berkapasitas besar 7.000 mAh dan pengisian cepat 100W. Keduanya juga menggunakan EMUI 16.0, bukan HarmonyOS, dengan Kirin 9010S pada model Pro dan Kirin 8020 pada model reguler. Detail harga dan ketersediaan globalnya masih belum diumumkan Huawei.
Baca Juga: HUAWEI Umumkan Pura X View, Smartphone dengan Layar Lebar Pertama
Kamera 200MP dan Layar OLED 120Hz
HUAWEI nova 16s Pro dibekali layar LTPO OLED berukuran 6,84 inci dengan refresh rate adaptif 1-120Hz. Huawei mengklaim panel ini dapat mencapai tingkat kecerahan hingga 6.000 nits pada kondisi tertentu, sementara dynamic peak brightness mencapai 4.000 nits. Layar tersebut juga menggunakan PWM dimming 2.160Hz untuk pengaturan kecerahan.
Untuk fotografi, HUAWEI menyertakan sejumlah fitur berbasis AI seperti AI Composition, AI Move, AI Remove, AI Best Expression, dan AI De-Glare. Fitur-fitur tersebut memungkinkan pengguna mendapatkan bantuan untuk komposisi, memindahkan atau menghapus objek, memilih ekspresi terbaik, hingga mengurangi pantulan pada permukaan kaca.
Baterai Besar, Bodi Tetap Tipis
Salah satu daya tarik kedua perangkat adalah baterai 7.000 mAh yang dipadukan dengan HUAWEI SuperCharge Turbo 100W. Namun, kapasitas besar tersebut tetap memiliki kompromi. nova 16s Pro memiliki ketebalan 7,1 mm dengan bobot mencapai 218 gram, sedangkan nova 16s sedikit lebih tipis di kelasnya dengan ketebalan 7,3 mm.
Untuk material, HUAWEI nova 16s Pro menggunakan frame aluminium dan Kunlun Glass dengan lapisan nano-crystal di bagian depan. Huawei mengklaim perlindungannya memiliki ketahanan jatuh hingga 10 kali lebih baik dibanding nova 15. Klaim tersebut tetap perlu dilihat melalui pengujian penggunaan nyata, terutama karena daya tahan perangkat tidak hanya bergantung pada material kaca.
Huawei nova 16s tersedia dengan penyimpanan 256GB dan 512GB. Sementara itu, informasi mengenai harga, konfigurasi memori lengkap, serta jadwal peluncuran di masing-masing negara masih akan diumumkan kemudian.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
ASUS ROG memperluas lini perangkat yang ditujukan untuk kebutuhan esports dengan memperkenalkan mouse gaming Gladius IV Ace dan tiga monitor OLED berukuran 24,5 inci. Produk-produk tersebut dikembangkan dengan masukan dari pemain esports dan dirancang untuk memenuhi kebutuhan permainan kompetitif yang membutuhkan respons cepat serta konsistensi perangkat.
ROG Gladius IV Ace menjadi salah satu produk utama dalam lini periferal terbaru. Mouse ini memiliki bobot awal 56 gram dengan desain center-balanced dan menyediakan sejumlah konfigurasi bobot tambahan. ASUS juga mengklaim setiap unit melewati pengujian mesin untuk memastikan konsistensi aktuasi tombol kiri dan kanan pada tekanan 5gf.
Di sektor konektivitas, Gladius IV Ace menggunakan teknologi SpeedNova 8K Gen II dengan receiver yang dapat memantau kondisi frekuensi radio di sekitar perangkat. Mouse ini juga membawa sensor AimPoint Pro 65K dengan sensitivitas hingga 65.000 DPI, akselerasi 70G, kecepatan 800 IPS, serta polling rate hingga 8.000Hz.
Baca Juga: ASUS ROG Edition 20 Hadir di Indonesia, PC Flagship Dibanderol Rp279 Juta
Monitor OLED hingga Refresh Rate 720Hz
ASUS ROG juga memperkenalkan tiga monitor OLED baru, yakni Swift OLED PG259QWS Ace, Strix OLED XG259QDPG Ace, dan Strix OLED XG259QDNS Ace. Ketiganya menggunakan panel 24,5 inci dan menyasar pemain esports yang membutuhkan refresh rate tinggi serta waktu respons cepat.
Model tertinggi adalah ASUS ROG Swift OLED PG259QWS Ace dengan refresh rate 720Hz. Monitor ini menggunakan panel Tandem WOLED TrueBlack Glossy dan menawarkan kecerahan puncak hingga 1.700 nits serta dukungan Dolby Vision. ROG juga menyematkan Position Sensor untuk membantu pengguna mencatat posisi dan sudut monitor saat melakukan setup.
Sementara itu, ASUS ROG Strix OLED XG259QDPG Ace menggunakan panel RGB QD-OLED dengan refresh rate 560Hz, BlackShield Film, serta lapisan anti-glare low-reflection. Model XG259QDNS Ace menjadi pilihan dengan refresh rate 360Hz. Keduanya tetap menyediakan konektivitas seperti DisplayPort 1.4 dan HDMI 2.1.
Perluas Kerja Sama dengan Pemain Esports
View this post on Instagram
Di luar perangkat keras, ASUS ROG memperluas kerja sama dengan organisasi dan pemain esports. Salah satunya adalah GamerLegion yang menjadi mitra periferal resmi, dengan ROG menyediakan perangkat seperti mouse, keyboard, mouse pad, dan perlengkapan gaming lainnya untuk tim tersebut.
ROG juga menggandeng Timothy “iiTzTimmy” An, kreator konten FPS sekaligus mantan pemain profesional Apex Legends. Kolaborasi tersebut mencakup produksi konten, aktivitas komunitas, serta keterlibatan iiTzTimmy dalam memberikan masukan terkait perangkat gaming.
Dari sisi harga, ROG Swift OLED PG259QWS Ace dibanderol MSRP US$1.099, sedangkan ROG Strix OLED XG259QWPG Ace berada di US$699 dan dijadwalkan tersedia pada awal kuartal keempat. Namun, angka tersebut merupakan MSRP dan harga di masing-masing pasar dapat berbeda. Di luar itu, manfaat refresh rate hingga 720Hz juga sangat bergantung pada kemampuan PC menghasilkan frame rate setinggi itu, sehingga fitur tersebut lebih relevan untuk skenario esports tertentu dibandingkan penggunaan gaming secara umum.

items.content:
Flipkart Enters The Microdrama Fray
India’s microdrama war has a new challenger. Flipkart is diving into the entertainment industry with short-form scripted shows and microdramas. Already experimenting with food delivery and ticketing, can entertainment become the ecommerce giant’s next growth engine?
Flipkart’s Latest Tryst: The ecommerce giant is testing a dedicated microdrama feed within its main app rather than building a standalone platform. It also plans to partner with Terribly Tiny Tales, Pratilipi and others to produce microdramas exclusively for its platform. Flipkart is also expected to source content from its digital media arm, Pinkvilla.
To lead its content push, Flipkart has roped in ex-JioStar executive Vivek Mohan Sharma as the new CEO of Pinkvilla, replacing founder Nandini Shenoy.
But Why Microdramas? Flipkart’s microdrama feed is designed to boost engagement and retain users. Simultaneously, the ecommerce giant also aims to create impulse purchase moments by embedding content inside the main app. The integration also leverages the ecommerce giant’s existing media assets to produce exclusive content.
The Many Tailwinds: What also sets Flipkart apart is that it does not have to worry about distribution costs, unlike specialist players, as its 500 Mn-strong network effects make it easy to acquire users. It may also not have to worry about monetisation as Flipkart so far appears to be treating microdramas as a sales funnel. Advertising could also add a parallel revenue stream if the company goes that way.
Beyond Ecommerce: The microdrama entry is part of Flipkart’s broader diversification spree. Having already launched its quick commerce vertical in 2024, the ecommerce major is now exploring foraying into food delivery and online ticketing. Together, these moves reflect Flipkart’s ambition to capture more of consumers’ daily time and spending under one platform.
But as the ecommerce giant rejigs its top brass and prepares for an eventual IPO, will Flipkart’s microdrama bet pay off? Let’s find out…
From The Editor’s Desk
Purple Style Labs Wraps Up IPO
The Pernia’s Pop Up Shop parent’s public issue was oversubscribed by 1.29X on the final day of bidding, with investors placing bids for 88.54 Lakh shares against 68.49 Lakh on offer.
Retail investors and QIBs led the demand, oversubscribed their quotas by 1.57X and 1.43X, respectively. However, NIIs subscribed their portion by just 84%, placing bids for 15.70 Lakh shares against 18.68 Lakh shares on offer.
Founded in 2015, Purple Style Labs is an omnichannel luxury fashion company that operates and owns designer brands such as Wendell Rodricks and Hemant Trivedi. Its public issue consisted solely of a fresh issue of shares worth ₹680 Cr.
Jagdish Farshan’s Q-Comm Bet
In its first institutional fundraise since 1938, the Gujarat-based snacking brand has raised ₹43.5 Cr in a round led by Sharrp Ventures to expand manufacturing capacity, add new retail stores and deepen its quick commerce presence.
Digital sales and exports currently account for about 15% of Jagdiish Farshan’s revenue, with the company viewing quick commerce as a better fit for impulse-led snack purchases because of shorter delivery times and higher immediacy.
Established 88-years ago, Jagdish Farshan operates 27 retail outlets in central Gujarat and two in North America, offering over 500 SKUs across traditional Gujarati snacks, namkeen and sweets. It claims to process 250-300 online orders a day.
Aeron Systems Bags ₹45 Cr
The deeptech company has raised about $4.7 Mn in its pre-Series B round co-led by Riverwalk Holdings and MGF-Kavachh to expand its manufacturing capacity, accelerate R&D and strengthen its presence in international markets.
Founded in 2008, Aeron designs and manufactures inertial navigation and IoT-based weather-monitoring systems for aerospace and defence applications. It claims to have so far deployed 10,000 inertial systems and over 2,500 weather stations globally.
The funding comes amid growing demand for aerospace and defence technologies that can operate in complex and contested environments. At the heart of all this is the Indian deeptech market, which is projected to become a $27 Bn opportunity by 2030.
Yotta Gears Up For 2027 IPO
The AI data centre provider plans to file its DRHP with the SEBI by October this year. With this, the company has set its eyes on going public within the March quarter of the ongoing fiscal year.
The company is looking to raise up to $1.5 Bn from its IPO, which will likely consist solely of a fresh issue of equity shares. The fresh proceeds will go towards repaying debt, purchasing new GPUs and expanding sovereign cloud infrastructure.
Founded in 2019, Yotta started out as a colocation centre and integrated data centre services provider. The Hiranandani Group-backed firm has since grown to offer AI compute to companies. It has so far raised $150 Mn and was last pegged at $3.9 Bn.
JioHotstar Goes Global
Expanding its footprint beyond India, the streaming giant has now rolled out its services in the UK, Canada and Singapore. With this, it aims to capture the South Asian diaspora and wider audiences in the three nations.
JioHotstar said that it will roll out 1.6 Lakh hours of content, including webseries, TV shows, films and regional programming, across 12+ languages in the new markets. It has so far introduced only quarterly and annual plans in the three geographies.
With this, JioHotstar appears to be trying to convert cultural affinity into a sticky streaming proposition in the three markets. The launch is also expected to act as a test bed for tracking the demand for JioStar’s products overseas.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
Can Antimattr Make Voice The Primary Interface For AI?
AI assistants are getting smarter. But noisy surroundings still break voice interactions, forcing users back to the screens. Antimattr is tackling this problem with a voice-first hardware system that makes memory and productivity hands-free.
An Audio Computer: Founded in 2025, Antimattr is building Project Mnemosyne, which it describes as the “world’s first audio computer” built for memory and voice productivity. Its hardware combines a smart ring with a pair of voice-isolation earphones to enable clearer conversations and dictation in noisy environments.
The Wearable Stack: The earphones use six microphones, bone-conduction sensors and proprietary voice-isolation algorithms to capture only the wearer’s voice. On top of this, the companion smart ring acts as a quick-access interface to record ideas and conversations. The combined system then transcribes speech to text, organises notes, summarises meetings, supports live translation and lets users query an AI assistant.
The Road Ahead: Backed by Y Combinator and Nikhil Kamath’s WTFund, the startup now plans to begin shipping Mnemosyne in Q4 2026. It has a longer-term roadmap that extends to a privacy-focused AI computer and eventually an AI-native vehicle. With India’s AI wearable market projected to reach $19.1 Bn by 2033, can Antimattr make voice the default interface for the AI era?

items.content:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) hosted the Third Conference of Registrars of Cooperative Societies (RCSs) at its New Delhi office on September 1, 2026. Deputy Governors Shri Swaminathan J. and Shri Shirish Chandra Murmu, Shri Shiv Pal Singh, Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS), Registrars of Cooperative Societies from various States, and senior officials of the RBI participated in the Conference.
Deputy Governor Shri Swaminathan J emphasised stronger governance and institutional capacity in UCBs, closer coordination between the RBI and the RCS/CRCS, and timely action where needed. He also highlighted the need to strengthen controls against cyber-enabled frauds and money-mule accounts, and referred to Mission SAKSHAM as an initiative for capacity building in the sector.
Deputy Governor Shri Shirish Chandra Murmu observed that while cooperation has deep roots in India, a cooperative society, once licensed as a bank, assumes greater responsibilities and accountability. He emphasised the importance of professional and fit-and-proper Boards and senior management, robust internal controls, greater technology adoption and timely resolution of weak UCBs.
Shri Shiv Pal Singh, Central Registrar of Cooperative Societies (CRCS), emphasised closer coordination between the cooperative authorities and the RBI, continued professionalisation of UCBs, and timely resolution of banks under liquidation.
Discussions during the Conference covered key governance, regulatory and supervisory issues concerning UCBs, including the expectations of the RBI and the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC).
(Brij Raj)           
Chief General Manager
Press Release: 2026-2027/1021

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
· Express surprise over inclusion of garri by NBS
· Lists causes of high food prices
By Cynthia Alo
Stakeholders in the agricultural sector and economy experts have raised concerns over the latest food inflation report released by the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS), describing it as inconsistent with prevailing conditions in farms and markets across the country.
They also picked hole the agric policies and practices that may have undermined productivity in the sector.
However they also expressed divergent views over the NBS report on the direction of food inflation.
According to the NBS, Nigeria’s food inflation rate rose by 2.79 percentage points to 20.31 per cent in July, from 17.52 per cent in June, marking the fifth consecutive monthly increase since March.
The Bureau attributed the rise to price changes in commodities such as garri, crayfish, fresh pepper, onions, carrots, rice, water yam, tomatoes, plantain, beef, eggs, guinea corn, ginger, and plantain flour, among others.
The experts question the accuracy of the underlying data collection methods.
Meanwhile, weekly market track by Vanguard AgroBiz at Mile 12 food market in Lagos in July showed a price fluctuation in some of the commodities while some remained unchanged.
A bag of garri, which sold for N30,000 on July 18, dropped to N25,000 by July 24.
Tomato prices also fell within the period. A basket of tomatoes from Cameroon sold for N90,000 on July 18, while one from Jos sold for N80,000. By July 24, a basket of tomatoes from Jos reduced to N65,000.
Traders attributed the drop to early harvest and increased supply from South West farms. The influx also introduced cheaper alternatives from Ogun State, with small baskets selling between N18,000 and N40,000 for medium-sized baskets.
Pepper and palm oil prices remained unchanged. A small bag of pepper sold for N40,000 on both dates, while a 25-litre keg of palm oil held steady at N48,000.
A bag of onions, however, dropped slightly from N140,000 on July 18 to N130,000 on July 24.
Commenting on the development at a recent event in Lagos,Chief Executive Officer and Founder of Farm Credit NG, Mr. Afioluwa Mogaji, said that the NBS report has failed to reflect market reality.
“I challenged Nigeria Statistics recently on television when they said inflation has gone up and they mentioned garri. Price of cassava has dropped by over 70 per cent. Whoever gave them that data is not a field person,” he said, insisting that garri ought not to be counted among items driving the inflation figure.
He, however, acknowledged that while garri prices have not fallen side by side with cassava, the resulting margin presents an opportunity that value chain actors ought to explore.
“The farmers are crying. They need many of us to go into processing now. The processing facilities are down.’’
On tomatoes, Mogaji noted that Adamawa State, which recorded about 50 per cent food inflation, had for years relied on tomato supplies from Cameroon, despite the two locations sharing similar climatic and production conditions, a scenario he said pointed to poor local leveraging of production timing rather than genuine scarcity.
He disclosed that a 2024 agreement reached with the Federal Ministry of Agriculture had helped cap the price of a basket of tomatoes at N50,000 nationally throughout 2025, describing it as a feat unachieved in 26 years, made possible by collaboration between government and the private sector.
Mogaji called for greater knowledge-sharing among operators in the sector, lamenting that too many players work in isolation and fail as a result.
He advised farmers and processors to identify and study individuals who have made notable progress in specific areas of the value chain.
He further advocated stronger political advocacy for farmers, saying that with sustained pressure, the sector could in future secure direct representation in government, given that politicians rely heavily on rural votes during elections.
However, the immediate past Director-General of the Lagos Chamber of Commerce and Industry (LCCI), Dr Muda Yusuf, agreed that the food inflation was on upward direction in July but he tied the inflationary trend to broader public dissatisfaction with ongoing economic reforms, noting that food security remains one of the most visible gaps between policy intent and citizens’ lived experience.
To address this, Yusuf canvassed a shift away from viewing agriculture solely as farming, stressing the need for a transition from subsistence practices to a commercially integrated agricultural economy.
He advocated increased investment in agro-processing, so that raw produce such as cassava proceeds beyond the farm gate into finished, value-added goods.
He maintained that while the government has a role in creating an enabling environment, private capital must drive the establishment and expansion of agro-allied industries.
He said: “Food inflation, as I have seen, is over 20 per cent. And if you talk to some people, it is even higher based on what they experience practically. Many things that used to be affordable are now becoming out of reach.
“We have large land resources. We have a large labour force. We have a big domestic market. But unfortunately, we are dealing with low productivity and high food inflation.”
Yusuf emphasized that states must step up saying, “Rather than go out and set up airlines, build airports, buy SUVs for traditional rulers, these are the kind of things the states should be doing because the majority of the citizens are in this sector. If you want to take them out of poverty, then invest in where they are operating.”
Speaking for farmers, Chief Tony Okafor, Deputy National President of the All Farmers Association of Nigeria (AFAN), stressed that the insecurity in farming communities poses a major constraint, noting that it restricts cultivation and disrupts the movement of produce from rural areas to urban markets.
According to him, high cost of diesel and petrol, including poor road infrastructure inflate the cost of logistics.
He added that unpredictable weather patterns, including flooding, drought and extreme heat, continue to affect production output, while multiple taxation remains a significant burden on farmers.
Seasonal shortages, he noted, disproportionately affect perishables such as pepper, onions and other vegetables.
On measures to address these challenges, Okafor called for sustained investment in rural road networks to lower the cost of transporting produce to markets, alongside improved security to enable farmers cultivate larger expanses of land with confidence.
He further urged for the provision of farm inputs and adequate training for farmers, as well as greater consistency in agricultural policy formulation, to allow farmers and investors to plan beyond a single farming season.
He also called for expanded irrigation infrastructure to reduce the sector’s overreliance on rainfall.
Also speaking, Chief Executive Officer of GBI Farms, Mr.Opeyemi Adeyanju, lamented on the price fluctuation as a longstanding and unresolved challenge for the sector.
He called on the government to design policies that guarantee greater price stability for both farmers and consumers.
The post Agric sector’s stakeholders disagree over food inflation appeared first on Vanguard News.
