items.author: Anjali Jain
items.content:
Bharti Group-backed satcom services provider Eutelsat OneWeb has sought the immediate grant of security approval for its low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellation, which would take it closer to commercially launching its services in India.
Many of OneWeb’s satellites are nearing the end of their operational lives and could become useless if there are further delays in launching its services in India, the Economic Times reported, citing sources.
The company has been awaiting security approval for more than 18 months after conducting its security compliance demonstration in January 2025.
OneWeb has informed the DoT that it submitted all the required data and information related to the security demonstration and responded to additional queries raised by law enforcement agencies. However, the approval is yet to come, the report said.
Questions sent to OneWeb remained unanswered till the time of publication. The story will be updated on receiving a response.
The clearance covers requirements related to lawful interception, network monitoring, and the localisation of critical network functions.
OneWeb’s Long Wait
OneWeb was the first satcom operator to secure a GMPCS licence in India, receiving the permit from the DoT in August 2021. The company was initially looking to launch its services in the country in 2022.
However, its rollout has faced repeated delays due to the Russia-Ukraine war, which disrupted the launch of its satellites, and the wait for approvals from Indian authorities, the report said.
The company subsequently received authorisation from IN-SPACe in November 2023 to provide the capacity of its satellite constellation in India.
OneWeb has established the necessary ground infrastructure, including gateways in Mehsana, Gujarat, and Thoothukudi, Tamil Nadu, as well as two points of presence in Mumbai and Chennai.
The gateways will connect with OneWeb’s global LEO satellite constellation and enable the delivery of satellite broadband services in India.
OneWeb operates a global constellation of more than 600 LEO satellites. ISRO launched 72 OneWeb satellites across two dedicated LVM3 missions in October 2022 and March 2023.
The report said OneWeb is replacing some satellites that have completed their operational lives. However, the number of operational satellites in its existing constellation could decline as more reach the end of their lives.
Even after securing security approval, OneWeb will require spectrum assignment before it can commercially launch services in India.
India’s Satcom Race
Elon Musk-led Starlink and Jio Satellite are also awaiting security clearance to commercially launch their satcom services in India.
However, the three companies are targeting different customer segments. OneWeb plans to cater primarily to businesses, while Starlink intends to offer services directly to retail consumers. Jio Satellite, meanwhile, plans to offer services through Reliance Jio’s joint venture with Luxembourg-based SES, which operates a medium Earth orbit satellite constellation.
Reliance Industries is also said to be evaluating a multi-billion-dollar investment in its own LEO satellite constellation. The conglomerate is exploring both organic and inorganic expansion opportunities, including possible acquisitions of satellite companies with existing orbital slots and infrastructure.
Last month, Starlink reapplied to IN-SPACe for authorisation for its second-generation constellation comprising nearly 30,000 satellites, which will include direct-to-device connectivity capabilities.

items.title: Volume Transaksi INDODAX Naik ke Rp8,7 Triliun di Tengah Aktivitas Pasar Kripto yang Menguat
items.summary:
Aktivitas perdagangan aset kripto di Indonesia mulai kembali meningkat pada Agustus 2026. Volume transaksi INDODAX tercatat mencapai sekitar Rp8,7 triliun, naik sekitar 16 persen dibandingkan Juli yang berada di kisaran Rp7,5 triliun. Kenaikan tersebut terjadi ketika pasar kripto global menunjukkan penguatan di sejumlah aset utama.
Di sisi lain, pertumbuhan volume transaksi INDODAX terjadi ketika nilai transaksi aset kripto nasional pada Juli justru mengalami penurunan. Berdasarkan data yang disampaikan INDODAX, nilai transaksi kripto nasional pada Juli mencapai Rp20,52 triliun, turun 28,2 persen dari Rp28,58 triliun pada Juni. Pada periode yang sama, jumlah konsumen aset keuangan digital Indonesia meningkat menjadi 22,93 juta akun.
Dengan volume sekitar Rp7,5 triliun pada Juli, transaksi INDODAX menyumbang sekitar 36,5 persen dari nilai transaksi kripto nasional pada bulan tersebut. Memasuki Agustus, peningkatan menjadi Rp8,7 triliun menunjukkan aktivitas di platform tersebut kembali

Berdasarkan data yang disampaikan INDODAX, nilai transaksi kripto nasional pada Juli mencapai Rp20,52 triliun, turun 28,2 persen dari Rp28,58 triliun pada Juni. Pada periode yang sama, jumlah konsumen aset keuangan digital Indonesia meningkat menjadi 22,93 juta akun.
Dengan volume sekitar Rp7,5 triliun pada Juli, transaksi INDODAX menyumbang sekitar 36,5 persen dari nilai transaksi kripto nasional pada bulan tersebut. Memasuki Agustus, peningkatan menjadi Rp8,7 triliun menunjukkan aktivitas di platform tersebut kembali meningkat, meski angka tersebut belum dapat menggambarkan keseluruhan kondisi pasar kripto Indonesia.
Baca Juga: SK hynix Prediksi Krisis Memori Berlanjut hingga 2030, Harga Tetap Tinggi
Bitcoin Menguat, Altcoin Ikut Bergerak
Chief Marketing Officer INDODAX Aloysia Dian menilai peningkatan volume transaksi pada Agustus mencerminkan aktivitas pasar yang mulai kembali menguat. Menurutnya, pergerakan Bitcoin turut menarik perhatian investor, sementara pertumbuhan jumlah investor menunjukkan minat terhadap aset kripto masih bertahan.
Data CoinMarketCap yang dikutip INDODAX menunjukkan Bitcoin menguat 24,36 persen dalam satu bulan. Sejumlah aset lain bahkan mencatat kenaikan lebih tinggi, seperti Ethereum sebesar 32,01 persen, XRP 28,22 persen, Solana 41,33 persen, dan Hyperliquid (HYPE) 61,53 persen. Namun, kenaikan tersebut juga menunjukkan bahwa pemulihan sentimen tidak berarti tingkat risiko setiap aset menjadi sama.
Aktivitas Naik Bukan Berarti Risiko Menurun
Peningkatan volume perdagangan dapat menjadi indikasi pasar yang lebih aktif, tetapi tidak otomatis menunjukkan kondisi yang sepenuhnya positif bagi investor. Pergerakan harga kripto tetap sangat dipengaruhi volatilitas, likuiditas, kondisi ekonomi global, serta arah kebijakan moneter.
Aloysia juga mengingatkan bahwa penguatan pasar dapat berubah mengikuti perkembangan ekonomi dan kebijakan global. Karena itu, kenaikan aktivitas transaksi pada Agustus sebaiknya tidak langsung diterjemahkan sebagai sinyal untuk meningkatkan eksposur. Investor tetap perlu mempertimbangkan karakteristik masing-masing aset, melakukan riset, serta memahami risiko sebelum mengambil keputusan.

items.author: Rizwana Omer
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa has launched an International Skills Certification Programme, described by officials as the province’s first initiative built specifically to equip young people with internationally recognized skills certifications, aimed at improving job prospects both inside Pakistan and abroad.
The programme, run under the NH-P Tobacco Cess Development Programme, was formalized through a Memorandum of Understanding signed with Pak-Austria Fachhochschule Institute of Applied Sciences and Technology in Haripur.
What The Programme Actually Covers
The training list is broad, spanning cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, mobile phone repair, plumbing, general technical skills, solar panel installation, e-commerce, and international languages. It also includes IOSH, NEBOSH and OSHA certifications, three globally recognized occupational health and safety qualifications commonly required for construction, industrial and overseas employment roles.
That mix matters because it spans two very different labour markets at once. Cybersecurity and AI training targets Pakistan’s growing digital economy and remote-work opportunities, while trades like plumbing, solar installation and the OSHA-style safety certifications are aimed squarely at overseas employment, particularly in Gulf countries where such certifications are frequently prerequisites for skilled labour visas.
Project Director Hashmat Ali said more than two dozen technical, digital and health-related courses are being introduced under the initiative, positioning it as a considerably wider offering than typical single-sector vocational programmes run in the province before.
Scholarships Tied To Germany And Austria
A specific component of the programme offers scholarships in robotics and cybersecurity in collaboration with Germany and Austria. Neither the scale of these scholarships nor the number of seats available was disclosed at the signing ceremony, so it’s not yet clear how many students will actually benefit from this component versus the broader certification training.
The European connection isn’t incidental. Pak-Austria Fachhochschule was itself established through a Rs250 billion government initiative to build technology-focused universities in partnership with China and several European countries, with a founding mandate centered on artificial intelligence, engineering and applied sciences. The institute has run on a campus in Haripur since 2020 and currently serves around 5,000 students, giving it existing infrastructure and academic partnerships to draw on for a programme like this one.
Who’s Backing The Initiative
Former National Assembly Speaker Asad Qaiser, speaking at the MoU-signing ceremony, said global-standard training and international education opportunities would help empower youth and support regional economic development. MPA Rangez Khan said the initiative would promote quality education, practical skills and improved employment outcomes.
Neither official’s remarks included specific targets, such as how many students the programme aims to train in its first phase or what employment outcomes will be tracked to measure success. That’s a common gap in programme launch announcements generally, and it means the real test of this initiative’s impact will come from data released once training cohorts actually begin completing courses.
Starting In Swabi, With Provincial Expansion Planned
The programme has initially launched in Swabi, with plans to expand across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa over time, according to Hashmat Ali. No timeline was given for what that expansion would look like or which districts would be next in line.
Starting in a single district before scaling is a reasonably standard approach for vocational programmes of this size, allowing implementers to work out logistics and course delivery before committing resources province-wide. Whether that expansion happens on schedule, and how quickly, will be the clearest early signal of whether this programme has the institutional backing to match its ambitious course list.
How This Fits Into KP’s Broader Skills Landscape
This isn’t the first skills initiative aimed at KP’s youth. The UNDP, working with Japan’s government and the Sarhad Rural Support Programme, ran a separate three-month vocational training programme in 2024 that equipped 700 young people, including 375 women, from Kurram and Orakzai districts with skills like cell phone repair, electrical work, plumbing and solar and UPS installation.
That earlier programme shares some overlap in subject matter, particularly around technical trades, but ran at a smaller scale and without the international certification and university partnership structure this new initiative is built around. The distinguishing feature of the NH-P programme is its pairing of vocational trades with globally recognized certifications and a formal academic institution, rather than standalone skills training delivered through an NGO partnership.
What Determines Whether This Programme Delivers
The ambition here is clear: cover a wide span of in-demand skills, attach internationally recognized certifications to them, and use tobacco cess revenue, a funding source tied to the province rather than dependent on federal allocation, to sustain it. That funding structure is worth noting on its own, since programmes reliant on provincial cess revenue tend to have more predictable continuity than those dependent on annual federal budget approval.
What isn’t yet clear is capacity. Running two dozen distinct courses, several of them requiring specialized instructors and equipment, such as cybersecurity labs or solar installation training, is a significant operational undertaking for a programme just getting off the ground in one district. How quickly Pak-Austria Fachhochschule can scale that capacity, and how many students actually complete courses and go on to secure jobs locally or abroad, will determine whether this becomes a genuine employment pipeline or another well-intentioned announcement that struggles to scale past its pilot phase.

items.author: Shraddha Goled
items.content:
If you asked ChatGPT for a new phone, a family car or the best way to plan a holiday, you were probably looking for an answer, not an ad. That’s changing fast.
Last week, OpenAI launched ChatGPT Ads in India, bringing sponsored messages into conversations on the AI chatbot for the first time in one of its largest markets. It’s the latest to introduce ads into its AI tools after Gemini and Meta, signalling a shift in digital advertising and marketing.
Ads will roll out to those using Free and Go tiers, while those on Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise and Education plans will get an ad-free experience.
The AI giant claims more than 50 brands are expected to go live during the initial rollout, with WPP and Omnicom as OpenAI’s first agency partners in India. Businesses will be able to access ChatGPT’s self-serve Ads Manager, with daily budgets starting at ₹725.
OpenAI’s pitch to advertisers is fairly straightforward if you believe that the world is moving on beyond search engines. The company says ChatGPT is increasingly becoming a place where people don’t just look for information, but think through what they want to buy.
In India, the company claims more than 100 Mn weekly active users, though how many of these are on the free and Go tiers is unclear. ChatGPT Ads arrive at an interesting moment for the advertising industry. Google and Meta have already begun putting ads into their AI-powered experiences, while other AI companies are still figuring out whether advertising can coexist with the trust users place in conversational assistants.
OpenAI now has to answer a harder question: will advertisers actually move money to a chatbot simply because it knows what consumers are thinking about?
How ChatGPT Ads Work
OpenAI’s initial advertising model is deliberately closer to search advertising than traditional display advertising. But it also says that unlike a conventional search query, a conversation can reveal the user’s budget, preferences, concerns and trade-offs.
“People do not simply enter a few keywords into ChatGPT. They express their goals, constraints, preferences and trade-offs. That produces a much richer expression of intent than a search for ‘best family car,” said Preetham Venkky, chief digital officer, Omnicom Advertising India.
Under the hood, OpenAI’s ads system uses conversation context to show an ad relevant to what the user is exploring. It considers multiple signals, including the context and intent of users’ current conversation, the ad’s landing page, title, copy, advertiser-provided context hints and targeting selections.
In this case, ads will appear at the end of a response by ChatGPT. Ads are labelled as sponsored messages and visually separated from ChatGPT’s response. For its rollout in India, ChatGPT is going for direct relationships with select brands and agencies to begin with.
Globally, studies show that ads on AI platforms align with the topic of the query and score high on relevance metrics. A study by SE Rankings showed that only 14% of the times the ads seemed irrelevant to a query on ChatGPT. However, for specific topics such as news and politics, the figure was much higher, up to 50%, which shows that the AI ad engines have a lot of fine-tuning ahead of them.
For now, brands who are experimenting with ChatGPT ads can use the company’s SaaS tool to set their own bid strategy, choose a destination URL, add context hints and target users by devices. ChatGPT automatically generates personalised and translated versions of headlines and descriptions, which may run without individual review, if the user opts for this approach.
Helping marketing teams generate personalised versions of the campaign at hand is a key facet of this tool. This helps marketers instantly tailor their messaging for the conversational AI world.
“Search advertising responds primarily to an explicit query. Social advertising is largely built around audiences, interests and attention. Conversational AI introduces a third signal: the broader context surrounding a decision,” Omnicom’s Venkky added.
He cited the example of someone asking ChatGPT for a family car within a particular budget, suitable for city driving and with strong safety ratings as opposed to someone just asking about the best family car. The former is expressing a much more detailed need and the AI’s advantage is the ability to understand this need and add it to the context around the stage of decision-making and intent of the user.
Will Ads Worsen The Data Privacy Issues?
Now addressing the elephant in the room. AI chatbots have had some notorious data privacy and security issues. While OpenAI says advertisements do not influence the answer generated by the model, one would assume this behaviour will not be inflexible.
The company says advertisers do not get access to conversations or personal information of the users. And while ads are selected based on the conversation’s context, the content of the user’s conversation is not shared with advertisers.
OpenAI has also said advertisers will receive aggregate campaign-performance information, such as impressions and clicks, rather than access to individual conversations. But there are still concerns about how far OpenAI will push the ad agenda.
A report by Wired showed that close to one in five conversations triggered an ad at the bottom of the output, often tailored to the most recent prompts. That said, the formatting and frequency of these ads may change with OpenAI’s new experiments.
The company is also putting guardrails around where ads can appear. Ads will not be eligible alongside sensitive or regulated topics, including mental health and politics. They will also not be shown on accounts belonging to people who identify themselves as under 18 or are predicted to be minors by OpenAI’s systems.
Users will also be able to dismiss ads, provide feedback, understand why an ad was shown, manage personalisation and clear the data used for advertising, according to OpenAI.
Will Brands Embrace The AI Shift?
OpenAI has also moved from experimentation towards a conventional advertising infrastructure. Its initial pilot used CPM, which is cost per thousand impressions, but the company subsequently added cost per click (CPC) bidding, allowing advertisers to pay based on clicks.
For CPC campaigns, OpenAI recommends starting with a maximum bid of $3–$5 per click.
In India, OpenAI is also preparing a self-serve ad management dashboard for brands and marketers. The minimum daily budget is ₹725, making the platform accessible beyond large agency-led campaigns. The important caveat for Indian marketers is that there is still limited public data on Indian clearing prices, conversion rates and return on ad spend. The market is too new for meaningful India-specific benchmarks.
That said, experts believe that these ads are expected to work best for ‘intent’ based buys instead of brands that lean in more towards impulse or awareness-led.
OpenAI’s early signals are encouraging, but there is little evidence yet that AI advertising can outperform established channels.
The company said its initial US pilot delivered encouraging results, it revealed that ChatGPT Ads has reached $1 Bn in annualised revenue run rate in 200 days of launch. In another forecast report by Axios, OpenAI’s advertising revenue is expected to reach $2.5 Bn in 2026, $11 Bn in 2027 and potentially $100 Bn by 2030.
But these are global figures and may not be justifiable in India till we see more data from the company.
Perplexity’s experience offers a different picture of how the AI industry sees advertising. After experimenting with ads, the AI search startup shifted towards a more subscription-led model.
However, a Perplexity spokesperson told Inc42, “We’re continually experimenting with advertisers that prioritise our users and how they use the internet now.”
For ChatGPT, Google is the more consequential benchmark. Google Search advertising revenue rose 14.5% to $81.6 Bn in Q2, while the company has already integrated ads into AI Overviews in India and is testing them in AI Mode in the US. Existing AI Max and Performance Max campaigns can extend into these experiences through Google’s standard auction system.
“Search is becoming an even deeper tool for discovery and decision-making through conversational AI. In India, 87% of surveyed users report making more confident decisions using AI Overviews and AI Mode,” a Google spokesperson told us, adding that ads can fuel brand discovery at the moment of intent.
Meta is also using AI to automate targeting, creative and campaign optimisation through Advantage+, with Bernstein analysts expecting its ad revenue to surpass Google’s in 2026.
Against these entrenched platforms, ChatGPT Ads are expected to remain experimental initially, according to advertising experts. For the first 12–24 months, most advertisers will treat ChatGPT Ads as a complementary channel funded through innovation, experimentation or performance-media budgets.
The bigger prize will depend on whether conversational intent delivers better economics. As consumers shift more product research to AI, some budgets could move from Google Search and other lower-funnel media. But stronger conversion rates, lead quality or lower acquisition costs will need to be demonstrated before ChatGPT becomes a core channel.
Brands And Industries Most Suited For GPT Ads
The brands that will do well here are the ones selling into a decision, not just a purchase. Medium and high-involvement categories are likely to adopt the format first because consumers in these categories typically search, compare and evaluate before making a decision, Omnicom’s Venkky said.
The automotive industry, consumer electronics, beauty and personal care, B2B technology and travel are expected to merge as natural early categories. These are categories where someone is actually asking a question and weighing options, not just scrolling.
“If you’re selling something people research before they buy, a mid-conversation ad sits naturally in that moment,” said Paramdeep Singh, cofounder of Shorthills AI.
If it is an impulse or awareness-led brand, this format probably is not for them yet. The whole value of ChatGPT ads comes from intent, and low-intent categories won’t get the premium they are paying for, the experts said.
Not Everyone Wants An Ads In AI
The most interesting counter-position for the ads in AI debate comes from Anthropic. In February, the company explicitly said Claude would remain ad-free. Its argument was not simply about user experience. Anthropic said advertising incentives were incompatible with its vision of Claude as a genuinely helpful assistant.
It specifically ruled out sponsored links, third-party product placements and advertiser influence over Claude’s responses.
Just a year after Perplexity rolled out ads in 2024, it began phasing out ads, and reportedly said that it was not exploring any new ad deals at the moment. It is a noteworthy U-turn for the AI startup, which became one of the first generative AI companies to test ads on its platform in 2024. Similar to Anthropic, trust was the factor cited as the reason behind this decision.
Before embracing ads, CEO Sam Altman had once called the combination of AI and advertising “uniquely unsettling” and described ads as a “last resort” business model.
Now, OpenAI is betting on the very model that Altman once viewed as a last resort. Whether that becomes a major revenue engine, or remains a way to subsidise free access, will depend on whether advertisers find enough value in ChatGPT’s most valuable asset: user intent.
Top Stories From India & Around The World
Gnani.ai Unveils Sovereign AI Stack Artha For Enterprises: Gnani.ai unveiled Artha, a sovereign AI stack pairing its 30 Bn-parameter multilingual model Evon v3.3 with agentic platform Plexus. It targets Indian enterprises and government bodies seeking control over sensitive data.
Runable Raises $21 Mn To Help Small Businesses Grow: AI agent platform Runable raised $21 Mn in a Series A co-led by Susquehanna and Nexus to automate customer acquisition, marketing and operations. The startup claims 1.5 Mn users and $2 Mn in ARR within weeks of launch.
Ringg AI Nets Additional $10 Mn, Closes Series A At $15.5 Mn: Voice AI startup Ringg netted an additional $10 Mn, closing its Series A at $15.5 Mn. Peak XV Partners led the round, with Arkam Ventures and Capital 2B doubling down.
ESDS Tests Market Amid Soaring Server, GPU Costs: ESDS opens its ₹720 Cr IPO at ₹408-₹429 to fund data-centre expansion and GPU-as-a-service. But server costs have nearly doubled since filing, stretching the capital it will raise.
Nvidia is Going For Hugging Face Acquisition: Several reports suggest that Nvidia has agreed to on acquire Hugging Face, the go-to open-weight model repository used by developers worldwide for $12.9 billion. The deal would hand the GPU giant control over one of the largest distribution channels for open-source AI models, potentially reshaping how open-weight tech reaches the market. (Source: The Information)
Sony Music, Warner Sue Anthropic Over Alleged IP Theft: Sony Music and Warner have sued Anthropic, as per a report by TechCrunch accusing the AI company of a “brazen campaign” of copyright infringement in how it trains its models. It is the latest in a wave of music-industry litigation targeting AI firms over the unauthorised use of copyrighted lyrics and recordings.
The Weekly Buzz: OpenAI Cuts Off Cursor
OpenAI is ending its long-running model-supply agreement with Cursor after SpaceXAI completed its $60 billion acquisition of the AI coding startup.
Direct access to OpenAI models will terminate on November 12, 2026, the maximum notice period permitted under the contract’s change-of-control clause. Future models, including the upcoming Astra, will also be withheld from the platform. In its official statement, OpenAI said it could not be confident that SpaceXAI would respect its terms of service, citing previous contract violations by Musk-linked companies including X and xAI.
Cursor CEO Michael Truell responded that OpenAI models currently account for only about 5% of user traffic and that discussions between the two sides are continuing. Anthropic quickly announced it would increase compute support for Claude models inside Cursor to help fill the gap. The decision escalates the already bitter rivalry between OpenAI and the SpaceXAI ecosystem at a moment.
Removing OpenAI models forces a faster shift toward Anthropic, open-weight alternatives, and Cursor’s own internal models. The episode highlights how fragile commercial alliances have become in the frontier AI stack. Model access is no longer neutral infrastructure. It is now shaped by personal history, competitive positioning, and control over the next generation of agentic coding systems.
Startup In The Spotlight: Gocodeo
Founded in 2023 by Meghana Jagadeesh and Jatin Garg, Bengaluru-based GoCodeo is an AI coding agent that works across the software development lifecycle. AI coding tools mostly behave like glorified autocomplete — helpful for snippets but stopping short of the full development loop professional teams actually run.
Instead of one-off suggestions, GoCodeo pitches context-aware, autonomous actions inside the IDE. Its VS Code-native agent handles build, test and deploy workflows, with Git integration for repository initialisation, commits and pull requests, and generates production-ready tests with debugging support.
The startup has open-sourced a full-stack SaaS builder framework and claims a developer base of over 25,000. It counts backing from Google for Startups and NSRCEL alongside its investors.
GoCodeo operates in the rapidly expanding AI software development tooling market, part of India’s enterprise AI opportunity, projected to grow from $11 Bn in 2025 to $71 Bn by 2030. As agentic coding tools move from snippet generation to owning the full build-test-deploy loop, GoCodeo believes an agent that ships production-ready code could help developers shift from assisted autocomplete to genuinely autonomous software delivery.
Prompt Of The Week
What prompts and hacks are CTOs, CEOs and cofounders using these days to streamline their work?
Here’s the prompt Viren Inaniyan, cofounder and CEO of Tru Commerce, uses to see a brand exactly the way ChatGPT sees it before deciding what to fix in its AI search presence.
“You are a brutally honest AI-commerce analyst. I’m the founder of [brand] in [category]. Treat me as an operator, not a beginner.
Using only what you actually know or can infer about my brand and category, produce three sections, no preamble:
The shelf test: Answer the 10 highest-intent buying questions in my category the way you would for a real shopper (for example, ‘best under [price]’, ‘[brand] vs [top competitor]’, ‘is [brand] legit’). For each, state which brands you would name, in what order, and whether my brand appears at all.
The why: For every question where my brand is absent or ranked low, name the exact reason missing structured product data, thin third-party validation (Reddit, reviews, press), weak comparison content, or you simply don’t know the brand exists. Flag which reasons are fixable in 30 days vs 90 days.
The fix list: Give me a prioritised 5-item action plan to win these answers: what to publish, where to earn citations, what data to structure, ranked by impact on revenue, not vanity metrics. For each item, name the query it will move and how I would verify it moved in 4 weeks.”
Editor’s Note: Some prompts may need to be adjusted by users for best results or may not work as intended for certain users.

items.author: Christopher Louis
items.content:
Sony memberikan tanggapan terhadap gugatan class action yang mempermasalahkan cara PlayStation Store mengungkap status lisensi game digital kepada konsumen. Dalam dokumen tanggapannya, Sony berargumen bahwa konsumen yang wajar seharusnya tidak menganggap pembelian game digital sebagai kepemilikan penuh atas software tersebut.
Gugatan bernama Heycock v. Sony Corporation of America diajukan oleh empat pemilik PlayStation di Pengadilan Distrik Utara California pada 18 Juni 2026. Para penggugat menilai proses checkout di PlayStation Store melanggar AB 2426, aturan California yang mengharuskan penjual memberikan informasi yang jelas ketika transaksi digital sebenarnya hanya memberikan lisensi, bukan kepemilikan.
Sony membantah konsumen dapat dengan mudah disesatkan mengenai hal tersebut. Dalam respons yang diajukan 21 Agustus, perusahaan menunjuk pada Software Product License Agreement (SPLA) yang harus disetujui sebelum pembelian. Perjanjian tersebut secara eksplisit menyatakan bahwa software diberikan melalui lisensi dan bukan dijual kepada pengguna.
Baca Juga: State of Play September 2026 Digelar, Ini Jadwal Lengkap Indonesia
Sony Gunakan Riwayat Pembelian Penggugat
Untuk memperkuat argumennya, pengacara Sony juga menggunakan riwayat pembelian dua penggugat. Jason Mendoza disebut membeli Resident Evil Requiem pada 14 Februari 2026, sementara Edward Heycock membeli game yang sama secara digital seharga US$69,99 hanya 11 hari kemudian.
Menurut Sony, situasi tersebut menunjukkan bahwa konsumen tidak mungkin memperoleh kepemilikan penuh atas salinan digital secara individual. Jika transaksi pertama benar-benar memindahkan kepemilikan game kepada Mendoza, Sony berargumen Heycock seharusnya tidak dapat membeli salinan digital yang sama.
Namun, inti persoalan dalam gugatan bukan sekadar apakah konsumen memahami adanya lisensi. Para penggugat mempermasalahkan apakah informasi mengenai status tersebut sudah disampaikan dengan cara yang memenuhi ketentuan AB 2426. Dengan demikian, pengadilan nantinya perlu menentukan apakah mekanisme dan informasi yang diberikan PlayStation Store sudah cukup jelas menurut hukum California.
Perdebatan Makin Relevan di Era Digital
Kasus ini menjadi semakin menarik karena Sony sendiri telah mengonfirmasi rencana menghentikan produksi cakram fisik untuk game PlayStation baru mulai Januari 2028. Jika kebijakan tersebut berjalan sesuai rencana, game baru akan semakin bergantung pada distribusi digital dan model lisensi.
Hakim Vince Chhabria dijadwalkan mendengar permohonan arbitrase sekaligus argumen alternatif Sony untuk membatalkan gugatan pada 1 Oktober di San Francisco. Putusan dalam perkara ini berpotensi menjadi salah satu acuan penting mengenai bagaimana platform digital menjelaskan perbedaan antara “membeli” sebuah produk dan memperoleh lisensi untuk menggunakannya.
Artikel berjudul Sony Berargumen Pembeli PlayStation Tak Pernah Benar-Benar Memiliki Game Digital yang ditulis oleh Christopher Louis pertama kali tampil di Gizmologi.id

items.title: Harga GPU Naik 15% dalam Sebulan, GeForce Kenaikan Paling Tinggi
items.summary:
Harga kartu grafis kembali mengalami kenaikan di pasar global. Berdasarkan data terbaru TechSpot yang memantau harga GPU di 10 negara, harga rata-rata seluruh model kartu grafis naik sekitar 15 persen hanya dalam satu bulan. Jika dibandingkan dengan harga peluncuran atau MSRP, harga GPU saat ini rata-rata sudah berada 28 persen lebih tinggi, dengan GeForce menjadi lini yang mengalami kenaikan lebih besar dibandingkan Radeon.
Dalam penghitungan tersebut, TechSpot tidak memasukkan GeForce RTX 5090 karena harganya dianggap sebagai outlier ekstrem. NVIDIA masih mencantumkan MSRP RTX 5090 sebesar US$1.999 (Rp35.500.000 dan ini kurs per 2 September 2026), tetapi harga model termurah yang tersedia di Amerika Serikat disebut sudah mendekati US$5.000 (Rp88.000.000). Itu berarti harganya sekitar 145 persen lebih mahal dari MSRP di AS dan 136 persen lebih tinggi secara global.
Jika RTX 5090 dikeluarkan dari perhitungan, kartu GeForce secara keseluruhan mengalami kenaikan harga rata-rata 19 persen

items.content:
Harga kartu grafis kembali mengalami kenaikan di pasar global. Berdasarkan data terbaru TechSpot yang memantau harga GPU di 10 negara, harga rata-rata seluruh model kartu grafis naik sekitar 15 persen hanya dalam satu bulan. Jika dibandingkan dengan harga peluncuran atau MSRP, harga GPU saat ini rata-rata sudah berada 28 persen lebih tinggi, dengan GeForce menjadi lini yang mengalami kenaikan lebih besar dibandingkan Radeon.
Dalam penghitungan tersebut, TechSpot tidak memasukkan GeForce RTX 5090 karena harganya dianggap sebagai outlier ekstrem. NVIDIA masih mencantumkan MSRP RTX 5090 sebesar US$1.999 (Rp35.500.000 dan ini kurs per 2 September 2026), tetapi harga model termurah yang tersedia di Amerika Serikat disebut sudah mendekati US$5.000 (Rp88.000.000). Itu berarti harganya sekitar 145 persen lebih mahal dari MSRP di AS dan 136 persen lebih tinggi secara global.
Jika RTX 5090 dikeluarkan dari perhitungan, kartu GeForce secara keseluruhan mengalami kenaikan harga rata-rata 19 persen secara bulanan. Sementara itu, GPU Radeon naik sekitar 11 persen. Tren tersebut juga sejalan dengan laporan sebelumnya yang menunjukkan harga sejumlah RTX 50 Series mengalami lonjakan signifikan sepanjang Agustus, membuat MSRP semakin sulit dijadikan patokan harga aktual di pasaran.
Baca Juga: NVIDIA Investasikan Rp57 Triliun ke MediaTek, Perluas Kolaborasi Chip AI
RTX 5060 Ti 16GB Jadi Salah Satu yang Paling Mahal
Salah satu contoh paling mencolok adalah RTX 5060 Ti 16GB. GPU yang memiliki MSRP US$429 tersebut kini dijual rata-rata sekitar 70 persen lebih mahal di Amerika Serikat dan 53 persen di pasar global. Menariknya, versi 8GB justru memiliki kenaikan yang jauh lebih rendah, yakni sekitar 14 persen di atas MSRP secara global.
Perbedaan tersebut menunjukkan bahwa harga GPU saat ini tidak hanya dipengaruhi oleh kelas produk, tetapi juga konfigurasi memori yang digunakan. Kapasitas VRAM lebih besar tampaknya memberikan tekanan harga yang lebih tinggi, meski faktor pasokan dan distribusi juga bisa berbeda antarwilayah.
Radeon Masih Lebih Terkendali
AMD juga tidak sepenuhnya terbebas dari kenaikan harga. Radeon RX 9060 XT 16GB tercatat sekitar 28 persen lebih mahal dari MSRP secara global. Namun, Radeon RX 9070 masih relatif lebih dekat dengan harga peluncurannya, dengan kenaikan sekitar 13 persen.
Salah satu faktor yang banyak dikaitkan dengan kondisi ini adalah pasokan memori GDDR7 yang disebut turut dialihkan untuk kebutuhan perangkat keras AI. Berbeda dengan GPU RTX 50 Series yang menggunakan GDDR7, sebagian besar Radeon generasi terbaru masih mengandalkan GDDR6. Kondisi tersebut mungkin membantu AMD menahan tekanan harga untuk sementara, meski belum berarti Radeon akan sepenuhnya terbebas dari kenaikan jika tekanan pasokan memori terus berlanjut.

items.content:
Unacademy Joins The upGrad Campus
After months of negotiations and regulatory approvals, upGrad has officially completed the acquisition of rival Unacademy in a deal valued at just over $200 Mn, a 94% drop from the latter’s peak $3.5 Bn valuation in 2021. So, can the combined entity unlock real value?
Strategic Fit For upGrad: The acquisition gives upGrad, which focuses on upskilling, a foothold in K-12 and competitive exam preparation. Beyond test prep, CEO Ronnie Screwvala also highlighted Unacademy’s tech stack, brand equity and the global potential of its language-learning app, Airlearn, as key drivers for the acquisition.
The Upside For Unacademy: For the troubled edtech platform, combining forces with upGrad offers a better growth trajectory. The all-stock deal gives Unacademy shareholders a stake in upGrad, while retaining CEO Gaurav Munjal to lead its core verticals. It will also leverage upGrad’s upskilling network, expertise and cash to explore new avenues.
But, the deal did not happen overnight. It was, as Screwvala said, six years in the making.
From Unicorn To Exit: Starting as a YouTube channel in 2015, Unacademy raised $600 Mn during the peak of the pandemic to build an edtech juggernaut. However, the reopening of offline institutions hit demand, prompting layoffs, burn reduction and shutdowns of several verticals. To tide over the issues, Unacademy explored a potential sale to Allen and K-12 Techno.
But the discussions failed over valuation before a term sheet was finally signed with upGrad this year. With the deal now sealed, the work is cut out for the combined entity.
The Road Ahead: Combining two distinct corporate cultures and operating models presents an immediate execution challenge for upGrad. The merged entity will also have to prove that Unacademy’s consumer reach can drive sustainable operating margins and justify the $200 Mn price tag. So, can upGrad and Unacademy together build what eluded them separately? Let’s find out…
From The Editor’s Desk
Whatfix’s CEO Passes Away
The cofounder and CEO of the SaaS soonicorn has passed away due to a cardiac arrest. He was about 50 years old. Friends and peers condoled his demise, remembering Batti as a friend and mentor who supported the wider Indian startup ecosystem.
Founded in 2013 by Batti and Vara Kumar Namburu, Whatfix offers an AI-powered digital adoption platform that helps enterprises train employees and drive the adoption of software. It has grown to cater to more than 700 enterprises today.
The Indian startup ecosystem has lost many luminaries this year. In July, Accel’s Akhilesh Agarwal passed away, while the ecosystem also mourned the demise of SaaS startup Xpedize’s cofounder Regan Mithani in March.
ESDS Wraps Up Bumper IPO
The enterprise cloud and AI company’s public issue was subscribed 135.88X on the final day of the bidding. QIBs subscribed their portion 261.5X, while NIIs and retail investors booked their quotas 192.9X and 39.7X, respectively.
ESDS’ ₹720 Cr IPO, which comprises entirely a fresh issue of shares, is priced in the range of ₹408 to ₹429 per share. Meanwhile, PSL’s public issue also consists solely of a fresh issue of shares worth up to ₹680 Cr, with no OFS component.
Meanwhile, Purple Style Labs’ IPO was subscribed a mere 24% on the second day of bidding. Retail investors led the charts (93% subscription), followed by NIIs (13%) and QIBs (6%).
Yuma Energy Bags $35 Mn
The battery swapping platform has raised around ₹333 Cr in its Series A round from existing backer Magna International to expand its footprint, diversify its client base and strengthen its tech platform.
Founded in 2023 as a JV between Magna and Yulu, Yuma offers battery swapping infrastructure and services for EVs. It operates more than 2,500 charging stations across 18 Indian cities and has accumulated 1 Lakh batteries so far.
Yuma operates in the growing Indian battery tech market, which is being driven by novel products, need for convenience and substantial subsidies from the Centre. It is eyeing a piece of the Indian EV market, which could become a $132 Bn opportunity by 2030.
Whistleblower Whiplash At Icertis
Anand Subbaraman stepped down as the CEO of the SaaS giant in July after whistleblower complaints accused him of misconduct, inappropriate behaviour and favouritism towards a junior employee.
This came after the company’s board received the complaint in May, prompting an internal probe and his eventual departure. CFO Rajat Bahri and board member Jim Moffatt have been appointed interim co-CEOs as the company searches for a successor.
The allegations come as Icertis is working with Goldman Sachs to explore a potential sale at around a $5 Bn valuation. Founded in 2009, Icertis operates an AI-native contract lifecycle management platform serving enterprises in over 90 countries.
VinFast Rejigs India Playbook
The Vietnamese EV giant has directed its suppliers to halt production of select cars in India to reassess costs. This came as VinFast could not achieve the planned costs for developing and sourcing parts locally.
The OEM has sought details of investments already made by suppliers for the three vehicle programmes. It remains to be seen whether the vendors will be compensated for tooling, engineering and other investments undertaken for the projects.
Just last year, VinFast planned to boost its annual EV production in India for exports to the Middle East and Africa. The OEM was banking on local manufacturing to reduce costs, but the cost conundrum appears to have put a spanner in the works.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
How AlgoFET Is Building Autonomous Docking Stations For Drones
Tactical drones may be getting smarter, but they still need to land, recharge or swap batteries with human help. This creates a bottleneck for continuous, remote operations. AlgoFET is building the infrastructure to change this with autonomous docking.
Ground Layer For Fleets: Founded in 2023, AlgoFET offers an integrated stack covering autonomous docking stations, battery management systems, high-power charging, embedded electronics and cloud-based fleet monitoring. Its AlgoDOCK enables precision landing and autonomous recharging, while AlgoBMS provides real-time battery health, diagnostics and predictive maintenance.
From Labs To the Field: Incubated at IISc, the Bengaluru-based startup operates a 12,000 sq ft manufacturing facility in Bengaluru. It claims to have deployed more than 2,000 units, with a pipeline exceeding 4,000 units and an order book worth around ₹100 Cr. Catering to drone makers and the Indian Army, the startup has so far deployed its products in areas like defence, agriculture, logistics, surveillance and infrastructure inspection.
The Road Ahead: Backed by Piper Serica, the startup now plans to focus on next-gen product development, in-house manufacturing expansion and deeper proprietary IP. It also plans to scale deployments and expand to the US and Europe. With India’s drone ecosystem projected to cross $3.2 Bn by 2030, can AlgoFET build the infrastructure that keeps drones airborne round the clock?

From Tata and Bikaji to dedicated players like Vratam and Upvasa, brands are lining up to capitalise on the latest D2C goldmine: fasting food. Whatever the reason someone’s fasting, there’s now a whole aisle for it…

Preliminary data on India's balance of payments (BoP) for the first quarter (Q1) of 2026-27, i.e., April-June 2026, are presented in Statements I and II.
Key Features of India’s BoP in Q1:2026-27
India’s current account deficit stood at US$ 4.2 billion (0.5 per cent of GDP) in Q1:2026-27 as compared to US$ 3.4 billion (0.4 per cent of GDP) in Q1:2025-26 (Table 1).
Merchandise trade deficit at US$ 86.1 billion in Q1:2026-27 was higher than US$ 68.9 billion in Q1:2025-26.
Net services receipts increased to US$ 51.6 billion in Q1:2026-27 from US$ 47.9 billion a year ago.
Services exports have risen on a year-on-year basis in major categories such as computer services, other business services and transportation services.
Net outgo on the primary income account, mainly reflecting payments of investment income, decreased to US$ 10.5 billion in Q1:2026-27 from US$ 13.3 billion in Q1:2025-26.
Personal transfer receipts under secondary income account, mainly representing remittances by Indians employed overseas, rose to US$ 42.9 billion in Q1:2026-27 from US$ 33.2 billion in Q1:2025-26.
In the financial account, foreign direct investment (FDI) recorded a net inflow of US$ 6.1 billion in Q1:2026-27, higher than US$ 5.2 billion in Q1:2025-26.
Foreign portfolio investment (FPI) recorded a net outflow of US$ 9.6 billion in Q1:2026-27 as against a net inflow of US$ 1.6 billion in Q1:2025-26.
Non-resident deposits (NRI deposits) recorded a net inflow of US$ 2.8 billion in Q1:2026-27 as compared to US$ 3.6 billion in Q1:2025-26.
Net inflows under external commercial borrowings (ECBs) to India amounted to US$ 3.3 billion in Q1:2026-27 as compared to US$ 4.4 billion in Q1:2025-26.
Foreign exchange reserves depleted by US$ 8.1 billion (on a BoP basis) in Q1:2026-27 as against an accretion of US$ 4.5 billion in Q1:2025-26 (Table 1).

items.title: RBI appoints Shri Suman Ray as new Executive Director
items.summary:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has appointed Shri Suman Ray as Executive Director (ED) with effect from September 01, 2026.
Prior to being promoted as ED, Shri Suman Ray was serving as Regional Director for Maharashtra.
As a career central banker, Shri Ray has experience of over three decades in the Reserve Bank, having worked in several areas including Currency Management, Financial Inclusion, Payment and Settlement System, Consumer Education and Protection, and Human Resources. Shri Ray has also served as Secretary to the Western Area Local Board.
As Executive Director, Shri Suman Ray will look after Deposit Insurance & Credit Guarantee Corporation and Premises Department.
(Brij Raj)           
Chief General Manager

Sony Interactive Entertainment (SIE) sedang bersiap untuk menggelar State of Play September. Perusahaan menjadwalkan livestreaming ini digelar pada Kamis, 3 September 2026.
Berbeda dari State of Play sebelumnya, kali ini PlayStation menyiapkan dua presentasi yang ditayangkan secara berurutan, yakni State of Play reguler dan State of Play Japan.
Kedua acara mulai tayang di kanal resmi PlayStation di YouTube dan Twitch mulai pukul 20.00 WIB bagi gamer di Indonesia yang ingin nonton pengumuman.
Lalu bagaimana dengan State of Play Japan? Streaming ini akan langsung ditayangkan menyusul begitu State of Play reguler berakhir tanpa jeda pengumuman waktu tayang terpisah.
Baca Juga: Marvel’s Wolverine Akhirnya Pamer Gameplay
Dua State of Play September dengan Fokus Berbeda
Final Fantasy VII Revelation tampil di State of Play September
State of Play September akan membawa update dan pengumuman dari PlayStation Studios serta sejumlah partner third-party. Sony juga memastikan presentasi tersebut akan ditutup dengan extended look untuk Final Fantasy VII Revelation dari Square Enix.
Setelah acara pertama selesai, PlayStation langsung melanjutkannya dengan State of Play Japan. Presentasi yang kembali dipandu Yuki Kaji ini berfokus pada game dari studio Jepang dan Asia, termasuk gameplay baru dan sejumlah pengumuman.
State of Play September utama akan disiarkan dalam bahasa Inggris dengan subtitle Jepang. Sementara State of Play Japan menggunakan bahasa Jepang dengan subtitle bahasa Inggris.
Final Fantasy VII Revelation Sudah Dipastikan Tampil
Untuk sementara, Final Fantasy VII Revelation menjadi satu-satunya judul yang secara eksplisit sudah dikonfirmasi Sony untuk streaming 3 September kali ini.
Sejumlah nama lain mulai beredar sebagai prediksi maupun rumor menjelang acara State of Play September ini, tetapi belum masuk dalam lineup resmi. Karena itu, masih terlalu dini untuk memastikan game lain akan tampil sebelum ada pengumuman dari PlayStation atau masing-masing publisher.
Sony juga belum mengumumkan berapa lama durasi kedua streaming ini. Presentasi kedua hanya disebut akan dimulai langsung setelah streaming PlayStation tersebut pertama berakhir.
Dengan demikian, gamer di Indonesia yang ingin mengikuti keduanya bisa mulai menonton pada Kamis, 3 September 2026 pukul 20.00 WIB.
God of War Laufey Diumumkan
Santa Monica Studio dan Playtation resmi umumkan God of War Laufey. Singkatnya, ini merupakan petualangan baru dalam GoW Santa Monica Universe dan juga sekaligus spin-off dari cerita utamanya. Nah, pada game ini menceritakan petualangan Faye yang merupakan istri dari Kratos dan ibu dari Atreus.
Mengingat, Faye merupakan karakter yang cukup misterius karena dalam garapan Santa Monica di God of War pertama mereka memperlihatkan Faye yang sudah meninggal, dan banyak pemain yang bingung tentang Faye. Maka dari itu, pihak studio dan Playstation mengumumkan game ini dan bisa menjawab semua rasa penasaran para penggemar.
Kehadiran Faye sebagai protagonis tentu menjadi langkah yang cukup berani. Selama saga Nordik berlangsung, karakter ini lebih sering hadir melalui kilas balik dan cerita dari karakter lain. Kini Santa Monica Studio mencoba mengeksplorasi sosok Faye secara lebih mendalam, sekaligus membuka babak baru bagi semesta God of War setelah berakhirnya Ragnarök.
Menjelajahi Dunia Baru di Luar Sembilan Realm
Dalam God of War Laufey, pemain akan menjelajahi Everywhen, sebuah dimensi yang digambarkan sebagai asal dan tujuan akhir seluruh sihir. Tempat ini menjadi rumah bagi berbagai dewa dan makhluk dari beragam mitologi yang hidup berdampingan, meski tidak selalu dalam keadaan damai.
Beberapa karakter baru yang diperlihatkan antara lain Sekhmet dan Begtse, dua dewa yang tampaknya akan menjadi ancaman bagi Faye. Selain itu, Faye juga akan ditemani oleh dua karakter pendukung, yakni Phranque dan Rue. Kehadiran mereka menunjukkan bahwa Santa Monica Studio masih mempertahankan pendekatan cerita berbasis hubungan antar karakter yang menjadi salah satu kekuatan God of War modern.
Gameplay Lebih Cepat dengan Sentuhan Era Yunani
Dari sisi gameplay, Santa Monica Studio mengatakan bahwa God of War Laufey menggabungkan elemen pertarungan era Yunani yang lebih cepat dengan pendekatan eksplorasi dan narasi dari saga Nordik. Hasilnya adalah sistem pertarungan yang disebut lebih agresif dan memiliki mobilitas lebih tinggi dibandingkan gaya bermain Kratos.
Sebagai mantan pemilik Leviathan Axe dan pelindung kaum Jötnar, Faye juga memiliki kemampuan unik berupa manipulasi jiwa. Pemain dapat memisahkan jiwa musuh dari tubuhnya untuk kemudian digunakan dalam berbagai kombinasi serangan.
 Meski terdengar menjanjikan, tantangan terbesar Santa Monica Studio adalah meyakinkan penggemar bahwa God of War tetap menarik tanpa Kratos sebagai karakter utama. Namun dari materi perdana yang diperlihatkan, God of War Laufey setidaknya menawarkan arah baru yang cukup menarik untuk diikuti.
Artikel berjudul State of Play September 2026 Digelar, Ini Jadwal Lengkap Indonesia yang ditulis oleh Yus Lianson pertama kali tampil di Gizmologi.id

items.content:
By Damilola Samuel
Tobacco-leaf production is declining worldwide but continues to rise in Africa, with the continent recording an almost nine per cent increase between 2012 and 2024, according to a new analysis by the World Health Organisation, WHO.
The analysis found that global tobacco-leaf production fell by nearly 19 per cent over the same period, while Africa’s cigarette import bill more than doubled, rising from $833 million to $1.77 billion.
The trend means African countries are producing more raw tobacco for export while simultaneously spending more on imported cigarettes.
“This is not just a tobacco-control issue. It is a health, trade, development and environmental issue,” said Dr Vinayak Prasad, Head of the Tobacco Free Initiative at WHO.
Prasad said tobacco farming exposes workers and their families to health risks, damages the environment and can leave farmers trapped in debt.
Africa accounted for about 11 per cent of global tobacco-leaf production in 2024, with production concentrated largely in Zimbabwe, Malawi, Tanzania, Mozambique and Uganda.
East Africa alone accounts for nearly 90 per cent of the continent’s tobacco-leaf production.
WHO said tobacco cultivation also places pressure on land and water resources that could otherwise support food production and other sustainable livelihoods.
Farmers face several health hazards, including green tobacco sickness, which occurs when nicotine from wet tobacco leaves is absorbed through the skin. They may also be exposed to pesticides and tobacco dust.
The analysis linked tobacco farming to soil degradation, deforestation and greenhouse gas emissions generated during the curing process.
In some low- and middle-income countries, children from poor families are also involved in tobacco farming, with some missing school to supplement household income.
WHO noted that tobacco-leaf exports contribute more than one per cent of gross domestic product in only a few African countries, including Zimbabwe and Malawi. The finding challenges the argument that tobacco production is economically essential to most African economies.
The organisation called on governments to support farmers and workers seeking to move away from tobacco production and help them develop alternative livelihoods.
It also urged countries to strengthen tobacco-control measures to reduce the health and economic burden associated with tobacco use and trade.
Under the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control, countries are encouraged to promote economically viable alternatives for tobacco growers and workers while protecting human health and the environment from the effects of tobacco cultivation.

items.content: New Delhi: Several macro indicators released on Tuesday brought further economic cheer, underscoring domestic resilience in the face of tariff headwinds and the lingering crisis in West Asia. India's total goods and services tax (GST) collections rose 14.8% from a year earlier to Rs 2 lakh crore in August, while bulk car sales surged 36% to 448,000, putting India on course to hit 5 million units in the current fiscal year.The Unified Payments Interface (UPI) platform processed a record 24.51 billion transactions worth Rs 29.82 lakh crore in the month, underlining consumer demand. Year-on-year, transaction volume increased 22%, while transaction value went up 20%. Power consumption rose 12.9% YoY to 169 billion units.Also Read: India seeks applications for remaining raw sugar import quotaHealthy ConsumptionThese numbers signal momentum persisting in July-September after data released on Monday showed the economy expanded by a better-than-expected 7.8% in April-June.133691042Petrol sales rose 7.9% and diesel sales 6.5% year-on-year in August, aided by increased mobility, stronger vehicle sales and an expanding economy. Aviation turbine fuel (ATF) sales rose 1.4%, while cooking gas sales fell 16.1%, according to preliminary data from the oil ministry.GST collections from imports continued to be the primary performance driver, accelerating 29% from a year earlier to Rs 62,604 crore, while domestic revenue from the levy rose 9.3% to more than Rs 1.37 lakh crore in August, buoyed by durable demand at home.The strong GST growth, combined with 7.8% GDP expansion in the June quarter, reflected the strength of the Indian economy despite geopolitical conflicts and global economic uncertainty, said Abhishek Jain, partner and national head, indirect tax at KPMG in India.Also Read: Indian banks slash FCNR deposit rates by up to 310 basis pointsThe latest numbers portray a mix of healthy consumption, expanding formalisation of the economy and improving compliance."These collections are a very reliable barometer of the economy since they cover both goods and services across the country," said MS Mani, partner, tax at Deloitte India. "There does not appear to be any slowdown in economic activity and consumption in India, despite the tariff headwinds and west Asia situation."Experts are optimistic that, despite an uncertain global outlook, GST collections will continue to surge from October onwards, backed by upcoming festivals when demand for consumer goods traditionally grows. "With the festive season round the corner, revenue collections over the next couple of months are likely to trend higher, supported by increased consumer spending," said Saurabh Agarwal, tax partner at EY India.Agarwal said the concurrent rise in imports showed the need for deeper localisation and import substitution.After refunds, net GST collections stood at Rs 1.68 lakh crore, up 8.3% year-on-year. Refunds surged 68% to Rs 31,795 crore, tempering the growth in the net tax take but also reflecting a sharp rise in refund processing.Mani said the sustained strength in collections should prompt the GST Council to look at easing input tax credit restrictions, rationalising audits and reducing compliance requirements, when it meets next on September 12."Businesses would expect fewer restrictions on ITC (input tax credit), centralisation of audits across states, simpler compliance for service providers, improved ease of registration and deregistration," said Mani.Total gross GST revenue during April to August rose 11% from a year earlier at Rs 10,42,757 crore. Total net GST revenue during the period increased 9% at Rs 8,89,523 crore.

items.content: Mumbai: The turnover of equity derivatives on the NSE and the BSE fell to fresh multi-month lows in August. Analysts attributed the decline to heightened volatility under the new Closing Auction Session (CAS) mechanism that drove several participants to cut back on derivatives activity, particularly in the final half-hour of the trading day."The decline in derivatives volumes is largely a result of the behavioural changes triggered by CAS," said Rajesh Palviya, head of research, Axis Securities.Last month, NSE's total monthly equity derivative turnover was ₹34.48 lakh crore, the lowest since November 2023. BSE's August turnover stood at ₹32.2 crore, the lowest since June 2025.CAS was implemented in Indian markets from August this year.It operates as a separate session of 20 minutes from 3.15 pm to 3.35 pm, during which the exchange first collects buy and sell orders and then matches them to determine a single official closing price for the stock.Palviya said that since this system was implemented, brokers are squaring off positions earlier by 3.05-3.10, while traders are also closing positions early to avoid the heightened volatility in the final minutes. "The early closure of the cash market also limits arbitrageurs and jobbers from executing delta-hedging strategies across cash, futures and options," he said. "Since algos, prop desks, scalpers and arbitrageurs operate on thin margins, many are choosing to stay away from the CAS window rather than risk losses."This daily loss in volumes has compounded into a larger decline in monthly turnover.Many traders and market participants opposed CAS and urged the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) to roll back the mechanism, saying that it creates significant uncertainty between the live market price and the final settlement price.Read more: FOMO alert: Retail investors sold 1,051 stocks before they soared 36% on averageA key concern has been that large orders in relatively thin volumes can cause sharp movements in stock prices seen at 3.15 versus those at 3.30. However, the regulator has clarified that CAS is here to stay. Sebi Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey said last week that he envisages no changes to the mechanism, indicating enhanced participation as investors become more aware of the new process.Mehul Kothari, deputy vice-president at Anand Rathi Share and Stock Brokers said the shift in the expiry-day trading structure has reduced some of the very short-term speculative activity that was contributing significantly to options volumes."In addition, the introduction of CAS has altered trading behaviour around the close and expiry, with participants adapting to the new mechanism," said Kothari, adding that lower market volatility and a relatively range-bound market have also reduced the opportunities for aggressive directional and intraday options trading.

items.content:
…Suspends renal transplant services
By Chidinma Chukwu
ABUJA — Wellington Clinics, Abuja, has denied involvement in any financial transaction linked to a controversial kidney transplant performed at its facility, saying its role was limited to providing an equipped theatre and a conducive environment for the procedure.
The hospital said the transplant was conducted by an independent specialist medical team led by Dr Benjamin Friday Oyimeh, Senior Consultant Nephrologist and Chief Executive Officer of Crown Medical and Kidney Centre, which it said retained responsibility for the recruitment, evaluation and screening of the donor and recipient.
In a statement signed by its Director of Administration, Mr Yemi Olatunbosun, and made available to journalists on Tuesday, Wellington Clinics said it neither participated in, facilitated, negotiated nor benefited from any transactional arrangement relating to the transplant.
The hospital said the kidney donor, identified in its records as Abubakar Hassan, was admitted on April 24, 2026, and underwent a left donor nephrectomy the same day.
It explained that, under its collaboration model with specialist medical teams, the lead consultant is responsible for patient recruitment, clinical assessment, donor-recipient compatibility, informed consent, ethical screening and other clinical and medico-legal requirements.
According to the hospital, the consultant and his team were also responsible for ensuring compliance with the National Health Act 2014 and relevant guidelines of the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria, MDCN.
Wellington said the donor presented several documents at the point of admission, including a court affidavit, digital National Identification Number, NIN, slip, birth certificate issued by the National Population Commission, NPC, affidavit of consent and statutory declaration of age.
“He was also accompanied by a man identified as Abubakar Isa, whom he described as his brother. The donor was admitted under the name Abubakar Hassan, with a date of birth of February 4, 2000, and hospital number WCA/8066/2026,” the hospital said.
It said the donor was discharged on April 28, four days after the operation, but was readmitted on July 11 for wound management and removal of residual stitches before being discharged two days later.
The hospital added that the kidney removed from the donor was immediately transplanted into a patient suffering from end-stage kidney failure.
It stressed that neither the donor nor the recipient died as a result of the procedure.
“Wellington Clinics did not participate, facilitate, negotiate, or benefit from any transactional arrangements,” the statement said.
The management said it relied on the documents and declarations presented by the donor and the specialist medical team, noting that it had no independent means or legal duty to conduct forensic investigations into the relationship between a donor and recipient.
It added that there was no indication at the time of admission that the documents presented were false or that the donor had misrepresented his identity.
The hospital, however, said the donor’s real name was allegedly Samuel Ezekiel, claiming that he had previously deposed to an affidavit before an FCT High Court adopting the name Abubakar Hassan.
Wellington said the Nigeria Police Force was investigating the matter and assured that it was cooperating fully with the authorities.
As a result of the allegations, the hospital disclosed that it had suspended all renal transplant-related services pending the outcome of the investigation.
It reaffirmed its commitment to ethical and evidence-based healthcare, saying it would abide by the findings and directives of the relevant authorities.
The hospital also urged investigators to examine its records and other documents relating to the procedure, saying they would help clarify the extent of its involvement in the controversial transplant.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
… CFR rises to 24.4%, 87% of cases concentrated in five states
By Chioma Obinna
Nigeria’s Lassa fever outbreak on Tuesday continued to take a heavy toll, with the country recording 252 deaths from 1,035 confirmed cases as of epidemiological week 33, translating to a case fatality rate (CFR) of 24.4 per cent.
According to the latest figures from the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, (NCDC) showed that 14 new confirmed cases were recorded between August 10 and 16, 2026, a sharp increase from the four cases reported in the preceding week.
The new cases were reported in Ondo, Bauchi, Edo and Benue states, bringing the cumulative number of suspected cases to 7,426, while six probable cases have also been recorded.
The development has raised concern as the current CFR remains significantly higher than the 18.6 per cent recorded during the same period in 2025, despite intensified surveillance, case management and infection prevention measures.
According to the NCDC Lassa Fever Situation Report for Epi Week 33, released on the outbreak, 23 states and 117 Local Government Areas have recorded at least one confirmed case this year.
The agency said five states including Ondo, Bauchi, Taraba, Edo and Benue, accounted for 87 per cent of all confirmed cases recorded nationally.
Ondo State alone accounted for 33 per cent of confirmed cases, followed by Bauchi with 25 per cent, Taraba 13 per cent, Edo 10 per cent and Benue six per cent.
The NCDC said the predominant age group affected was 21–30 years, with patients ranging from one to 93 years and a median age of 30 years. The male-to-female ratio among confirmed cases was 1:0.9.
The agency further disclosed that 54 healthcare workers have been affected cumulatively in 2026, although no new healthcare worker infection was reported during week 33.
The rising fatality rate has been linked in part to late presentation and poor health-seeking behaviour.
The NCDC identified late presentation of cases, high cost of treatment and clinical management, poor environmental sanitation, inadequate awareness in high-burden communities and healthcare-worker infections among the major challenges confronting the response.
It warned that delayed presentation could worsen outcomes, stressing the need for early recognition, referral and treatment.
The agency said, “Healthcare workers” should maintain a high index of suspicion for Lassa fever, initiate timely referral and treatment, and adhere strictly to standard infection prevention and control procedures.
To contain the outbreak, the NCDC said it had strengthened surveillance, contact tracing, laboratory diagnosis, infection prevention and control, risk communication and case management across affected states.
It also reported the development of a 30-day Healthcare Worker Protection Plan with support from the World Health Organisation, WHO, and US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, aimed at reducing infections among frontline health workers in endemic states.
The agency said PPE had been pre-positioned and distributed to health facilities, while national rapid response teams had been deployed across seven high-burden states.
It added that active case search and contact tracing were being supported in high-burden states, while healthcare workers were receiving additional training on Lassa fever case management, screening, triage and infection prevention.
The NCDC also urged states to intensify community engagement throughout the year, particularly in high-burden areas, to improve awareness and encourage early presentation.
“States should bolster efforts all-year-round for community engagements on prevention of Lassa fever,” the agency advised.
Lassa fever is an acute viral haemorrhagic illness primarily transmitted to humans through contact with food or household items contaminated by urine or faeces of infected multimammate rats. It can also spread from person to person, particularly in healthcare settings where infection prevention measures are inadequate.
The NCDC said strengthening the capacity of states to prevent, detect and respond promptly remains critical to reducing deaths from the disease.

“At this difficult moment, the Vice-Chancellor, Professor Mrs. Eunice Omonzejie, on behalf of the Governing Council, Management, staff and students of Ambrose Alli University, extends heartfelt condolences to the wife, children, siblings and the entire Orbih family.”

“As a trusted partner, his loyalty, wisdom and sense of duty have remained invaluable to the administration.”

“I must thank Vice-President Shettima for his steadfast support and partnership as we continue to join hands in delivering the promises of Renewed Hope to Nigerians.”

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
The National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP) says it has rescued more than 3,000 victims of sexual and gender-based violence in 2026.
The Head, Press and Public Relations of NAPTIP, Mr Vincent Adekoye, disclosed this on Tuesday in Abuja at the Joint Security News Briefing organised by the Office of the National Security Adviser.
Adekoye said the agency also secured more than 20 convictions in 2026 as it intensified operations against human trafficking and exploitation.
He said human trafficking was increasingly migrating to the digital space, with criminal networks exploiting social media, encrypted messaging platforms and fake online job portals.
“Human trafficking is migrating to the digital space, and we must adapt our response to meet this emerging threat,” Adekoye said.
He said traffickers were increasingly targeting Nigerian youths with fraudulent offers of lucrative employment in Southeast Asia, particularly Laos, Cambodia and Thailand.
According to him, victims are often stripped of their travel documents on arrival and forced into guarded compounds controlled by cybercrime syndicates.
Adekoye said the victims were subsequently coerced into online fraud, romance scams and cryptocurrency-related crimes targeting people in other countries.
He said NAPTIP was strengthening intelligence gathering and international cooperation to identify digital recruitment pipelines and dismantle transnational trafficking networks.
The spokesperson said the agency secured nine convictions and rescued more than 80 suspected trafficking victims during operations conducted in July and August.
He said intelligence-led operations around the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja and Mallam Aminu Kano International Airport disrupted trafficking “muster points” used to transit victims abroad.
Adekoye said rescued victims were placed under NAPTIP’s protective care and provided with counselling, medical evaluation and rehabilitation.
He also disclosed that the agency was investigating the alleged trafficking and illegal adoption of 54 children from Loko community in Nasarawa State.
He said the children were allegedly taken from displaced families through a fraudulent “Back to School Initiative” and trafficked to unauthorised orphanages and adoption brokers.
Adekoye said investigators were working with state welfare authorities and other security agencies to recover the children and prosecute those responsible.
He said NAPTIP also sealed an illegal maternity facility in Port Harcourt in August and arrested three persons allegedly linked to an international baby-selling network.
The spokesperson said the agency, supported by partners, had inaugurated a specialised Sexual and Gender-Based Violence Media Corps to strengthen public awareness and address technology-facilitated exploitation.
He urged Nigerians to verify overseas employment offers before travelling and avoid engaging unverified online recruiters.
Adekoye also called on members of the public to report suspicious recruitment schemes, unauthorised child-placement activities and unregistered care facilities to NAPTIP.
He said the agency would continue adapting its strategies to ensure that technology did not become a tool for traffickers to recruit, exploit and control vulnerable Nigerians.
Meanwhile, the Public Relations Officer of the Nigeria Immigration Service (NIS), ACI Akinsola Akinlabi, said NIS had intensified border surveillance and migration management to identify and disrupt activities linked to irregular migration and human trafficking.
Akinlabi said the Service rescued 23 suspected victims during interventions in July and August, including cases intercepted at airports and land-border locations.
He said 99 foreigners were repatriated during the period, while the Service also apprehended a stowaway and identified four persons of interest during its border and migration-control operations.
Akinlabi said the NIS had commenced the second phase of measures to extend enhanced migration-control coverage to additional land-border points.
He said the Service was also strengthening airport operations and personnel capacity to improve the detection of trafficking, document fraud and other forms of irregular migration.
The spokesperson said the NIS and National Counter-Terrorism Centre had jointly hosted a national coordination meeting on the implementation of the Advance Passenger Information and Passenger Name Record systems.
He said the initiative would strengthen passenger screening, information sharing and the early identification of persons and movements considered security concerns.

items.content:
Justice Inyang Ekwo of the Federal High Court in Abuja has warned lawyers involved in the suit seeking the disqualification of President Bola Tinubu from the 2027 presidential election against discussing the matter in the media or on social media.
Justice Ekwo gave the warning on Tuesday while adjourning proceedings in the case instituted by former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar and the African Democratic Congress (ADC).
The judge said all arguments concerning the suit, which centres on an alleged forged National Youth Service Scheme (NYSC) certificate, must be presented before the court rather than through public platforms.
“This case is to be conducted in court and not in the media, whether it is regular or social,” Ekwo warned.
He cautioned that any attempt by counsel to discuss the case on social media would attract sanctions.
“If this case is discussed on social media, I will hold counsel for the party responsible, and I will take very drastic action.”
The suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/1888/2026, has Tinubu, the All Progressives Congress (APC) and the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) as defendants.
At Tuesday’s sitting, Omosanya Popoola announced his appearance for Tinubu, while Joseph Onu, counsel to Atiku, told the court that the plaintiffs had yet to serve the president with the originating processes.
Onu said the plaintiffs were insisting on personal service on Tinubu because of the sensitive nature of the case. Alternatively, he said they would consider substituted service if the president formally agreed to receive the documents through his lawyer.
“My lord, this is a very important case, and we do not want to leave any chance for a technicality. We do not want to fall into any trap,” Onu said.
He added: “But if we have a written undertaking from the 1st defendant to be served through counsel, we will accept.”
Counsel to INEC, Alex Iziyon, opposed the demand for personal service, arguing that the appearance of Tinubu’s lawyer before the court was enough to establish that the president was represented in the proceedings.
Iziyon also urged the court to move quickly on the matter, noting that more than 17 days had elapsed since the case was filed. He said INEC was prepared to submit its defence within 10 days.
Justice Ekwo, however, said the court could not determine how the plaintiffs should pursue their case.
The judge thereafter adjourned the matter until September 28 for mention.
Atiku and the ADC are challenging Tinubu’s eligibility to participate in the 2027 presidential election, alleging that the president submitted a forged NYSC discharge certificate to INEC.
The plaintiffs alleged that the document submitted to the electoral commission bears the name “Tinubu Bola Adekunle” and contend that this amounted to the presentation of false information to INEC.
They are relying on Section 137(1)(j) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which provides for disqualification where a candidate presents a forged certificate to the electoral commission.
