items.author: ZAFAR BHUTTA
items.content:
The government has approved the Pakistan Information Security Framework (PISF) 2026 aimed at reducing risk exposure for public sector orginsations while directing to specify clear implementation timelines and include a provision for an independent third-party audit.
It has also directed the Ministry of Planning, Development and Special Initiatives that no proposal of any ministry regarding independent and new data centres would be approved or included in PC-1s.
During discussions in a recent meeting, the cabinet members appreciated the Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunication for timely formulation of the Pakistan Information Security Framework 2026, which was urgently required in view of the growing cybersecurity threats.
They, however, observed that the framework should specify clear implementation timelines and should also include a provision for an independent third-party audit.
On a query, the meeting was informed that the prime minister had already issued strict directives that the policy framework prepared by the IT ministry for the establishment and use of data centres should be strictly adhered to and enforced. Also, it should be ensured that the data centres already established by the IT ministry are used by every ministry for any of their initiatives and the Ministry of Planning will ensure that no proposal of any ministry regarding independent/new data centre is approved/included in the PC-1.
Sources in the Ministry of IT and Telecom told The Express Tribune that the cabinet was informed that increasing digitalisation of government functions, expansion of e-governance initiatives and growing interconnectivity of public sector systems had significantly increased exposure to cyber risks and "government entities now rely extensively on information systems for service delivery, financial operations, citizen data management and inter-organisational coordination/ communication".
The ministry further said that variations in institutional capacity and the absence of a unified reference framework had resulted in inconsistent security practices across the public sector, leading to vulnerabilities and exposures. The National Cyber Security Policy 2021, the CERT Rules 2023 and CERT Council emphasise the strengthening of governance, coordinated response mechanisms and standardised implementation of information security controls, therefore, a nationally approved framework is required to translate policy direction into a uniform operational structure, enable regulatory oversight and ensure accountability.
The approval and implementation of PISF will enable the achievement of objectives, in line with the National Cyber Security Policy 2021, which include establishing a standardised national information security baseline across all public and private sector entities and designated critical sectors. It will also strengthen the protection of government information assets, digital platforms and citizen data, while enhancing institutional capacity to prevent, detect and respond to cyber incidents.
The maturity-based compliance mechanism will help in evidence-based decision-making, targeted investment in information/ cybersecurity capabilities, secure digital transformation initiatives and continuity of essential government services.
It will also enhance public trust in government digital services and strengthen national resilience in the digital domain. The Ministry of IT said that the PISF may be notified as the national baseline information security standard for all public and private sector entities (federal or provincial), including autonomous/ semi-autonomous, corporations, CERTs, and the designated critical information infrastructure in order to establish standardised information security governance and strengthen the national cyber security posture.

Speaking on the theme, “Collaborative Approaches to Strengthening Security and Regional Stability,” the President said insecurity had become too complex for any single security agency, government or community to tackle in isolation.
“No single agency, no single tier of government and no single community can secure this region acting alone. Insecurity does not respect state boundaries or agency mandates,” he said.

items.author: Olusola Jide Jide
items.content:
President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has warned that military action alone cannot end insecurity in the North-Central region, urging communities, traditional and religious leaders, youths, women and the private sector to unite with security agencies in confronting criminality and addressing the root causes of violence.
Tinubu gave the charge on Monday at the 2026 North Central Regional Security Summit in Makurdi, Benue State, where he was represented by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume.
Speaking on the theme, “Collaborative Approaches to Strengthening Security and Regional Stability,” the President said insecurity had become too complex for any single security agency, government or community to tackle in isolation.
“No single agency, no single tier of government and no single community can secure this region acting alone. Insecurity does not respect state boundaries or agency mandates,” he said.
Opposition Summit: We can repeat what APC did in 2015 &#8211; Rep minority caucus
Provide evidence on replacement of your candidates, INEC challenges NDC
Tinubu urged stakeholders to end rivalry, duplication of efforts and the withholding of intelligence, stressing that criminals often move across local government and state boundaries while security responses remain fragmented.
While commending the Armed Forces, police and intelligence agencies for recent gains against terrorists and other criminal groups, including the neutralisation of commanders, surrender of fighters and rescue of captives, the President said military operations must be complemented by measures addressing the conditions that fuel violence.
“Military action alone will not deliver lasting peace to the North Central. Force can suppress violence; it cannot resolve the grievances that produce it,” he said.
He identified competition over land and water, climate change, desertification, unresolved land-use disputes, weak local conflict-resolution mechanisms and the proliferation of illicit weapons among factors sustaining insecurity.
Tinubu urged traditional and religious leaders to become the first line of defence against emerging threats by providing early warning and promoting reconciliation.
“I ask you to be our first line of early warning and our most trusted voice of reconciliation,” he said.
He also called on communities to provide security agencies with timely intelligence and stop protecting criminals because of family, ethnic or other affiliations.
“Security begins with you. I call on every citizen to share information with the security agencies, to refuse to shield criminality out of kinship or sentiment,” he said.
The President said women and youths must be central to peace-building, while government would expand economic opportunities to reduce the attraction of criminality among young people.
“To our young people, your energy is this region’s greatest asset. This administration is committed to expanding the opportunities that make a rifle a far less attractive prospect than a livelihood,” he said.
He also urged investors and development partners to increase their presence in the region, stressing that economic development was integral to security.
“Peace and investment reinforce one another. Every factory built, every farm expanded and every young person employed in this region is a contribution to its security,” Tinubu said.
The President directed the Minister of Defence, Gen. Christopher Musa (retd.), to transmit the summit’s recommendations to him, insisting that its outcome must include clear responsibilities, timelines and measurable results.
“We will be judged not by the quality of our deliberations here, but by whether a farmer in this region sleeps more soundly a year from now,” he said.

items.content:
The Capital Development Authority (CDA) is working on a time-based electronic parking system at seven locations in Islamabad, with the duration of vehicles’ stay to be recorded digitally and parking charges monitored through an electronic dashboard.
CDA officials told the Senate Standing Committee on Interior that work on the project was underway. Under the proposed system, the time a vehicle remains in a designated parking area will be tracked on a dashboard, allowing the authority to monitor both parking duration and applicable charges electronically.
Senator Naseema Ehsan said a traffic management system similar to one introduced in Karachi had also been started in Islamabad. She highlighted the difficulties faced by residents and visitors in finding parking spaces, noting that people from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Balochistan and other provinces also live in or regularly visit the capital.
Director General Enforcement Anum Fatima told the committee that the Blue Area parking plaza had been completed and would help address parking problems in the area. She said parking fees were being collected according to the CDA’s approved layout plan, while cashless payments and QR codes were being used for transactions at all parking facilities.
Senator Abid Sher Ali questioned the CDA’s parking arrangements, pointing out that parking fees were still being collected on roads despite the authority’s statement that the Blue Area parking plaza had been completed.
He described the two positions as contradictory and asked the CDA Chairman about parking arrangements in newly constructed plazas.
Sher Ali also proposed that new plazas should not be granted a No Objection Certificate unless they provide adequate underground parking facilities.

items.author: Afaq Wajdan Malik
items.content:
Xiaomi’s upcoming XRING 03 chipset could make the Xiaomi 18 Fold one of the first smartphones to use next-generation LPDDR6 RAM.
Chinese memory maker CXMT is reportedly preparing to begin mass production of LPDDR6 chips next month, giving it an early lead over Samsung, SK hynix and Micron.
The development follows reports that Xiaomi has partnered with CXMT to bring LPDDR6 support to its XRING 03 platform.
Xiaomi 18 Fold Expected to Get LPDDR6 First
According to the latest information, Xiaomi could reserve CXMT’s first LPDDR6 memory for the upcoming Xiaomi 18 Fold.
The foldable is expected to compete with devices such as Apple’s upcoming iPhone Fold and Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold8.
However, production volumes are expected to remain relatively low.
One report estimates that XRING 03-powered devices may not exceed around 300,000 units in total shipments, suggesting that Xiaomi and CXMT may initially keep the LPDDR6 partnership limited.
This could make it easier for CXMT to supply enough memory despite the challenges involved in producing a new generation of DRAM.
CXMT Faces Production Challenges
CXMT may be ahead of larger memory companies in bringing LPDDR6 into production, but scaling output could be much more difficult.
The company faces U.S. trade restrictions that limit its access to advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment.
As a result, CXMT reportedly relies on older Deep Ultraviolet (DUV) lithography systems and more complicated multi-patterning methods.
These techniques can increase manufacturing costs while reducing production yields.
That could make it difficult for CXMT to produce LPDDR6 memory in the same volumes as Samsung, SK hynix or Micron.
XRING 03 Could Help Xiaomi Stand Out
The XRING 03 is expected to use TSMC’s 3nm N3P process, meaning Xiaomi should have fewer problems securing enough processor production capacity.
Memory supply may therefore become the bigger challenge.
Xiaomi could technically use LPDDR5X instead, but the company may want LPDDR6 to help differentiate the Xiaomi 18 Fold, especially if the device launches at a premium price.
CXMT’s early move into LPDDR6 could also help it secure additional customers in China, including Huawei.
However, the larger test will be whether the company can increase production while maintaining acceptable yields.
Samsung, SK hynix and Micron may still catch up quickly once they begin large-scale LPDDR6 manufacturing.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
With more than 1 billion people living with obesity worldwide, health experts in Lahore on August 31 called for treating obesity as a chronic disease and expanding access to medical and surgical care in Pakistan.
Obesity has emerged as a major public health challenge. The World Health Organization estimates that in 2022, 43% of adults globally were overweight and 16% were living with obesity – more than double the rate recorded in 1990.
Pakistan is seeing one of the fastest increases. According to WHO data for 2022, 23% of Pakistani adults were living with obesity, marking a 16.4% increase over the previous decade. Modeled estimates show nearly 60% of adults are now overweight and 25% are obese with obesity rates having more than tripled in 20 years.
Health experts estimate around 38 million Pakistanis are currently living with obesity, with women and urban residents disproportionately impacted. Among children, 40% are overweight or obese, and projections warn that 57% of Pakistani children could be obese by age 35 if current trends continue.
A WHO-supported STEPS survey previously found low physical activity and inadequate fruit and vegetable consumption to be significant risk factors. The WHO also classifies obesity as a chronic, relapsing disease* linked to type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease and other non-communicable diseases.
Against this backdrop, Chisel Health concluded its Obesity Awareness Week with an Obesity Evening in Lahore on August 31, bringing together patients, healthcare professionals and community members for discussions on awareness, education and modern treatment options.
Speakers highlighted the need to move away from viewing obesity as solely a matter of lifestyle or willpower, and stressed the importance of personalized medical care and evidence-based treatment.
At the forefront of this evolving field is Dr. Tanveer Abbas, recognized as Pakistan’s youngest bariatric surgeon with the highest surgical volume. Through Chisel Health, Dr. Abbas has established a dedicated obesity-focused centre where patients receive comprehensive assessment and treatment under one roof. The centre offers a multidisciplinary approach to weight management, with a focus on advanced bariatric surgery and weight loss procedures.
“We need to stop seeing obesity as a failure of willpower. It is a chronic disease. With the right medical and surgical support, patients can achieve long-term health outcomes, not just weight loss,” Dr. Tanveer Abbas said.
The Obesity Evening represented another step in Chisel Health’s efforts to bring obesity into the centre of Pakistan’s healthcare conversation. As obesity continues to rise across generations, initiatives such as Obesity Awareness Week underscore the need for greater awareness, earlier intervention and broader access to effective treatment.

items.author: Press Release
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
OPPO has officially launched the Reno16 Series in Pakistan, bringing the Reno16 and Reno16 F to local shelves alongside a striking new companion device, OPPO Bubble. Built for a new generation of creators, the series pairs a design nobody has seen on a phone before with a camera system built for storytelling. The launch spilled off the stage too, into an exclusive celebration across Lahore that had the city’s biggest content creators talking.
The Pop White edition has a planet floating on its back. Not printed, not painted, actually floating, thanks to HoloVerse 3D Technology: millions of micro lenses under the glass bending light into a nebula style visual that shifts as you move the phone. It’s Pakistan’s first 3D Pop Planet Design, and Pakistan gets it on day one.
The rest of the series feels just as considered. A one piece cold sculpted back flows straight into the camera module with zero seams and way less dust buildup. The Reno16 keeps things pocket friendly at 6.32 inches with an aerospace grade aluminium frame, while the Reno16 F goes bigger at 6.57 inches for anyone who wants more room to scroll and stream. Pick your mood in Pop White and Twilight Violet.
The Reno16 Series with Quad 50MP Cameras was designed with creators in mind to make both capturing and editing content more intuitive, expressive, and fun a phone designed to create with.
The 50MP Ultra Wide Selfie Camera comes with a 100-degree field of view, so group selfies actually fit everyone. Around back, a triple camera setup pairs a high-resolution main sensor with OIS, a 3.5x telephoto portrait lens, and an ultra-wide for whenever you need to fit more into the shot.
New to the Reno Series, Pop Cam introduces a dedicated creative shooting experience directly within the Camera app. This feature lets the user apply vintage-inspired styles such as Digicam, Instant Film and Light Leak effects with a single tap, making it easy to create distinctive photos with different moods and aesthetics.. Filming stays smooth with 4K Auto Straighten Video and Dual View Video 2.0, letting you switch lenses mid recording.
Beyond shooting, the Reno16 Series also expands creative editing capabilities through a new Create hub within the Photos app, bringing together a range of AI-powered tools for more playful, personalized storytelling. AI Remix Collage lets users combine multiple photos or short videos into layered visual compositions with animated stickers, outlines, and text, and it even lets users extract moving subjects from Motion Photos or videos and use them as stickers. Popout Collage 2.0 further enhances creative flexibility by allowing subjects to break out of the frame in multiple directions for more dynamic visual effects.
ColorOS 16 runs underneath it all, loaded with AI that actually feels useful, from AI Mind Space organising your screen to AI Menu Translation turning a confusing foreign menu into something you can picture before the food arrives. The Reno16 Series also introduces AI Mind Pilot, which intelligently coordinates multiple AI models to deliver more relevant and context-aware assistance.
None of this matters if the phone can’t keep up. The Reno16 packs a 6,700mAh battery; the Reno16 F pushes that to 7,000mAh, both with 80W SUPERVOOC fast charging. The Reno16 runs on the Snapdragon 7 Gen 4 Mobile Platform, with AI LinkBoost 4.0 keeping connections steady in crowded spaces, plus IP68, IP69 and IP69K resistance, wet hands and all.
Alongside the phones, OPPO introduced something nobody saw coming: OPPO Bubble. This tiny 35 gram magnetic companion clips onto compatible cases or rings and turns into a live monitor for your rear camera, so framing a shot is never a guessing game again. It also works as a remote viewfinder and shutter button from up to 10 metres away, and its own app lets you personalise the display with your own photos, animations, text and colours.
OPPO Pakistan followed the launch with something the city is still talking about. The Reno16 Coffee Party took over in Lahore, pulling in the country’s Big lifestyle influencers for a first look at the Renoverse, an immersive showcase built around the Reno16 and OPPO Bubble. The cafe was transformed into a dreamy, planet lit set piece matching the phone’s floating design. Guests shot selfies with the Ultra Wide Selfie Camera, tested Bubble as a live framing monitor, and captured it all through Pop Cam’s vintage filters. Within hours, the Renoverse had spilled onto every feed in Lahore, proof OPPO isn’t just selling a phone; it’s building a whole aesthetic around it.
The OPPO Reno16 Series and OPPO Bubble are officially launched across Pakistan, with pre -orders starting today, with the first sale lined up for September 5th. Reno16 and Reno16 F will be offered in Pop White and Twilight Violet. A phone with a floating planet on it, a magnetic sidekick to match, and a launch moment the whole city showed up for- this is OPPO’s biggest design swing yet.

items.author: Our Correspondent
items.content:
The provincial assembly of Punjab on Monday passed the Punjab Anti-Terrorism (Amendment) Bill, 2026 amid protests and a walkout by opposition lawmakers.
During the session, Punjab Assembly Speaker Malik Muhammad Ahmad Khan and Opposition Leader Moin Riaz Qureshi held a heated debate over the new legislation's legal and constitutional implications.
Addressing the house, the speaker issued a ruling confirming that the bill could legally be placed on the agenda, citing Article 142 of the Constitution concerning criminal-law jurisdiction.
Defending the move, the speaker recalled how terrorism claimed more than 100,000 lives in Pakistan during the war on terror, including those of high-profile figures, and led to attacks on places of worship.
He argued that, in the past, terrorists often walked free due to a lack of witness protection and physical security. He noted that even democratic nations such as the US have established “faceless” or anonymous courts to deal with extreme terror threats, urging the opposition to propose constructive amendments rather than block the bill.
Qureshi condemned the “draconian” law, which he claimed aimed at "crushing the citizens of Punjab”. He accused the ruling government of introducing the amendment to target political rivals, particularly PTI leaders and activists, much like previous defamation and National Accountability Bureau laws.
He raised concerns about a provision under which a Grade-20-designated official would have the authority to advise the chief justice of the Lahore High Court on whether cases should be classified as “special security cases”.
Joining the debate, opposition lawmaker Ahmar Rashid Bhatti read out on the floor of the House an opinion column he had written for a daily newspaper, comparing the proposed law to a 1909 British colonial-era act that Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah opposed.
He warned that allowing the identities and voices of judges, prosecutors, defence lawyers and witnesses to be concealed or altered would violate Article 10-A of the Constitution, which guarantees the fundamental right to a fair and transparent trial.
Following the intense debate, opposition members chanted slogans against the bill and walked out of the hall. As they exited, lawmaker Waqas Mann pointed out a lack of quorum, but the treasury benches successfully rallied enough members to maintain it.
With the opposition absent, their proposed amendments were rejected, and the House voted to approve the Anti-Terrorism (Amendment) Bill, 2026.
The bill seeks to insert a new Section 21AAA into the Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997, creating a “special security case” mechanism for cases in which participants are considered to require extraordinary protection.
Under the proposed law, a designated authority — an officer of at least BS-20 whose identity would itself remain confidential — could declare a case or a class of cases a special security case. At the authority’s request, the LHC chief justice would assign the case to an Anti-Terrorism Court judge.
The bill also proposes that the identities of judges, public prosecutors, defence counsel, police officers, witnesses and other persons involved in such proceedings “shall not be disclosed”.
Judicial orders would carry official titles instead of the judges’ names, while witnesses would be identified through codes issued by the designated authority.
The proceedings could be held at secure premises or conducted through video links, including from prisons. The proposed provision would also allow the government to adopt other security measures it considers appropriate.

On August 23, snowfall at Spantik forced the suspension of efforts to recover the body with the recovery team reaching Camp 2 before being advised to return to base camp and wait for a suitable weather window, the Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) said on Sunday.
According to an earlier statement, the ACP announced that Dr Asma had died during her descent from Spantik after successfully reaching the 7,027-metre summit. The club said, "she had suffered serious high-altitude sickness at around 6,400 metres, which apparently led to her death".
In the latest statement, the club said Asma’s body remained at an altitude of about 6,400 metres, while approval for a helicopter “mercy mission” was also being sought on humanitarian grounds with the support of the Pakistan Army.
In a post on X, Tarar said on August 23 that high-altitude porters were expected to reach Camp 3 and bring Dr Asma’s body down to Base Camp by Monday. However, the rescue team had reached almost Camp 3 before severe weather, heavy snowfall and strong winds forced it to turn back and return to Camp 2.

items.author: Web Desk
items.content:
The federal government on Monday increased the price of petrol by 77 paisas per litre, while decreasing the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs1.03 per litre, respectively, for September 1.
According to a notification issued by the Petroleum Division, the price of petrol was fixed at Rs342.79 per litre, while HSD would cost Rs370.41 per litre for September 1.
The latest revision comes after the government reduced the price of petrol and HSD by 58 paisas and 17 paisas per litre, respectively, effective from August 29 till August 31.
Read: Govt decreases petrol price by 58 paisas, HSD by 17 paisas till August 31
Last month, the government announced a new pricing mechanism under which petroleum product prices would be reviewed and notified on a daily basis, replacing the weekly pricing mechanism, as renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to drive volatility in global oil markets and raise concerns over fuel supplies.
According to the Pakistan Economic Survey 2024-25, petroleum products constitute one of the country's largest import categories, making the economy highly vulnerable to changes in global crude oil prices. Domestic refineries satisfy only part of national demand, while the remainder is met through imports of crude oil and refined petroleum products. Consequently, every increase in international oil prices raises Pakistan's import bill, pressures foreign exchange reserves, and contributes to inflation.
Pakistan previously exercised significant government control over petroleum pricing through subsidies and administrative interventions. While these measures temporarily protected consumers, they imposed substantial fiscal costs. During periods of elevated global oil prices, successive governments delayed passing price increases to consumers, creating financial pressures for oil marketing companies, refineries, and the national budget. Large fuel subsidies widened fiscal deficits, increased public borrowing, and weakened macroeconomic stability.
Global geopolitical developments continue to pose significant risks. International oil prices are influenced by decisions taken by OPEC+, conflicts in the Middle East, sanctions on oil-producing nations, and disruptions in critical shipping routes such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea. Any interruption in these supply chains can immediately increase crude oil prices and freight costs. Since Pakistan imports the majority of its petroleum requirements, these developments quickly translate into higher domestic fuel prices.
Oil prices gained more than 2% on Monday after a resumption of military action between the US and Iran ‌rekindled market concerns about global supply disruption, as the conflict extended into its sixth month.
Brent crude futures were up $2.17, or 2.46%, to $90.27 a barrel at 12:12 pm EDT (1612 GMT). US West Texas Intermediate crude was up $2.06, or 2.47%, to $85.46. Brent rose as high as $91.52 during the ​session, its highest since August 25.
Last week, crude stocks in the US Strategic Petroleum Reserve fell by around 3.1 million ​barrels to 286.6 million barrels.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
John Ternus takes over as Apple’s chief executive on Tuesday, inheriting a company that towers over the smartphone market but trails its rivals in artificial intelligence (AI).
One of his biggest challenges will be balancing the company’s dependence on China while parrying acute political pressure from the White House.
The handover ends Tim Cook’s 15-year run, replacing the operations specialist who built Apple’s supply chain with the engineer who built its hardware.
Ternus, 51, joined Apple’s design team in 2001 and worked his way up to senior vice president of hardware engineering, reporting to Cook.
He leads the engineering teams behind Apple’s entire product lineup, including the iPhones that generate most of the company’s revenue.
He gets barely a week to settle in, with Apple holding its annual iPhone event on September 9, where it is expected to unveil its first foldable handset.
“Tim Cook left the house in phenomenal order,” said Dan Ives, partner and senior managing director at investment firm Yorkville Ives & Co.
“But now it’s about Ternus defining the AI chapter.”
Ives expects the new chief executive to lean into what he knows.
“There’s no reason to fix what’s already working,” he said, predicting Ternus will concentrate on hardware innovation while leaving Cook’s supply chain intact.
Some analysts had argued software chief Craig Federighi was the more logical pick for a company scrambling to catch up on AI.
Carolina Milanesi, an analyst at Creative Strategies, said that misreads how consumers actually adopt technology.
“Consumers are still buying hardware first, and it’s going to be like that for a long time,” she said.
“You’re not going to discover the value of AI if you’re not interested in the hardware.”
Ternus earned a bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering from the University of Pennsylvania and worked as an engineer at Virtual Research Systems before joining Apple.
Inside the company he is credited with driving a push to make products more durable, reliable and resilient, and with design work that cut their carbon footprint.
Read More: Sony, Warner sue Anthropic over alleged mass copyright infringement
The harder question is what kind of leader he becomes.
“Even people that know him now don’t know him as a CEO,” Milanesi said.
“You might know him as the head of engineering, but once you’re CEO, things change. Your responsibility is bigger, your power is bigger. You’re dancing a different kind of dance.”
‘Learn on the job’
Nowhere is that gap wider than in the geopolitical role Cook excelled at, courting both Beijing and Donald Trump’s White House to protect a supply chain that runs largely through China.
Apple’s manufacturing operation is among the most complex in corporate history, a web of hundreds of suppliers and assembly lines that Cook painstakingly built over decades.
Cook in recent years began shifting some of the work elsewhere — iPhone assembly to India, other production to Vietnam — but the diversification has been gradual with China, one of Apple’s biggest consumer markets, still anchoring the system.
Complicating matters, Trump has repeatedly demanded Apple build iPhones on American soil, threatening tariffs on those made overseas.
Cook avoided the heaviest blows of Trump’s trade war by cultivating the president directly, making US investment commitments and political donations — all while also keeping Beijing onside.
The tricky political terrain will be new for Ternus.
“He knows Apple Park like the back of his pocket in terms of hardware,” Ives said of Ternus.
“But on the global stage — that’s probably one of the biggest areas where he’s going to have to learn on the job.”
Cook is not going far. He becomes executive chairman of Apple’s board on the same day, with a mandate the company has said includes engaging policymakers around the world.
“That was really clever,” said Milanesi, arguing the arrangement frees Ternus from a role Cook has handled alone for years.
The September 9 iPhone event will be the first public measure of the handover.
A foldable iPhone would be the most significant redesign in years, and Ternus will be its face — eight days into the job.
“This is a moment that they created for him,” Milanesi said.

items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
As India’s D2C and retail ecosystem enters the era of D2C 3.0, Inc42’s flagship, The D2C & Retail Summit, continues to bring the country’s sharpest founders, operators, investors, and enablers into one room to decode what it takes to build enduring consumer brands.
Over the past seven editions, Inc42 has closely tracked this ecosystem through in-depth reporting, data-led research, cohort-based learning programmes and marquee summits, chronicling how brands move from early traction to scale while navigating shifting capital cycles, quick-commerce economics and evolving consumer expectations.
This August, Inc42 brought together this ecosystem at the seventh edition of The D2C & Retail Summit, held on 19th August 2026 at The Leela Ambience, Gurugram, under the theme ‘Commerce In The Age Of AI & 10-Min Delivery.’
The invite-only summit convened 600+ founders, CXOs, investors and operators, selected from 2,000+ applications, with 70%+ of attendees being founders themselves. The agenda featured 15+ high-impact sessions and 5 hands-on workshops, alongside 60+ speakers spanning legacy brands, new-age disruptors, investors and commerce enablers.
Over half the brands represented were at ₹15 Cr+ ARR, with Fashion & Accessories and F&B leading the mix, alongside beauty & personal care, electronics, home and retail. The summit also featured 27 booths showcasing brands across categories.
The day’s marquee conversations included boAt cofounder Aman Gupta in an unfiltered AMA on building consumer brands and his new venture OFF/BEAT; Veeba founder and MD Viraj Bahl on scaling the sauces major to a ₹1,000 Cr+ FMCG engine; Snitch founder Siddharth Dungarwal on How Speed, Stores & Community Built A Cult Menswear Brand; Manyavar-Mohey CRO Vedant Modi on phygital retail; and Agilitas Sports cofounder Abhishek Ganguly on India’s sportswear opportunity.
Investors including Manu Chandra of Sauce.vc, Archana Jahagirdar of Rukam Capital, Aditya Singh of All In Capital and Kannan Sitaram of Fireside Ventures also came together to discuss where consumer capital is headed next.
In a fireside chat, Veeba’s Bahl said quick commerce can grow alongside other distribution channels, creating broader momentum for emerging consumer brands.
“Quick commerce entered Veeba’s journey relatively late but has since emerged as an important revenue channel and growth driver for the sauce and condiment maker,” Bahl said.
Meanwhile, Vedant Fashions’ Modi shared how data and AI are becoming central to how Manyavar-Mohey makes retail decisions. According to Modi, data helps the brand decide which products should go to which stores, move inventory based on local demand, and protect its premium pricing as it scales.
“Our overall growth is being driven by our ability to turn data into decisions — from product design and inventory allocation to store-level performance,” Modi said.
Across panels and workshops, speakers unpacked themes ranging from quick commerce margins and distribution moats to agentic commerce, export economics, and AI-led brand building.
But none of these insightful dialogues would have been possible without the support of our sponsors and partners, who helped make The Inc42 D2C & Retail Summit 2026 into a platform for meaningful dialogue and ecosystem-level impact.
Presenting Partner
PhonePe Payment Gateway
PhonePe Payment Gateway is the merchant payments arm of PhonePe, India’s leading digital payments major, enabling businesses to accept payments seamlessly across cards, UPI, net banking, wallets and BNPL.
With a strong focus on speed, reliability and high-conversion checkout experiences, PhonePe Payment Gateway helps D2C and retail brands meet the default expectation of seamless commerce, powering payment acceptance at scale for businesses across categories.
Kamal Lochan Das, business head, PhonePe Payment Gateway, joined a panel discussion titled ‘What Do India’s Shopping Patterns Reveal About The Next Growth Wave?‘, alongside Akash Agrawalla, cofounder of D2C spice brand ZOFF Foods; Ayush Bansal, director at Liberty Shoes; and was moderated by Karan Saraf of PwC India.
During the discussion, Das pointed to a shift in how Indian consumers approach digital payments, moving from a purely utility-led mindset to increasingly discretionary spending, as part of the broader convenience-led consumption wave reshaping Indian retail.
Co-Presenting Partners
Shadowfax
Shadowfax is a last-mile and hyperlocal logistics major, with a nationwide network spanning over 14,700 pin codes across first-mile, last-mile and sort centres. It serves ecommerce, quick commerce, food delivery and on-demand mobility clients, offering express parcel delivery alongside reverse pickups, exchanges and same-day delivery. The company listed on the NSE and BSE in January 2026.
During the summit, Shadowfax cofounder and CEO Abhishek Bansal moderated a fireside session with Agilitas Sports cofounder and CEO Abhishek Ganguli, titled ‘The $1 Bn Sportswear Bet: Building India’s Sportswear House.’
The conversation covered how Agilitas is building an integrated sportswear business, spanning athlete-led brands like One8 and Mochiko’s manufacturing depth to its retail and channel strategy, as it works towards building India’s own globally competitive sportswear house.
Glance
Glance, part of the InMobi Group, is an AI-native content and commerce platform that turns lock screens and connected devices into discovery surfaces. Through personalised, shoppable content delivered at scale, Glance is helping brands reach consumers at moments of high intent, extending discovery and commerce beyond the traditional app and website funnel.
Piyush Shah, cofounder of InMobi and Glance, joined a fireside chat titled ‘How Agentic Commerce Will Change The Way India Shops,‘ alongside The Bear House cofounder Harsh Somaiya and Inc42 cofounder and CEO Vaibhav Vardhan.
Explaining the premise behind agentic commerce, Shah said, “Consumers no longer need to navigate every stage of the purchase journey, a shift Glance is betting on through its AI shopping agent, which uses signals like a consumer’s preferences, budget, context and appearance to recommend products, create complete looks and enable virtual try-ons.”
Powered By Partners
Gupshup
Gupshup is a global conversational engagement platform that helps businesses build AI-led messaging experiences across WhatsApp, RCS and other channels. Its tools enable D2C brands to run conversational commerce, marketing and support at scale, turning routine customer touchpoints into revenue and retention opportunities.
Adwit Sharma, senior director – presales & solutions, Gupshup.ai, was also part of a DRS 2026 panel discussion titled ‘Turning One-Time Buyers Into Repeat Customers,’ where he spoke about moving conversations beyond customer support to discovery, education, reactivation and loyalty, and building AI-led conversational flows for recommendations, replenishment nudges and human escalation.
Elements Wellness
Elements Wellness is the flagship wellness brand of Indiashoppe, bringing together Ayurvedic formulations with modern research, quality manufacturing and scalable distribution. Since its 2014 launch, it has grown into one of India’s fastest-expanding wellness brands, with a presence across 750+ distribution centres and a growing digital education push for its distributor network.
Rajesh Chandan, founder of Elements Wellness, was also part of a panel discussion titled ‘Growth Without The Burn: Engineering Profitable Growth,’ where he spoke about moving from GMV-led growth to margin quality and capital-efficient scale, and building repeat cohorts and owned customer relationships as acquisition costs rise.
NITRO
Nitro is a revenue-as-a-service full-stack platform for ecommerce, D2C and retail brands, built to solve acquisition and retention bottlenecks with technology. The platform addresses challenges like anonymous visitor conversion, simplifying complex marketing workflows for growing consumer brands.
Nitro Commerce cofounder and CEO Umair Mohammad joined The D2C & Retail Summit 2026 as a speaker in a panel discussion titled ‘Is Quick Commerce A Margin Trap?‘ alongside 4700BC cofounder Chirag Gupta and Longway cofounder Ritish Garg, moderated by Commercify360 founder and managing director Renu Bisht.
During the session, Mohammad outlined three metrics: availability, assortment and advertising, or the “3As” that brands should track on quick commerce platforms, adding that returns on advertising spend shouldn’t be assessed in isolation. During the summit, Mohammad also launched Nitro Apps, an AI-powered platform that allows Shopify merchants to build private applications using prompts.
CashKaro
CashKaro is India’s leading cashback and coupons platform, helping shoppers save on purchases across major ecommerce and D2C sites while giving brands a high-intent channel to drive traffic, conversions and repeat purchases.
At The D2C & Retail Summit 2026, CashKaro cofounder Swati Bhargava moderated a panel discussion titled ‘Growth Without The Burn: Engineering Profitable Growth,’ featuring Neeru’s chairman and MD Avnish Kumar, Elements Wellness founder Rajesh Chandan and The Bear House cofounder Harsh Somaiya, on moving from GMV-led growth to margin quality and using AI to improve operating leverage without slowing growth momentum.
Base.com
Base.com is an ecommerce automation platform that helps D2C and omnichannel brands streamline order processing, fulfilment, and inventory tracking across multiple sales channels. Its workflow automation tools are aimed at cutting operational costs so brands can scale order volumes without scaling manual effort.
Pradeep Sekhar, CEO, India, Base.com, was also part of The DRS 2026 panel discussion titled ‘The Consumer Reset: Winning Gen Z, Bharat & Premium India,’ where he spoke about tracking India’s changing consumption map across Gen Z, Bharat and premium consumers, and reading consumer signals across channels to understand what drives conversion and repeat behaviour.
SafeGold
SafeGold is a digital gold platform that allows consumers to buy, sell, save in and redeem 24K gold in small denominations, backed by fully insured, vaulted physical gold. It works with fintech and D2C partners to embed gold-based savings and investment products into everyday commerce.
At DRS 2026, SafeGold’s cofounder and COO Rhea Chaterji was also part of a discussion titled ‘Turning One-Time Buyers Into Repeat Customers,’ where she spoke about moving conversations beyond customer support to discovery and loyalty, and turning conversational data into sharper segmentation and stronger owned customer relationships.
Loti
Loti AI helps individuals, creators, celebrities and brands protect their digital identity from misuse online. The company specialises in detecting and removing unauthorised content, including AI-generated deepfakes, fake advertisements and impersonation attempts.
The platform continuously scans the internet for content that misuses a person’s likeness, voice or brand assets. When harmful or fraudulent content is identified, Loti AI helps clients take action to remove it.
Snapmint
Snapmint is a no-cost EMI and buy-now-pay-later platform that helps ecommerce and D2C brands offer flexible, easy-to-access financing at checkout, aimed at improving affordability and conversion for a wider base of Indian shoppers.
Amitt Sharma, chief customer officer, Snapmint, was also part of a panel discussion titled ‘The Conversion Stack For Consumer Brands,’ where he spoke about why high-intent shoppers drop off despite strong product interest, and using flexible payment options as one lever to improve conversion without hurting margins or customer trust.
Stelcore Group
Stelcore Group works with Indian consumer brands on cross-border expansion, treating global growth as an infrastructure problem rather than an afterthought. Led by chairman Bharat Mandot, the group helps brands navigate customs, compliance, warehousing and market entry as they take their businesses beyond India.
Bharat Mandot, chairman of Stelcore Group and cofounder of Globbel, was also part of a panel discussion titled ‘Cracking Export Economics Beyond The Topline,’ where he spoke about choosing the right export markets and navigating the new export reality shaped by changing trade agreements and tariff uncertainty.
Associate Partners
Rukam Capital: Delhi-based Rukam Capital is an early stage venture capital firm investing in consumer products and services companies with strong growth potential. Its portfolio includes brands such as GO DESi, Sleepy Owl, Burger Singh, Curefoods, Beco, and Yoho.
Sagepilot: An AI-powered customer support platform that deploys human-like AI agents to handle customer engagement, sales and support across channels, helping brands automate service operations while improving response times.
Losung360: A 360-degree ecommerce enabler offering demand generation and demand fulfilment services, including supply chain management from order to delivery, for growing D2C brands and enterprises.
Amazon Shipping: It allows D2C brands and sellers to tap into Amazon’s logistics network to fulfil orders placed on their own websites and other sales channels, extending Amazon’s delivery reach beyond its own marketplace.
Ginesys: A cloud-based retail ERP, POS, OMS and WMS suite built for D2C brands, retailers and wholesalers, unifying inventory, warehouse, finance and omnichannel operations on a single platform.
Similarweb: A digital intelligence platform that gives brands visibility into web and app traffic, competitor benchmarking and market trends, helping D2C teams make sharper decisions on channel strategy and growth.
Juspay: A payments infrastructure company that powers checkout and payment orchestration for some of India’s largest digital platforms, helping brands improve payment success rates and reduce transaction drop-offs.
Frameo.ai: Part of the Dashverse ecosystem, Frameo.ai is an AI-native video creation platform that turns story prompts into short, cinematic videos, designed to power high-velocity, low-cost content production for brands and creators.
Cashfree Payments: A payments and banking-as-a-service platform offering payment gateway, payouts and API banking solutions that help D2C and ecommerce businesses collect and disburse payments efficiently.
Shopflo: A checkout optimisation platform for D2C brands, offering one-click checkout, address autofill, discounting and RTO tools that have driven reported conversion gains of 15–20% for its merchants.
Whilter.AI: A platform to run paid acquisition, customer conversations, and personalised retention, instead of separate agencies and tools, operated by AI agents that know a brand.
Nuvr: A full-stack, tech-enabled ecommerce growth accelerator that helps consumer brands scale rapidly across ecommerce, quick commerce and D2C platforms, combining brand strategy, performance marketing and channel management.
Truecaller Business: Best known for caller ID and spam protection, Truecaller also offers business messaging and verification solutions that help D2C brands build trust and improve customer engagement via calls and messages.
Primarc Pecan: An end-to-end ecommerce business solutions provider, helping brands scale marketplace operations across platforms like Amazon, Flipkart and Myntra, backed by a pan-India warehousing and fulfilment network.
StoreSignal: It builds AI agents for ecommerce, Sales, Shopping, and Support that handle everything from product recommendations and upsells to order status queries and returns, helping brands lift conversion rate and average order value while cutting support ticket volumes.
Rootle: A KPI-first Voice AI platform for enterprise customer engagement, Rootle helps D2C and quick commerce brands resolve order, exchange and refund queries in more than 20 Indian languages directly through their existing support and telephony stack.
Importerr: The B2B global sourcing and supply platform offers access to 100 Mn+ products from verified suppliers along with procurement and fulfilment tools for D2C brands, retailers and online sellers.
We would also like to thank our giveaway partners: Fix My Curl, O3+, Ningen, DailyObjects, Beanly Coffee, Antinorm, 4700 BC, Arata, Troovy, Blue Tea, Conscious Chemist, Moxie, Bakers Dozen, Phirki Zero, Papa Nata, Nurasoi’s Vyndo and BRB Chips.

The company ​said it plans to offer over 27 ​million eligible Saudi citizens and residents free ⁠access to its Adobe Firefly Standard subscription ​tier, plus Adobe Express Premium features, including a ​new image generation model "tuned to Saudi culture." Its commitment is valued at more than $4 billion.
The image model is jointly ​developed by Adobe and Humain, backed by ​Saudi's sovereign wealth fund, and will allow users to ‌create "culturally ⁠aligned" images using Arabic-language prompts.
The free access will start rolling out by the end of 2026, Adobe said.
The companies had announced their partnership in ​November, aiming ​to boost ⁠Humain's development of tools for generating content in Arabic and for ​the broader Middle East region.
For Adobe, the ​expanded ⁠partnership is expected to aid user growth for its AI products and tools, crucial for driving ⁠growth ​in a crowded design software ​industry where smaller firms have been gaining share rapidly.

items.author: MA Mir
items.content:
Political and religious parties, along with people from different walks of life, took to the streets in Sudhnoti on Monday, some 155 Kilometres away from the capital city of Azad Jammu and Kashmir. The peace march in Palandri called for an end to unrest, violence and instability in AJK.
The march was organised by the Awami Ittehad Forum Sudhnoti and brought together representatives and workers of the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz, Pakistan Peoples Party, Muslim Conference, Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam, Jammu and Kashmir Peoples Party, Istehkam-e-Pakistan Party and Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf, besides traders, lawyers, civil society activists, transporters, students, ex-servicemen and other citizens.
The rally began from Kotli Chowk and passed through various parts of the city before culminating at Kachehri Chowk, where a public gathering was held. Participants raised slogans including “This land is ours, we are its guardians”, “No to unrest in AJK ”, “No to violence”, “No to instability”, “Kashmir and Pakistan are one” and “What do we want? Peace.”
Speakers from political and religious parties and representatives of different sections of society expressed their resolve to promote peace, stability and protection of public rights in the region.
In a joint declaration issued at the conclusion of the march, participants congratulated the government of Pakistan and the armed forces for playing a role as an intermediary for global peace. They also rejected attempts to portray the ongoing rights movement in Azad Kashmir as an anti-state narrative.
The declaration said the “everlasting bond” between AJK and Pakistan could not be weakened, adding that a strong and stable Pakistan was essential for the success of the Kashmir freedom movement. It described Azad Kashmir as Pakistan’s “defensive bulwark” and called for preventing the spread of unrest in the region.
The participants demanded that immediate elections be held in the seven constituencies of Rawalakot and Sudhnoti. They also called for uninterrupted transportation of food and other essential commodities from Pakistan to AJK.
The declaration demanded an immediate end to blockades and restrictions at entry points in AJK and Pakistan, saying such measures were causing hardships for the people and affecting travel and the movement of essential goods.
The participants also called on the AJK government to restore travel and educational facilities, particularly in Sudhnoti and Rawalakot, and demanded the immediate restoration of internet services across the region.
They urged authorities to simplify and expedite the issuance of documents required by people travelling abroad and called for the provision of wheat to flour mills in Azad Kashmir to ensure an uninterrupted supply of flour.
The peace march participants also expressed concern over reports regarding the possible relocation of educational and administrative institutions from Rawalakot. They urged the authorities to refrain from steps that could create a sense of deprivation among the people, stressing that the sacrifices rendered by the people of the region for the Kashmir freedom movement and the cause of Pakistan should not be overlooked.
The participants further demanded uninterrupted supplies of petrol and called for the immediate removal of all obstacles affecting the provision of essential commodities, transport facilities and communication services to the people.

items.author: M A Mir
items.content:
Azad Jammu and Kashmir AJK Prime Minister Iftikhar Gilani has fulfilled his first promise to restore internet services in AJK, bringing relief to thousands of residents, students, freelancers and business owners who welcomed the move after months of disruption.
The AJK government has ordered the restoration of internet services in eight districts, with full services resumed in four districts while broadband and Wi-Fi connectivity will be available only to educational institutions in four others.
According to a notification issued by the AJK Home Department on the directions of PM Gilani, internet services will remain completely suspended in Poonch division’s two districts, Sudhnoti and Rawalakot.
In Muzaffarabad, Jhelum Valley, Bagh and Kotli, the broadband and Wi-Fi internet services will be restored only for educational institutions, including schools, colleges and universities.
Meanwhile, full internet services have been ordered restored in Mirpur, Bhimber, Haveli and Neelum Valley. Complete internet connectivity has also been restored in Leepa Valley, according to the notification.
Gilani had announced the restoration of internet services during his first media talk at Central Press Club two days ago.
The AJK people and freelancers welcomed the partial restoration, saying the move would help revive business and professional activities that had been badly affected by the prolonged suspension.
Internet services were initially suspended in Rawalakot on June 5 following restrictions imposed after the proscribed Joint Awami Action Committee JAAC called for a long march and sit-in. The services were partially restored after a prolonged 48-day suspension.
However, following a strike and clashes in the capital city of AJK’s commercial nerve, Lower Plate, internet services were suspended again on July 25, just two days after their restoration.
Officials said the restoration process would be completed in phases, adding that mobile internet services would also be restored in a subsequent phase.
The prolonged suspension severely affected business activities and government operations, while thousands of residents remained deprived of internet access. Traders dependent on digital payments suffered financial losses, while students, freelancers, government employees and other professionals faced difficulties in carrying out their routine activities.
The AJK residents and freelancers also urged the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority PTA, Special Communication Organisation and other internet service providers to waive charges for the days during which internet services remained unavailable across AJK.
They argued that consumers had paid for services that were not available during the suspension period, while businesses and professional activities were also severely disrupted.

items.author: Reuters
items.content:
Lionel Messi brought down the curtain on his extraordinary international career on Monday, announcing his retirement soon after inspiring Argentina to within one victory of a second successive World ​Cup triumph.
At 39, two decades after first appearing on football’s biggest stage, Messi walked away having long since repaired a complicated relationship with his country that once threatened ‌to define his career.
The record eight-times Ballon d’Or winner leaves as a World Cup winner and twice Copa America champion, the man who stepped out of Diego Maradona’s immense shadow to create an Argentine legacy entirely his own.
Defeat by Spain in this year's World Cup final denied Messi the perfect farewell and the chance to become a world champion for a second time. But after a career that transformed Barcelona, Argentina and the modern game itself, there was precious little ​left to prove.
Four years earlier in Qatar, he lifted the trophy he had pursued throughout his career, scoring seven goals in the tournament and twice in the final against France ​before Argentina prevailed on penalties.
It was the crowning moment of a remarkable career, and also the culmination of one of football’s most compelling stories ⁠of perseverance.
For all his success at Barcelona, where his brilliance brought him every major individual and collective honour available, Messi’s relationship with the Argentina shirt was for years defined as much by what ​he had not won as by what he had achieved.
He reached the 2014 World Cup final in Brazil only for Argentina to lose to Germany in extra time, before successive Copa America final ​defeats in 2015 and 2016 deepened the sense that international glory might elude him.
Devastated Messi
After the second of those defeats, against Chile on penalties, a devastated Messi briefly walked away.
"The national team is over for me," he said.
It was not.
Messi returned and, gradually, the story changed.
Read More: Fact box: A look at former Argentina forward Lionel Messi's career
Under Lionel Scaloni, Argentina built a team around their captain without becoming entirely dependent on him, surrounding their ageing number 10 with the energy, aggression and collective commitment that allowed ​his genius to flourish.
Argentina's Lionel Messi during the match against Spain on July 19. PHOTO: REUTERS
The breakthrough came at the 2021 Copa America, when Argentina beat Brazil at the Maracana to give Messi his first major senior international trophy.
The World Cup followed 18 months later.
Messi ​was magnificent in Qatar, producing goals, assists and moments of inspiration as Argentina recovered from a shock opening defeat by Saudi Arabia to reach the final.
He scored twice against France before converting his penalty in the ‌shootout, finally ⁠lifting the trophy that had become the missing piece in his claim to stand alongside, or above, the greatest players in the sport.
For Argentina, the triumph also completed Messi’s transformation.
Shy teenager
The shy teenager who had left Rosario for Barcelona at 13, and was sometimes portrayed at home as more Catalan than Argentine, had become the unquestioned leader of the national team.
The tears and frustration of earlier failures gave way to songs, murals and celebrations. The comparisons with Maradona did not disappear, but they no longer carried the same accusatory weight.
Messi had become Argentina’s Messi.
He could have stopped then.
Instead, he played on, ​moving from Paris St Germain to Inter Miami ​and helping Argentina retain the Copa America ⁠in 2024 before one last tilt at the World Cup.
By 2026, the explosive acceleration that had once left defenders helpless had inevitably faded but Messi adapted.
He walked more, waited more and chose his moments, conserving his energy while younger legs worked around him. Yet the essential qualities remained: the awareness of ​space, the weight of a pass and the capacity to alter a match with a single touch.
Argentina, meanwhile, had changed with him.
Battle-hardened team
The ​team who reached the July ⁠19 final were no longer merely a collection of players looking to Messi for salvation. It was an experienced, battle-hardened side accustomed to winning and shaped by years of playing alongside their captain.
That evolution allowed Messi to extend his international career far beyond what once appeared possible and to leave the game on his own terms.
His numbers place him among the giants of international football, but statistics alone did not ⁠tell the ​story of his journey from expectation to rejection, then heartbreak to adoration.
For years, every defeat was presented as evidence of ​what separated him from Maradona. By the end, the argument had become largely irrelevant.
One carried Argentina to the World Cup in 1986. The other, after years of trying, did so in 2022 and returned four years later to take his ​country to within a hair's breadth of another title.
He walks away from his national team as a man who played a defining role in Argentina's football history.

items.author: Anne Florentyna
items.content:
Walmart-owned fintech major PhonePe has launched UPI payments for feature phones, mobile phones that handle basic calling and text messaging, enabling them to make digital transactions without requiring an internet connection.
With the launch, PhonePe claimed to have become the first major third-party application provider (TPAP) to extend UPI payments to feature phone users at scale.
The company said that its new service, dubbed PhonePe UPI 123Pay, will bring UPI capabilities to more than 20 Cr feature phone users in the country.
The service will come pre-installed on feature phones manufactured by Nokia, HMD, Lava International and Itel Mobile, which is owned by Transsion Holdings. PhonePe said it plans to add more handset partners in the coming months.
PhonePe UPI 123Pay uses an SMS-based architecture, processing transactions in areas with limited 2G connectivity. Users will be able to make P2P (peer-to-peer) transfers using mobile numbers or UPI IDs and pay merchants through UPI IDs and QR codes on camera-enabled devices.
To help users activate the service, PhonePe has also launched a voice-first, AI-powered helpline that offers assistance in English and 12 Indian languages. Users can register for the service directly on compatible feature phones by selecting their bank, entering the last six digits and expiry date of their debit card, and setting a UPI PIN.
“Bringing UPI to feature phones through PhonePe UPI 123Pay extends the benefits of digital payments beyond smartphones to every corner of the country,” said Sameer Nigam, founder and CEO of PhonePe.
For context, the RBI announced the introduction of UPI123Pay, the offline version of UPI in 2022. UPI123Pay works primarily on IVR technology, and the process is automated in terms of carrying out transactions.
To foray into this space, PhonePe had acquired Gupshup’s proprietary technology GSPay in June 2025. Back then, it had revealed plans to customise the freshly bought GSPay IP to launch its own UPI-based payment solution for feature phones.
The launch comes as digital payment companies look to expand UPI adoption beyond smartphone users, particularly in rural and semi-urban parts of the country where smartphone penetration and reliable internet connectivity remain inconsistent.
Meanwhile, UPI transaction volume rose 4% to 23.66 Bn in July from 22.72 Bn in June, as per data released by the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI), of which PhonePe and Google Pay continue to dominate the UPI ecosystem. PhonePe processed the highest 1,085.8 Cr transactions worth ₹14.4 Lakh Cr during the month.
PhonePe filed the updated draft red herring prospectus (UDRHP) with SEBI for its IPO in January this year. However, it paused its public listing plans in the months that followed, stating volatility in the global equity markets.
The fintech major’s net loss widened by 62% in FY26 to ₹2,792 Cr from ₹1,727.4 Cr reported in the previous fiscal year. Operating revenue rose 11.5% to ₹7,920.5 Cr in the year under review from ₹7,105 Cr in FY25.

items.author: Usama Anjum
items.content:
Copyright protected content copied from PhoneWorld website.
A Senate committee has recommended an immediate reduction in taxes imposed on imported mobile phones while directing customs authorities to develop a mechanism for determining their valuation and taxation.
The recommendation was made during a meeting of the Senate Standing Committee on Cabinet Secretariat, chaired by Senator Rana Mahmood-ul-Hassan, where the committee discussed the pricing and taxation of imported mobile phones.
Officials of the Pakistan Telecommunication Authority (PTA) told the committee that customs authorities would need to establish a proper mechanism for determining the prices of imported mobile phones.
The committee subsequently directed customs officials to devise a mechanism for the taxation of imported mobile phones and recommended an immediate reduction in the taxes imposed on them.
Senator Abdul Qadir questioned the need for taxing mobile phones altogether, saying the government would have to consider whether taxes should be imposed on mobile phones in the first place.
Officials of the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR), however, told the committee that the authority to impose or abolish taxes rests with Parliament.
The committee sought reports from the FBR and the National Tariff Commission on the existing taxation structure applicable to mobile phones.
During the meeting, Senator Dilawar Khan criticized the country’s policymaking, saying that Pakistan’s policies were not being formulated with a long-term perspective.
PTA officials informed the committee that 35 companies are currently manufacturing smartphones in Pakistan, highlighting the growing presence of local mobile phone production.
Senator Sadia Abbasi called for greater facilitation of businesses and consumers, arguing that the government should focus on facilitating economic activity rather than exploiting businesses and citizens through excessive taxation.
“Instead of exploitation, businesses should be facilitated,” she said, adding that government revenue measures were creating difficulties for the public.
The meeting also touched upon the country’s growing digital payments ecosystem. Cabinet Secretary Kamran Ali Afzal said digital payments were bringing about a transformation in Pakistan’s payments system.
The cabinet secretary also opposed the imposition of sales tax on mobile phones.
The committee’s recommendations are expected to put the existing taxation and valuation mechanism for imported mobile phones under renewed scrutiny, with the FBR and National Tariff Commission now required to submit reports on the matter.

PTA Supports Lower Mobile Taxes to Improve Smartphone Affordability

items.content:
Argentina's Lionel Messi announced his retirement from international football on Monday. Following are facts about Messi's playing career.
Barcelona
Messi joined Barcelona at 13 years old in 2000 and shone in the youth ranks before making his senior debut at 16 in a friendly against Porto in 2003.
He made his La Liga debut in October 2004 and scored his ​first league goal the following May in a match against Albacete.
From 2004 to 2021, he won 10 La Liga titles, seven Spanish Cups, seven Spanish ‌Super Cups, four Champions Leagues, three UEFA Super Cups and three FIFA Club World Cups.
Messi also played a key role as Barca claimed six trophies in the calendar year of 2009 and produced scintillating performances in their treble-winning 2014-15 season.
Argentina's Lionel Messi celebrates scoring his first goal in FIFA CUP on July19.REUTERS
As another milestone of his career, he completed 2012 with 91 goals in all competitions, a record for a calendar year, and smashed La Liga's scoring record for one season in 2011-12 with 50 goals.
After Barcelona went trophyless in 2019-20, the ​club captain expressed his desire to leave but decided to fulfill his contract until 2021.
Messi wanted to stay with Barca but the club said they could not re-sign ​him due to economic and structural obstacles.
Read : Messi announces retirement from Argentina national team
He left Barcelona in August 2021 as their all-time top scorer.
Paris St German
Lionel Messi joined PSG in August 2021.
he won a Ligue 1 title in his debut season but managed just 11 goals in all competitions.
Also won the 2022 Trophee des Champions before claiming another Ligue 1 title in 2022-23.
Inter Miami
Messi Joined Major League Soccer's Inter Miami in July 2023 and captained them to a Leagues Cup title, their first-ever trophy.
He also guided Miami to the 2024 Supporters' Shield award.
He became the fastest ​player in MLS history to reach 40 league goals in 2025 and led Miami to their first league championship.
Messi Surpassed Hungarian Ferenc Puskas to become the all-time leader in career assists across all competitions in 2025.
Argentina
He Led Argentina to the 2005 World Youth Championship title, scoring two penalties in a 2-1 victory over Nigeria.
Messi also made his senior debut as a substitute in a friendly against Hungary in August 2005 but was sent off after ​less than a minute for elbowing an opponent who pulled his shirt.
He played only a bit-part role at the 2006 World Cup. Argentina were knocked out in the quarter-finals.
Messi also led Argentina ​to the gold medal at the 2008 Beijing Olympic Games.
However, he failed to score at the 2010 World Cup. Argentina exited in the quarter-finals.
He also captained Argentina to the 2014 World Cup final, where they lost 1-0 ‌to Germany. ⁠Messi, who scored four goals at the finals, won the Golden Ball as the tournament's best player.
Lionel Messi played in his second Copa America final for Argentina in 2015, which they lost on penalties to Chile.
As a feather in his cap, he scored a hat trick in 18 minutes after coming off the bench in Argentina's 5-0 win over Panama in the 2016 Centenary Copa America.
He set a record of 55 goals for Argentina when he scored in the 4-0 win over the U.S. in the semi-finals.
He was on the losing side after a penalty shootout defeat by Chile in the centenary final and said ​he was retiring from internationals.
Messi returned to the ​national team in August 2016 and helped ⁠secure their spot in the 2018 World Cup with a hat-trick against Ecuador in the last game of the qualifiers.
He recorded one goal and two assists at the 2018 World Cup as Argentina were knocked out in the round of 16.
He won the 2021 Copa America to end ​the nation's 28-year trophy drought and was named the player of the tournament, contributing to nine of Argentina's 12 goals.
Lionel Messi also guided Argentina to ​another victory over Italy ⁠at the 2022 Finalissima.
At the 2022 World Cup, Messi scored twice in the final to help beat France as Argentina lifted their first World Cup in 36 years. Became the first player to win the Golden Ball twice after recording seven goals and three assists.
The legend reached 100 international goals in 2023.
He won the Copa America in 2024 and later that year became the all-time top assist-provider in ⁠men's international ​soccer.
He also netted twice against Austria at the 2026 World Cup to become the tournament's all-time leading scorer with 18 ​goals. Added three more for a total of 21 but was surpassed by France's Kylian Mbappe.
He produced eight goals and four assists to guide Argentina to the final, where they lost 1-0 in extra time to Spain.
Lionel Messi became the second ​player to feature in three World Cup finals and the oldest outfield player in the global final.

items.author: Shrishti Bisht
items.content:
The Centre has notified the ₹1.28 Lakh Cr Semicon 2.0 scheme to accelerate the development of India’s semiconductor design and manufacturing ecosystem and strengthen domestic capabilities across the chip value chain.
The notification comes more than a month after the Union Cabinet approved the second phase of the India Semiconductor Mission with an exact outlay of ₹1,27,500 Cr. Semicon 2.0 was first announced by finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman in the Union Budget for FY27.
“Semicon 2.0 provides fiscal support to various verticals across the complete value chain of the semiconductor industry, ranging from chip design, fabrication and packaging to various segments of the semiconductor ecosystem,” the notification said.
The scheme has been divided into six pillars covering semiconductor design, machines and materials, fabs, assembly and packaging, R&D, and talent development. These pillars encompass 10 categories of support.
The scheme aims to build a strong, trusted and self-reliant semiconductor ecosystem in India by supporting the development and use of technologies for critical and strategic infrastructure.
Under the design component, the government will support the development of semiconductor IP cores, chips, system-on-chips (SoCs) and modules for electronic products based on national priorities and strategic needs.
The government also plans to develop standard IP building blocks for areas such as computing, memory, radio frequency (RF), power, networking and sensors, the notification said.
Support Across Semiconductor Value Chain
Semicon 2.0 extends government support beyond chip fabrication to the infrastructure and capabilities needed to build a domestic semiconductor ecosystem.
The scheme provides support for semiconductor equipment and materials, wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, marking and packaging (ATMP), outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT), as well as semiconductor research and development and talent development.
For semiconductor design, eligible startups and MSMEs can receive seed funding of up to ₹15 Cr. The scheme also provides equity co-investment support for eligible companies that have raised funding from VC or PE investors.
The government will also provide deployment-linked incentives for eligible semiconductor IPs, chips and SoCs launched for the first time after the scheme’s announcement.
Semicon 2.0 also provides fiscal support for setting up semiconductor fabs and advanced packaging facilities, alongside manufacturing infrastructure for semiconductor equipment and materials.
Silicon wafer fabs with a minimum capital investment of ₹20,000 Cr will be eligible for government support equivalent to 40% of eligible capital expenditure. Compound semiconductor, photonics, sensor and discrete semiconductor fabs will also receive fiscal support under the scheme.
Advanced semiconductor packaging projects, including 2.5D and 3D packaging, wafer-level chip-scale packaging and heterogeneous integration, will also qualify for government support.
The scheme further provides support for R&D facilities focused on semiconductor equipment, semiconductor-grade raw materials, and testing and characterisation infrastructure.
Semicon 2.0 To Build Domestic Chip Capabilities
The government is also looking to strengthen India’s semiconductor R&D, design capabilities and talent pool under Semicon 2.0.
The scheme will support research in advanced technologies such as CMOS fabrication, silicon photonics, display fabrication and chiplets, while also providing access to advanced design tools, fabrication services and training infrastructure.
Speaking at a press conference after the scheme was notified, IT minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said India aims to develop 1 Lakh additional semiconductor engineers under the programme, citing an expected global shortage of about 1 Mn workers by 2032.
“Now, we have set up a target of developing 1 Lakh more engineers,” Vaishnaw said.
India has already trained 85,000 semiconductor engineers, achieving its 10-year target in four years.
“People should feel dependent on India. People should become dependent on our country, on our industry, on our production, on our design,” Vaishnaw said.
Semiconductor design programmes have also been expanded to 355 universities, including those in Tier II and III cities. Students have so far designed 255 chips, the minister said.
The programme has identified six key semiconductor categories — compute, memory, radio frequency (RF), power, networking and sensors — with around 100 chips prioritised for development. These chips are expected to cater to sectors such as aviation, transportation, consumer electronics and strategic industries.
The notification builds on the first phase of the India Semiconductor Mission, under which the Centre approved 12 manufacturing projects across six states. The push comes as major economies ramp up support for their semiconductor industries.
According to data presented by the government, the US has announced a support of $52.7 Bn under the CHIPS and Science Act, while the European Union has earmarked $49 Bn under the EU CHIPS Act 1.0 and is discussing a further $140 Bn proposal under CHIPS Act 2.0.
Japan has announced a $25.7 Bn Semiconductor Strategy, South Korea has committed $23.3 Bn under its Semiconductor Ecosystem Support Package, and Singapore has announced $27.5 Bn under its RIE2030 Strategy.
China has committed $47.5 Bn in the third round of its “Big Fund”, taking its cumulative semiconductor fund support to more than $150 Bn since 2014. Taiwan has announced $9.3 Bn under its Chip-based Industrial Innovation Program.
The post Centre Notifies ₹1.28 Lakh Cr Semicon 2.0, Targets 1 Lakh More Chip Engineers appeared first on Inc42 Media.
