items.author: Team Inc42
items.content:
Can ESDS Ace The IPO Test?
ESDS Software Solution’s public issue is all set to open for subscription later today. The data centre company’s fresh issue-only IPO will look to bring the much needed capital to add GPUs and pursue sovereign cloud ambitions. But with competition rising, will ESDS’ IPO find takers?
ESDS’s IPO Stack: The data centre company’s public issue consists entirely of a fresh issue of shares worth ₹720 Cr, with no offer for sale. Ahead of the IPO, ESDS yesterday raised ₹216 Cr from anchor investors such as Motilal Oswal, Quant MF, JM Financial MF and Samco. Notably, domestic mutual funds cornered 82% of the total anchor allotment.
The Number Game: ESDS Software Solution delivered a healthy FY26, driven by a surge in profitability and substantial operational leverage across its core cloud, SaaS and managed services segments.
Revenue from operations grew around 31% YoY to ₹472 Cr
Net profit zoomed 117% YoY to ₹120.8 Cr
EBITDA margin expanded to 49.6%
Expenses rose 6.5% YoY to ₹313.2 Cr
Enterprise-Grade Scale: As per its RHP, ESDS currently serves over 2,500 clients, including over 170 banking entities and 100 government organisations. This deep penetration in regulated sectors via community clouds yields recurring revenues and sticky client relationships. What also works for the company is its indigenous Swaraj Cloud platform, which reins in expensive third-party software licensing costs and unlocks long-term operating leverage.
Caught In Pricing War: Despite the demand, escalating hardware prices mean that the proceeds from the IPO will buy significantly fewer GPU and servers than ESDS initially projected. This could constrain planned capacity expansion. In addition, the company also faces intense competition from global hyperscalers and domestic conglomerates expanding into India’s data center market.
Additionally, high customer concentration, lingering government payment cycles and severe hypothecation of current assets also present ongoing working capital risks. With much on its plate, can ESDS deliver a bumper IPO? Let’s find out…
From The Editor’s Desk
Even Axes 350 Jobs
The healthtech startup has laid off around 350 employees, or nearly 30% of its total workforce. The retrenchments, which impacted multiple teams, aimed to slash costs, improve efficiency and route capital to the startup’s new business model.
The layoffs come as Even Healthcare phases down its insurance business to pivot to a hospital-led healthcare model. It launched its first multispeciality hospital in Bengaluru last year and has been expanding its footprint in the city.
Founded in 2020, Even Healthcare operates a membership-based healthcare model that offers primary care, diagnostics and hospital services. The startup also offers health insurance plans covering hospitalisation. It has raised $90 Mn to date.
InstaAstro Bags $12 Mn
The online astrology platform has raised about ₹115 Cr in its Series A round led by Singularity AMC and Artha Venture Fund to expand its footprint, strengthen its pooja seva offerings, scaling AI-led development and grow its product business.
Founded in 2021, InstaAstro connects users with astrologers and tarot card readers. It also offers pooja seva, astrology courses, accessories and gemstones. It claims to have 12 Mn registered users and more than 5,000 verified experts across 183 countries.
The round comes as India’s online faith commerce ecosystem is projected to become a $1.8 Bn opportunity by 2030. As a result, the number of spiritual tech startups in the country has grown to over 1,400.
Temple Acquires Longevous
Ahead of the launch of its first product, the Deepinder Goyal-led wearable startup has acquired the London-based longevity medicine practice for an undisclosed sum. As part of the deal, Longevous founders Robert Mohr and Avi Roy will join Temple.
While Mohr will join Temple as its chief medical officer and will oversee the clinical rigour of the startup’s experiments and health-related claims, Roy will take over as the startup’s head of science.
The acquisition comes days after Goyal unveiled the latest design of Temple’s wearable. He also said pre-orders for a limited-edition version will open soon, with shipments expected by the end of 2026.
Raphe mPhibr’s Quiet Ascent
Siblings Vivek and Vikash Mishra caught the attention of Indian government agencies when they built an octocopter during their university break in the US and posted it online. This paved the way for them to pursue indigenous drone R&D.
After years of low-profile work, the Noida-based startup brought its technology into the public view after its drones were deployed during Operation Sindoor in 2025. Since then, Raphe mPhibr has raised $100 Mn and is currently valued at $900 Mn.
Today, it designs and makes a host of UAVs for surveillance, logistics and other defence use cases. It also employs around 1,000 people, operates a 7 Lakh sq ft manufacturing campus and supplies more than 300 logistics drones to the Indian Army.
PRISM’s FY26 Profit Soars
The IPO-bound hospitality giant’s net profit soared 306% YoY to ₹994.2 Cr in FY26 on the back of a tax gain of ₹595.3 Cr, AI-led efficiencies and operating revenue zooming nearly 50% YoY to ₹9,358 Cr in the fiscal under review.
Meanwhile, EBITDA more than doubled YoY to ₹2,594 Cr in FY26, while its gross booking value zoomed 88.5% YoY to ₹30,683 Cr. Hotel storefronts, excluding G6, grew to 22,769 during the year and home storefronts stood at 1.3 Lakh.
The financials come as PRISM gears up to list on the bourses. The OYO parent has filed its updated DRHP with SEBI for a public issue, which will consist solely of a fresh issue of shares up to ₹6,650 Cr and no OFS.
Inc42 Markets
Inc42 Startup Spotlight
How SenseLive Is Making Factories Smarter
Many Indian factories still rely on manual monitoring and disconnected systems. This leaves them blind to energy waste, machine faults and downtime until it is too late. SenseLive is tackling this gap with its end-to-end industrial IoT platform.
Industrial Intelligence: Founded in 2022, SenseLive builds industrial IoT hardware, gateways and sensors paired with a cloud analytics layer. Its platform provides real-time visibility into energy consumption, machine health and production performance, helping factories move from reactive maintenance to predictive strategies.
The Predictive Care: SenseLive’s solutions span energy management, machine and condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. The startup’s edge devices, such as its X9000 4G gateway, collect data from controllers and sensors, perform local processing and transmit insights to the cloud for dashboards, alerts and optimisation.
The Industry 4.0 Pitch: The startup positions itself as a bridge for factories transitioning to Industry 4.0. It supports remote diagnostics, factory digitalisation and OEE monitoring. Incubated at IIT Indore, SenseLive also exports its hardware to international markets. Going forward, it plans to bolster product development and scale deployments.
With the global industrial IoT market projected to exceed $286 Bn by 2029, can SenseLive make fragmented factory floors intelligent and energy-efficient?

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
It was five years on Tuesday since I wrote a tribute to the Sultan of Sokoto, Muhammadu Sa’ad Abubakar III, who was 65 at the time. Our paths first crossed after he was named Sultan following the tragic death of his brother, Muhammadu Maccido, in the 2006 ADC air crash in which 93 persons were killed. Apart from his brother, Brigadier Abubakar (as he then was) also lost his nephew, Senator Badamasi Maccido, in that crash. It seemed that tragedy had not only struck without notice, but it had also come with its own chair and shelter. On Monday, August 24, Sultan Abubakar III turned 70. He’ll mark his 20th year on the throne on November 2. It’s remarkable what the last five years of his reign have revealed, for himself, the Sultanate, and the country. Two days after his 65th birthday in 2021, for example, the Sultan publicly said that things were not getting better and that religious leaders had a duty to tell the government so.
Shooting straight
He didn’t stop there. He said anyone who incited violence, whether religious leaders, traditional rulers or politicians, should face the law. And he said this at a time when Plateau State was in the middle of a dangerous cycle of ethnic violence, with serious threats of reprisal. He’s not one to mince his words. When mad men under the franchise of Boko Haram or their affiliates maim, murder, rape and destroy in the name of Allah, claiming that if they die, a bevy of brides awaits them in Paradise, some religious leaders may choose silence. Not Sultan Abubakar III. He tells such mad men in plain language, which he repeated to my hearing some time ago, that “They’ll go straight to hell!” No one can kill in Allah’s name and expect shelter in Paradise. The Arabic version of Surah Al-Ma’idah 5: 78-79, “L? yatan?hawna ‘an munkarin fa’al?hu,” expressly calls out those who do not forbid, restrain or admonish one another concerning the wrongdoing they committed.
Inter-faith champion
One year after his 65th birthday, his credentials as an interfaith leader were tested when Deborah Samuel, a student of the Shehu Shagari College of Education, Sokoto, was murdered over allegations of blasphemy. The Sultanate Council condemned the killing and demanded that the suspects face the law. That was extraordinary, even if the civil authorities under Governor Waziri Tambuwal ignored the advice, and a former Vice President, Atiku Abubakar, after condemning the act in a tweet, quickly deleted it. Abubakar III has done more for inter-faith unity and understanding than any Muslim spiritual leader I’ve known for a long, long time. In his capacity as co-chairman of the Nigeria Inter-Religious Council, he has worked tirelessly, drawing on his extensive network with other faith councils worldwide, to repair broken bonds and roll back religious intolerance and extremism.
Social crusader
Sultan Abubakar III is, if you like, a moderate social crusader, which is somewhat ironic, given that he is from Sokoto, often regarded as the bastion of conservatism. He has spoken out for education for the child – boy or girl – reminding fools and their enablers who despise education in the name of Islam that the Caliphate was founded on education and enlightenment. And he’s right. Much of the documented history of the Caliphate owes a lot to Nana Asmau, Sultan Mohammed Bello’s younger half-sister, who spoke four languages, according to the book by Fola Fagbule and Feyi Fawehinmi, entitled Formations: The Making of Nigeria from Jihad to Amalgamation. Sultan Abubakar has spoken about the link between rising insecurity, poverty, hunger, and social exclusion, saying on one occasion that “hunger knows no religion,” challenging the government to tackle rising inflation and the high cost of living and to stop making excuses. When the Buhari government was sleepwalking on court orders, including an order to release publisher and activist Omoyele Sowore from detention, the Sultan publicly said that disobedience to court orders was “a recipe for chaos and disaster.” And he said so at the meeting of the inter-religious council in Abuja, Buhari’s playground at the time.
Shuttle diplomacy
The 2023 coup in Niger was a tricky moment for President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s government, which had only just been sworn in. When the hardline posture of Nigeria and ECOWAS failed, the Nigerian government sent a delegation led by General Abdulsalami Abubakar and also comprising the Sultan to explore channels where presidents and diplomats had hit a brick wall. It was a reminder that soft power can sometimes find a way where force has exhausted itself. Although Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso went ahead to form the so-called Alliance of Sahel States (AES), the mediation by the General Abubakar-led committee averted the potential escalation of the crisis in the subregion.
Many rivers to cross
Yet one of the Sultan’s regrets as he turns 70 may well be the dangerous rise of insurgency in Nigeria’s Northwest. Borno (in the Northeast) remains the epicentre, but the deadly activities of Lakurawa indicate that Kebbi and Sokoto are emerging as jihadist fronts in the Northwest. What the Sultan was looking at from afar and warning against when he was 65 has arrived at the doorstep of the Caliphate, as a transnational Sahelian threat. Translation: his job as a moral compass and stabilising voice is not done. The world is not only listening, but also paying attention. The Sultan and his brother in the business of inter-faith engineering, Cardinal John Onaiyekan, were jointly nominated for the Nobel Peace Prize. The nomination was as good as winning, because it sent a clear message that the extraordinary work that both men are doing has not gone unnoticed – or unrewarded. Both had jointly shared the prize for the LEADERSHIP Persons of the Year 2012, proof that these prophets are worthy, at home and abroad.
Moment of trial
Yet, there have been moments of trial in the last few years. Two years ago, the future of the Sultanate seemed to be tottering. Governor Ahmed Aliyu proposed changes to the Sokoto Local Government and Chieftancy Law that could have curtailed the Sultanate Council’s authority to appoint district and village heads. Under the proposed changes, now suspended, the council could only recommend candidates, not appoint them. Whatever the letter of the law intended, coming five years after the Kano State government weakened the powers of Emir Muhammadu Sanusi, it was an affront to another important traditional institution in the North. The Sokoto State government wanted to bring the Sultanate to its knees, exposing the fundamental contradiction of modern Nigerian traditional institutions: a man could be the spiritual leader of tens of millions, internationally recognised and sought after by presidents, yet his stool is subject to state laws at the governor’s pleasure.
Soldier and gentleman
As the Sultan turns 70, I have struggled to figure out what might be behind his enigmatic path. He was a member of the 18th Regular Combatant Course of the Nigerian Defence Academy (the class of the former Chief of Army Staff, Lt. General Azubuike Ihejirika), and the first soldier to ascend the Sultanate. His extensive tour of duty in combatant and non-combatant positions, especially his deployment as defence adviser to Pakistan, with concurrent accreditation to Iran, Iraq, Afghanistan, Saudi Arabia, and the Gulf States, might also have shaped his worldview. To adapt Kipling’s words, at 70 and nearly 20 years on the throne, Sultan Muhammad Sa’ad Abukakar III has seen triumphs and setbacks and treated both impostors the same. Long, and well, may you live and reign!
•Ishiekwene is the Editor-In-Chief of LEADERSHIP and author of the book, Writing for Media and Monetising it.
The post Muhammadu Sa’ad Abubakar III: A Sultan for All Seasons, by Azu Ishiekwene appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
Travelling is good for the soul, a) especially if the place you are travelling AWAY from is a frustrating country like Nigeria. And b) especially if the places you are travelling TO are less stressful. Nigeria is deeply, deeply, deeply mired in corruption, spectacularly failing to rescue its teeming masses from hunger and being badly managed by leaders who are extremely disappointing, to put it politely. Nigeria, in a nutshell, has flatly refused to fulfil its potential! And I thank God that I am occasionally able to escape to less stressful, more ethical, more efficient and more civilized environments.
Don’t get me wrong. The relatively advanced nations I’m referring to – in Europe, the Americas, Asia, etc, – are not perfect by a long shot. But they are much more committed to progress than we are and much more committed to controlling corruption and much more committed to offering most of their citizens much better standards of living.
OK so I’ve been in the United States for nearly 2 months and arrived in London a couple of days ago. And these trips to better climes have massively boosted my sanity and physical wellbeing.
But every silver lining has a cloud attached to it. And I’m so sad I missed a great celebration of this newspaper’s 40th  anniversary.
A cross section of dignitaries at the Vanguard @ 40 book launch
I had already bought my airline tickets when the date was conveyed to me. And I’d have had to pay penalty fees I could ill afford if I changed my travel dates, so I regretfully watched both current and past Vanguard colleagues celebrating with our dear boss and mentor from afar. Our dear boss and mentor is, of course, the legendary Sam Amuka. Once a famous columnist nicknamed Sad Sam and skilled editor, he has gone from strength to strength as a publisher since he founded Vanguard in 1984 and is now the doyen of the Nigerian print media scene.
I started to work for him when I was in my late 20s and living in the UK, where I grew up. Uncle Sam gave me a column called Londonline that enabled me to connect with compatriots who shared my love of current affairs, feisty opinions and the written word. He basically enabled me to establish professional roots in the land of my ancestors; and I will always be grateful to him for this.
I am 66 now, so I am almost as old as Vanguard!…and just one of MANY journalists who have Uncle Sam to thank for their high profiles. And each and every one of us has a special relationship with him.
When I was kidnapped in Rivers State in 2015, Uncle Sam played a key role when my captors were demanding a large sum of money; and he even flew to Port Harcourt to see me when I was released. Informal, warm, kind-hearted, brilliant, original and somewhat eccentric, several other Vanguard staffers and alumni share my view that knowing him has been one of the greatest privileges of our lives.  
To commemorate Vanguard’s 40th  anniversary, a book titled The  Vanguard Chronology: 40 years of Nigeria’s Leading Tabloid  was launched a few days ago. It is 220 pages long and is full of contributions from members of the Vanguard family. One of the editors of the book, Eyobong Ita, quoted an African proverb to explain the reason for compiling it: “Until the Lion learns to write his own side of the story, every story will glorify the hunter, so the The Vanguard Chronology was written to ensure that a wrong story about the Vanguard is not told.” The Vanguard was, as one of the editors, Deba Uwadiae put it : “a place where you can get a job without knowing anybody.” That is Uncle Sam for you. Doggedly impartial, admirably meritocratic, refreshingly down to earth, no time for nonsensical flashiness, always wedded to substance, always ready to nurture talent.
DONU’S WORLD
I have a YouTube channel. It’s called DONU’S WORLD.
https://youtube.com/@donukogbara?si=bBm_IPdFZ_wUyKYq
NIGERIA UNFILTERED – spicy commentaries on Naija issues – appears every Wednesday, while DONU’S WEEK appears on Fridays and is international as well as local and covers a mish-mash of soft and tough issues around my personal life, my work and my worldview. Two days ago,
in this week’s Nigeria Unfiltered video, I wondered why Nigerian leaders are allergic to the true love they will earn from a grateful electorate if they do the right things.
Please check out my Donu’s World library (dating back to early 2024) on YouTube, plus the new videos I produce every week. I would love to hear your opinions and any constructive criticisms you may have to offer. And I will be very grateful if you “like”, subscribe and share!

Dolly Rebecca Parton-Dean taught the world that poverty is not a reproach. Not a DNA or a sin. In fact, that it can be a badge of honour worn with pride.
In her 1971 classic “Coat of Many Colours” she stitched a true story of poverty with the Biblical story of Joseph and presented humanity unforgettable lyrics. The “coat” was a biblical story of love, preference and anointment. But the Parton coat was parchment sewn with love and worn proudly by a child. items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
AGAIN, the matter of fuel subsidy has dominated national discourse in the last few days, with President Bola Tinubu, former vice-president and ADC presidential candidate, Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, NDC presidential candidate Mr Peter Obi and a host of others have had not a little to say about the issue.
The matter was reignited when Alhaji Atiku Abubakar said that if he should be elected, he would return subsidy on fuel energy. Expectedly, presidency officials descended on him, and in the exchanges that followed, harsh, near-uncivil words were used. The exchanges went as far as dredging up the matter of over $16 billion spent on the power sector during the Obasanjo administration. It just shows how deeply the issue of subsidy is affecting lives.
Beyond the brickbats however, what is clear is that nobody has interrogated Atiku Abubakar’s subsidy return plan, at least empirically. It is quite possible that the former vice-president is on a sympathy run, a vote-catching gambit to sway the voting populace to his side as January 2027 approaches. On the flip side, he may be altruistic; moved by the real and apparent suffering of Nigerians as runaway inflation makes nonsense of any amount held by anybody. The position taken by the president and his officials in defending subsidy removal is what it has always been — a rehash of previously spewed rhetoric about how the economy would have collapsed if it had not been done, and how the economy is on a skyward rebound, despite the fact that the people are simply suffering. Impressive GDP figures and positive ratings by Fitch and other agencies mean nothing if the average Nigerian still struggles to eat barely twice daily. Perhaps the easiest way to describe the situation is through the words of one Austin Okai, who, in a Facebook post said, inter alia, that “If your salary is not up to at least 300k in Abuja, the difference between you and Almajiri is just the plate.” The post, which stirred huge reaction online speaks only of Abuja residents. How many Nigerians earn N300k? And if you don’t earn that much, you’re just what he said — an almajiri. Truth is, many Nigerians are becoming almajirai; begging for urgent N2k from one friend to another. But I digress.
Back to the subsidy matter. I am of the belief that the issue has not been interrogated at all. A conscientious, people-centred interrogation of the subsidy issue will reveal that the political class ruling Nigeria at the moment, headed by Mr Bola Tinubu as President, simply decided to  sell Nigerians to the highest bidder, to say the least, in return for benefits accruing to them. The pricing template for imported petrol in place reveals this, and confounds the mind that same pricing template in place when imported petrol was the only option is still in use, months after Dangote Refinery began operations. From what we know, Dangote Refinery supplies no less than 80% of the petrol we burn daily., the remaining 20% made up by imported fuel. Why should the pricing template for just 20% be applied to 80%, which is domestically refined? 
With imported petrol, the following charges apply: These are 1. FOB cost — N434.32; 2. Freight cost— N86.48; 3. Insurance cost — N10.58; 4. Lightering cost — N23.45; 5. Jetty depot fees — N15.35; 6. Storage fees — N12.58; and 7. Financing costs — N34.67. Other charges are 8. Foreign exchange costs — N23.45; 9. NPA charges — N10.58; 10. NIMASA charges — N5.29; 11. Customs duties — N51.17; and 12. Other levies and charges — N50.00. Total is N757.87. Note that this template had been in place nearly12 year; inflation would have impacted it. Looking at these charges, some of them don’t apply to locally refined fuel. Cost of refining replaces Nos 1, 2, 3, for instance. NPA and NIMASA charges may also not apply, while foreign exchange costs should also not apply since refiners are buying crude in Naira. But this template is kept in use, perhaps to keep importers of fuel in business to the detriment of hapless Nigerian masses. In any case, if charges due NPA, NIMASA and Customs are waived, the cost will be reduced, and this will translate to subsidy, however little or large.
Beyond all of this, I have written earlier that when the US-Israel/Iran war broke out and caused an upsurge in global crude prices, about 60 countries have implemented no less than 200 different policies to reduce the impact on local economies. Here, we have been thrown to the scavenging dogs of international commerce. Nothing from our government. Even the much-hyped Presidential CNG Initiative has remained what it had been — hype, as CNG stations remain scarce. Given the state of the economy now, and what ordinary Nigerians are feeling, there is no need to deny the fact that the peoples of this country need a lifeline, and NOW. You may call it subsidy, or any other word from IMF/World Bank crafted jargon.
Beyond that, the economy needs to be reflated, and urgently too. Political brick-batting cannot deny the fact that Mr Bola Tinubu put the cart before the horse in the matter of subsidy removal. Not after his 2012 elaborate argument against President Goodluck Jonathan’s bid to remove subsidy. His removal of subsidy has worked only for the governors. Most of them now have far much more to spend but are hardly spending on what will benefit the people. What is worse, they are playing kalokalo with local government funds despite a Supreme Court judgement.Clearly there won’t be a return to subsidy under Tinubu. Nevertheless, we can’t take away the fact that we all need lifelines out of this self-inflicted hardship. Abi? TGIF.

items.title: Osun guber as a primer to 2027 elections
items.summary:
The Osun State governorship election has offered Nigeria a preview of what the 2027 general elections could become—and what they must never become. It was preceded by an ugly cocktail of defections, political brinkmanship, institutional controversy and violence. Governor Ademola Adeleke’s hurried exit from the PDP, after failing to secure a route into the APC amid resistance from Tinubu’s supporters in Osun, and his eventual adoption of the Accord Party ticket, confirmed the opportunistic fluidity of Nigerian politics. items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
The Osun State governorship election has offered Nigeria a preview of what the 2027 general elections could become—and what they must never become. It was preceded by an ugly cocktail of defections, political brinkmanship, institutional controversy and violence. Governor Ademola Adeleke’s hurried exit from the PDP, after failing to secure a route into the APC amid resistance from Tinubu’s supporters in Osun, and his eventual adoption of the Accord Party ticket, confirmed the opportunistic fluidity of Nigerian politics. When the EFCC restricted a state government account days before the poll over an investigation involving alleged N11 billion fund movements, controversy deepened. President Bola Tinubu subsequently directed the EFCC to vacate the freezing order, warning about its timing.
More troubling was the violence. Three politically linked killings were reported at Ikire, Ilobu and Esa-Oke, while an APC campaign procession in Ede suffered a fatal truck accident that killed one person and injured seven. These incidents showed how easily political competition can slide into bloodshed. The APC then brought its national machinery into Osun. Its campaign council included governors, federal lawmakers and party leaders, with Imo Governor Hope Uzodimma as chairman and Yobe Governor Mai Mala Buni, Senate President Godswill Akpabio and House Speaker Tajudeen Abbas as co-chairmen.
The ballot demonstrated that political heavyweights from outside the state cannot substitute for voters’ consent. The principal contenders were Adeleke of the Accord Party, Bola Oyebamiji of the APC and Najeem Salaam of the ADC. Adeleke won with 511,067 votes, against Oyebamiji’s 444,815, while Salaam finished a distant third. The margin of 66,252 votes was substantial enough to establish a clear verdict.
Remarkably, polling day itself was largely peaceful, notwithstanding isolated breaches of the electoral law. The huge crowds that gathered at collation centres on Saturday night, 15th August 2026, to “protect the vote” were encouraging. They demonstrated that Nigerians are increasingly unwilling to surrender their votes to manipulations behind closed doors.
INEC deserves commendation for conducting a credible exercise whose declared outcome reflected the electorate’s clear choice. This is precisely the confidence the commission must carry into 2027, avoiding the failures associated with former chairman Mahmood Yakubu, whose promises of improved electoral technology and transparency were dashed on Presidential election day.
President Tinubu also deserves commendation for congratulating the winner. Osun APC, Oyebamiji and other co-contenders should accept the result, unless they possess credible evidence warranting a judicial challenge.
The 2027 campaigns and elections must build on the strengths of the Osun guber, avoiding its violence, intimidation and abuse of state power. Opposition candidates must be free to campaign, voters must vote without fear, and INEC must protect every ballot. The people must prevail.
Adeleke, having renewed the people’s mandate, must now prove that their choice was deserved.

By Godwin Oritse
Crude oil maintained its position as the leading commodity on the import charts across Lagos ports in August, with a total volume of 2,392,354 metric tonnes recorded during the month.
Data showed that 1,867,712 metric tonnes of crude oil arrived at the Lekki Deep Sea Port in the first week of August, while another 524,742 metric tonnes was expected to be discharged at the Lagos Apapa Quays before the end of the month.
The figures indicate sustained dominance of crude oil among commodities handled through the Lagos ports during the period.
Crude oil is closely followed by bulk wheat with a total of 321,849 metric tons,an indication that the confectionery industry is experiencing a boost. Also recall that while 176,243 metric tons in the first week of the month as against 145,606 metric tons being expected towards the end of the month.
Other commodities that were captured in the chart include aviation fuel with a total of 118,000 metric tons against 44,000 recorded for bulk fertilizer. Recall that crude oil imports have led the two major ports in Lagos ( Lekki port and Papa port) in the month of August. Besides crude oil that topped the chart, aviation fuel amongst other commodities also made the chart.
The statistics showed that as of August 10, 2026, aviation fuel, Automated Gas Oil (AGO) and Premium Motor Spirit (PMS), popularly known as petrol, were among the major products recorded. A breakdown of the figures showed that a total of 1,525,612 metric tonnes of crude oil came into the country through the port for onward distribution across the country.
Of this volume, aviation fuel accounted for the largest share, with 245,600 metric tonnes, followed by Automated Gas Oil (AGO), which recorded 104,000 metric tonnes.
There was, however, no record of crude oil imports during the period under review. Other commodities on the import chart included Bulk Urea, with 99,000 metric tonnes. Although no containerised cargo was recorded during the period at the Lekki Port, a total of 25 vessels were involved in the shipment of imports through the port within the first 10 days of August.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
Mikel Arteta revealed he has had difficult conversations with forwards Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus as both Brazilian internationals appear set to depart Arsenal.
"It's inevitable, at some point you need to have certain discussions and say certain things that sometimes are tough," said Arteta.
Martinelli left training early on Thursday amid speculation he is set for a move to Saudi side Al Hilal for a fee that could reportedly rise to £50million ($68 million).
"I think everybody knows and recognises how much we love Gabi (Martinelli). Whatever the outcome is, it will be because everybody agrees to that," added Arteta.
Jesus has fallen well down the pecking order during an injury disrupted time in north London and was not even included in training on Thursday as he enters the final 12 months of his contract.
"It's something to do with the numbers that we have in the squad at the moment and the way we're managing that kind of situation individually with all the players -- they have some personal situations," Arteta said of the former Manchester City striker.
Arsenal have been linked with bolstering their forward line with a move for Atletico Madrid's Julian Alvarez.
The Argentine is caught in an acrimonious stand-off after Atletico refused to let him depart the Spanish capital for Barcelona.
"Don't go there," said Arteta about Arsenal's interest in Alvarez. "I'm not going to make any comment about any player that is not with us."
Ezri Konsa is already an Arsenal player and could make his debut back at Villa Park on Monday after securing a £51 million move from Aston Villa.
The England international could receive a frosty reception but Arteta said that would not influence his decision in throwing Konsa into action.
"If I see something different in the player then I may have a question about that, but the way I've seen Ezri since day one, knowing his personality really well and through people that have worked with him, I have no concern there."
Bruno Guimaraes could also be fit to make his first competitive Arsenal appearance after missing the 3-0 win over Coventry last weekend due to a groin problem.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
Alison Dos Santos and Masai Russell each set a world record while Armand 'Mondo' Duplantis won a historic pole vault in a barmy night of track and field in Zurich on Thursday that would have more than appeased onlooking World Athletics president Sebastian Coe.
"I expect the Olympic Games in two hours," Coe said of his expectations of the penultimate Diamond League meet of the season.
The Swiss city's Letzigrund Stadium had a raucous sell-out 25,000 crowd and the still, balmy weather conditions helped no end for a heady night of athletics.
Brazil's Dos Santos was first up, clocking a sensational 45.80 seconds to beat the previous mark of 45.94sec set by Norway's Karsten Warholm when winning gold at the Tokyo Olympics.
"I have been showing great form throughout the season -- that I am fast, I am strong," said a confident Dos Santos, with Warholm finishing second and dubbing their discipline a "crazy event".
"As soon as I knew I was coming here, I was excited. The weather's good, the track's amazing," the Brazilian added.
Then came Russell, the Olympic champion of the US timing 12.09sec to beat the previous best of 12.12sec set by Nigeria's Tobi Amusan at the Eugene world championships in 2022.
Both Dos Santos and Russell will leave Zurich with a cheque each for $80,000 for having broken their respective records.
The world records were punctuated by a scintillating competition in the pole vault, eventually won by double Olympic and triple world champion Duplantis.
The US-born Swede came under real pressure from Greek rival Emmanouil Karalis, who vaulted a personal best of 6.20m.
Duplantis cleared 6.25m for victory, while both vaulters tried a possible world record 6.32m, in a truly thrilling showdown that gripped the stadium's attention.
It was the first time in vaulting history that two athletes had gone beyond the 6.20m mark.
"It's not every day two people go for the world record, so that was nuts," said Karalis.
Werro edges nearer
The icing on the cake came in the women's 800m, with the star attraction Switzerland's own Audrey Werro.
Werro also did not disappoint, registering the third fastest time ever in the two-lap race, 1:53.70, as she edged ever closer to Jarmila Kratochvilova's Cold War world record of 1:53.28 set in Munich in 1983. 
"It was crazy, I am very proud. Thank you everybody!" the 22-year-old beamed.
Femke Broeders-Bol finished second as she continues to improve in her transition from the 400m hurdles in which she was twice a world champion.
"Being in a great event with a great time -- amazing," the Dutch athlete said.
Kenya's world and Olympic champion Emmanuel Wanyonyi held off Algeria's Djamel Sedjati for a nail-biting victory in the men's 800m.
Wanyonyi has said that going for David Rudisha's world record of 1:40.91 was like running a marathon under two hours, and it once again proved elusive as he timed a world lead of 1:41.76 for the win, Sedjati just 0.07sec adrift.
"When I see the world records being broken, I know my time will come. There is time for everything," said Wanyonyi.
US Olympic champion Cole Hocker, the world champ over 5,000m, claimed victory in a high-quality men's 1,500m in 3:31.71 ahead of Kenya's Phanuel Kipkosgei Koech.
Norway's Jakob Ingebrigtsen came in fifth as he continues his return to the track after an Achilles tendon injury that required surgery.
Olympic silver medallist Anna Cockrell bettered Broeders-Bol's meet record set last year by 0.05sec to win the 400m hurdles in 52.13sec ahead of US teammate Dalilah Muhammad.
American Parker Wolfe smashed the meet record in the men's non-Olympic distance of 3,000m, clocking a personal best of 7:27.43 to better Moroccan Said Aouita's previous best set in 1986 by more than 5sec.
And there was another world lead in the men's 200m by American Kenny Bednarek, who won in some style in 19.62sec.
World champion and two-time Olympic silver medallist Nicola Olyslagers of Australia won the women's high jump in a season's best of 2.02m.

items.title: Obafemi Hamzat and the Lagos State future: Between electoral expediency and governing reality
items.summary:

As the 2027 general election approaches with the inexorable certainty of a tide that waits for no man, there is a familiar rhythm that plays out across the political landscape of Lagos State. items.author: Emmanuel Okogba
items.content:
By MOSHOOD OSHUNFUREWA
As the 2027 general election approaches with the inexorable certainty of a tide that waits for no man, there is a familiar rhythm that plays out across the political landscape of Lagos State. The air thickens with promises, the streets swell with campaign paraphernalia, and those who hold power-or seek to-suddenly discover a newfound lenity toward behaviours that, in less politically charged seasons, would invite swift rebuke. Political supporters and cronies, emboldened by the proximity of the ballot, conduct themselves with an impunity that suggests the rules of governance have been suspended. Yet, for all the theatre of electoral politics, one truth remains stubbornly undeniable: the reality that will confront the next government, whether it be that of Dr. Obafemi Hamzat or another, will not be swayed by campaign slogans or the frenzied loyalty of party faithful.
Dr. Obafemi Hamzat, the Lagos State deputy governor who recently emerged as the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate with a resounding 657,917 votes against his sole rival’s single vote, stands at the threshold of history as the first deputy governor to secure a governorship ticket in the state. With the endorsement of President Bola Tinubu and Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu, his path to the pinnacle of Lagos politics appears assured. But the question that must be asked, and asked with the urgency that the moment demands, is whether the machinery of electoral victory can translate into the machinery of effective governance. For the challenges that await are not the stuff of political rhetoric; they are the gritty, unglamorous, and deeply consequential realities of a megacity straining at its seams.
Consider, first, the hydra-headed monster of housing that has turned the Lagos dream into a nightmare for millions. The Lagos State Government has unveiled the Tenancy and Recovery of Premises Bill 2025, a legislative effort to curb arbitrary rent increases, cap advance rent at one year, and limit agency fees to five per cent. The bill also empowers courts to determine whether rent hikes are reasonable by comparing rents in similar locations. On paper, this is commendable progress. But the gap between legislation and lived reality yawns as wide as the Atlantic.
The statistics are staggering. According to June 2026 rental estimates from Statisense, the average annual asking rent for a two-bedroom apartment in Lagos climbed to N8.1 million, representing a 22.7 per cent increase from the previous year. A worker earning the Lagos State minimum wage of N85,000 monthly would need almost eight years of total earnings to afford that single year’s rent. In upscale areas, annual rents for one-bedroom apartments have reached as high as N20.9 million. Residents now spend between 50 and 70 per cent of their income on rent, far above the globally recommended threshold of 30 per cent. One resident of Ajegunle, Ketu, Isolo, Badagry, to mention but a few, saw his rent for a single room rise from N800,000 to N1,500,000 in a single year; when he could not afford it, his landlord told him to move out. This is not a housing crisis; this is a housing catastrophe.
The new tenancy law, however well-intentioned, cannot by itself solve a crisis rooted in a housing deficit estimated at 29 million units nationwide and a population projected to reach 34 million within the next four years. The question for the next government is not whether it can pass laws, but whether it can build homes, and build them at a scale and speed that match the demographic tidal wave.
Then there is the matter of security, or rather, the growing insecurity that has transformed Lagos from Africa’s commercial capital into a theatre of lawlessness. The government has warned celebrities and residents against giving money to “area boys” and street miscreants, arguing that such acts only fuel insecurity. The warning came after a viral video showed touts chasing the convoy of Afrobeats superstar Burna Boy. But the problem runs far deeper than celebrity harassment. Along the Lekki-Epe Expressway, homeless boys and teenagers have been terrorising motorists with harassment, extortion, and assault. Deputy Governor Hamzat has vowed to remove these “car spotters” from the streets, describing their actions as “strictly criminal” and confirming that arrests have been made.
Yet the rot extends beyond street-level thuggery. In August 2026, suspected land grabbers and hundreds of armed thugs invaded Santos Layout, Valley Estate, and adjoining communities in Alimosho, vandalising homes and businesses over a three-day rampage. Residents alleged that about 400 armed thugs stormed the communities, armed with bottles and openly smoking, while police stood by. One resident’s desperate plea captures the depth of the crisis: “We don’t trust the police or the military anymore. They even told us the courts are not sitting now, so what are we supposed to do?”
Infrastructure vandalism has reached epidemic proportions. Scavengers have been caught on CCTV removing iron reinforcements from the pillars of the Alakija-Festac link bridge, compromising its structural integrity. Thirty suspected vandals were recently sentenced to two months’ imprisonment each for vandalising bridges across Lagos. But two months for compromising the safety of thousands of lives? This is not justice; this is a mockery of it. The Lagos State House of Assembly has called for tougher measures, but the question remains: will the next government have the political will to match rhetoric with action?
Perhaps the most troubling dimension of Lagos governance is the cancer of corruption at the local government level-a cancer that has metastasised to the point where democracy itself has become a curse rather than a blessing. The revelations are nothing short of scandalous. A former chairperson of a Local Council Development Area received N512 million from the Federation Account three days before her tenure ended, spent N492 million in 72 hours, and left behind a paltry N20 million for her successor. According to verifiable records, the same LCDA received N4.8 billion in allocation between January and July 2025. A newly built multi-million-naira hotel in Osogbo and a property in Magodo GRA Phase 2 have been linked to this same former chairperson.
The report submitted to the Speaker of the Lagos State House of Assembly paints a damning picture: “The brazen mismanagement of public funds by immediate past and newly elected Local Government chairmen in Lagos State is unparalleled by any Local Government in Nigeria.” There is a disturbing pattern of looting, particularly the diversion of monthly Joint Allocation Committee funds. The report further alleges that management officials buy their postings from the Local Government Service Commission at costs ranging from N5 million to N20 million, with monthly premiums of N2.5 million for “Category A” local governments. One chairman has allegedly embarked on lavish trips to London, Saudi Arabia, and Dubai for “birthday festivities of an urbane Oba,” while another stands accused of siphoning over N2 billion to construct private properties.
In this cesspool of corruption, thugs are appointed as supervisors and senior special assistants. Empowerment programmes are run without transparency or accountability, their records as ambiguous as an elephant’s footprint in a dust storm. The social contract between the government and the governed has been shredded, and in its place we have a system where political patronage trumps public service, where loyalty to party is rewarded with access to the public till, and where the people for whom democracy was supposedly designed are reduced to mere spectators in their own dispossession.
The next government cannot afford to ignore this rot. The question is not whether Dr. Hamzat, if elected, will be complicit in these practices-his record as deputy governor suggests a technocratic disposition-but whether he will have the courage and the political capital to confront a system that has made corruption its operating system. The local government system in Lagos, with its 20 local governments and 37 LCDAs, represents the frontline of governance for millions of residents. If that frontline is manned by looters and their cronies, then the entire edifice of democratic governance is a hollow sham.
Beyond these immediate crises lies the deeper question of infrastructure and the cost of living-the twin pillars upon which the liveability of Lagos rests. Deputy Governor Hamzat has disclosed that the state has spent more than N700 billion on road rehabilitation over the past 15 years. The Lagos State Public Works Corporation has expanded its maintenance gangs from 14 to 34 teams. There are now 9,911 roads across the state requiring regular maintenance. Yet the scale of the challenge far outstrips the resources available. Hamzat himself has acknowledged that available resources remain inadequate compared with the scale of infrastructure needs. The proposed Fourth Mainland Bridge remains on the government’s agenda but requires substantial financial resources.
Transportation, the lifeblood of any megacity, has become a source of daily anguish for millions. BRT fares increased by 13 per cent in 2026, following an 18 per cent increase in February 2025. Commuters lament that these increases came despite modest energy prices. A worker interviewed by BusinessDay noted that her daily transport cost had risen from N900 to N1,300. When transportation consumes such a significant portion of a worker’s income, and when rent consumes 50 to 70 per cent of that same income, the result is a population that is perpetually one crisis away from destitution.
The Nigeria Labour Congress has demanded a minimum wage of N150,000 for Lagos workers, arguing that the current N85,000 is insufficient to cover basic needs. Even a proposed N225,000 minimum wage, some experts argue, may still not be enough given the astronomical cost of housing, transportation, and food in Lagos. This is the arithmetic of survival in Lagos, and it does not favour the ordinary resident.
Then there is the scourge of hard drugs-a crisis that has been allowed to fester while the government focuses on enforcement rather than rehabilitation. The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency has reported that some rehabilitated clients are now excelling academically, and the agency has partnered with organisations to provide skills development. But these efforts remain woefully inadequate compared with the scale of the problem. The question is not merely how to punish offenders but how to rehabilitate them, how to develop skills that can make Lagos self-sufficient and capable of exporting specialised expertise. A society that only punishes without rehabilitating is a society that has given up on redemption-and on itself.
Food and agricultural needs present another frontier of governance failure. The Lagos State Government has unveiled ambitious plans: a N1 trillion food security fund, a N16.14 trillion food economy plan, and a target of 40 per cent food self-sufficiency through the cultivation of over 30,000 hectares of agricultural land. Over 66,000 beneficiaries have received support through various agricultural initiatives. A mid-level agro-produce hub has been unveiled in Agege. Yet the gap between planning and implementation remains vast. Food prices continue to soar, and the dream of food security remains distant for millions who struggle to put three square meals on their tables.
The truth, and we need sincerity that can only be achieved by being truthful to ourselves, is that Lagos is at a crossroads. The election of 2027 will not be a mere transfer of power; it will be a verdict on whether the political class is capable of rising above its self-interest to address the existential challenges confronting the state. Dr. Obafemi Hamzat has promised to “continue to build a Lagos that works for all.” But the path from promise to performance is littered with the debris of broken pledges.
The social contract in Lagos is broken. The people pay taxes, endure daily hardships, and watch as their leaders enrich themselves while the infrastructure crumbles, the rent soars, the miscreants roam freely, and the cost of living becomes a sentence of perpetual struggle. The next government, whether led by Hamzat or another, must recognise that the days of business as usual are over. The people are watching, and they are angry. The 2027 election will not be won by those who merely promise; it will be won by those who have demonstrated the capacity to deliver.
For Lagos to fulfil its promise as Africa’s greatest city, it must first confront its greatest failures. The housing crisis demands not just laws but homes. The security crisis demands not just arrests but a fundamental rethinking of how safety is guaranteed. The corruption crisis demands not just investigations but a systemic cleansing of the local government system. The infrastructure crisis demands not just budgets but the political will to prioritise the needs of the many over the interests of the few.
The question before us is not whether Femi Hamzat will be the next governor of Lagos State; that seems increasingly likely. The question is whether he and those who will govern alongside him have the vision, the courage, and the integrity to confront the hydra-headed monsters that threaten to consume the Lagos dream. The answer to that question will determine not just the future of one man or one administration, but the future of Lagos itself. And that future, dear reader, is a future we cannot afford to leave to chance.
The post Obafemi Hamzat and the Lagos State future: Between electoral expediency and governing reality appeared first on Vanguard News.

items.content:
Moonton baru saja mengumumkan pembagian slot untuk turnamen Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB) paling bergengsi di dunia, yakni M8 World Championship.
Setelah bertahun-tahun digelar hanya di area Asia, kompetisi MLBB yang mempertemukan tim-tim terbaik di masing-masing region ini akan menyambangi benua Eropa.
Digelar pada Januari 2027, sebanyak 16 tim akan berlaga di Main Stage M8 di Istanbul, Turkiye. Sebagai salah satu wilayah turnamen terpanas di Asia, Indonesia mendapatkan jatah terbesar lewat MPL Indonesia.
Baca Juga: Jadwal MPL ID S18 Hari Ini 22 Agustus: Onic vs RRQ Hoshi
Untuk pertama kalinya, MLBB Championship Tour atau MCT akan terhubung langsung dengan M Series, termasuk MCT Southeast Asia yang memberi kesempatan kepada juara MDL Indonesia untuk mengejar tiket M8 World Championship.
MPL ID Tetap Dapat 2 Slot ke M8 World Championship
Berdasarkan alokasi resmi Moonton, enam dari 16 tempat Main Stage berasal dari tiga liga franchise utama MLBB, sebagaimana dikutip dari keterangan Moonton, Jumat (27/8/2026).
MPL Indonesia mendapat dua slot, MPL Philippines dua slot, dan MPL Malaysia dua slot. Tujuh tiket lainnya dialokasikan melalu kompetisi regional: dua dari MCT SEA, dua dari EMEA, serta masing-masing satu dari EECA, MCT East Asia, dan MCT Americas.
Tiga posisi terakhir akan diisi tim yang lolos dari Wild Card. Artinya, jumlah peserta Main Stage tidak bertambah dibanding M7. Perubahan terjadi pada jalur menuju turnamen tersebut.
M7 mempertemukan 14 tim yang lolos langsung dengan dua pemenang Wild Card. Pada M8, jumlah tiket langsung berkurang menjadi 13, sementara Wild Card mendapat tiga tiket Main Stage.
Wild Card M8 World Championship sendiri akan digelar di Bangkok, Thailand, dengan 10 peserta. Mereka berasal dari EMEA, EECA, SEA, MCT East Asia, dan MCT Americas.
Juara MDL Indonesia Berkesempatan ke M8 World Championship
Dua tiket MPL ID bukan satu-satunya jalur yang melibatkan tim Indonesia. Perusahaan asal China itu sebelumnya mengumumkan MCT SEA sebagai kompetisi regional baru yang menghubungkan liga dan kualifikasi di Asia Tenggara dengan M8.
Juara MDL Indonesia akan masuk ke Open League Qualifier Group bersama juara MDL Philippines dan MLBB Academy League Malaysia. Ketiga tim tersebut memperebutkan satu tempat di Knockout Playoffs MCT SEA.
Dua tim terbaik di Knockout Playoffs MCT SEA akan mendapat tiket langsung ke Main Stage M8 di Istanbul. Tim peringkat ketiga dan keempat akan melanjutkan perjalanan melalui Wild Card di Bangkok.
Secara struktur, sistem ini membuka peluang bagi Indonesia untuk memiliki wakil M8 di luar dua tim dari MPL ID. Namun, jalur tersebut tidak bisa disebut sebagai “slot ketiga Indonesia”.
Juara MDL ID masih harus mengalahkan wakil open league Filipina dan Malaysia untuk mencapai playoff MCT SEA, kemudian bersaing dengan tim dari negara Asia Tenggara lain untuk benar-benar mendapatkan tiket M8.
Jadi, dua slot MPL ID tetap menjadi jatah langsung Indonesia. Jalur MDL ID melalui MCT SEA adalah peluang tambahan yang harus diperjuangkan.
Ekspansi Terjadi Saat Persaingan MLBB Lebih Terbuka
Perubahan struktur M8 datang setelah hasil yang tidak biasa di Mid Season Cup 2026.
Team Spirit dari kawasan EECA mengalahkan Yangon Galacticos asal Myanmar dengan skor 4-3 di Grand Final MSC 2026. Moonton menyebut Team Spirit sebagai tim pertama dari luar Asia Tenggara yang menjuarai major internasional resmi MLBB.
Dari sisi penonton, MSC 2026 juga menjadi kompetisi dengan peak viewers tertinggi di Esports World Cup 2026. Esports Charts mencatat sekitar 2,89 juta peak viewers, yang tercapai pada perempat final antara ONIC dan Aurora Gaming.
Angka tersebut tetap besar, meski bukan rekor baru MSC. Esports Charts mencatat peak viewers MSC 2026 turun sekitar 5,9 persen dibanding edisi 2025 sebelumnya yang mencatatkan angka penonton puncak lebih tinggi.
Konteks ini membuat ekspansi M8 lebih menarik untuk diperhatikan. MLBB masih sangat kuat di Asia Tenggara, tetapi hasil MSC menunjukkan tim dari kawasan lain mulai mampu menembus level tertinggi.
M8 akan menjadi salah satu ujian berikutnya: apakah jalur regional yang lebih luas hanya menambah keragaman peserta, atau benar-benar menghasilkan persaingan internasional yang lebih merata.
Untuk Indonesia, pertanyaannya lebih dekat. Dua tiket langsung MPL ID sudah tersedia. Kini ada satu jalur lain dari MDL Indonesia menuju MCT SEA dan, jika perjalanan itu berhasil, hingga panggung dunia di Istanbul.

items.author: AFP
items.content:
Raphinha and Fermin Lopez goals helped Spanish champions Barcelona beat Athletic Bilbao 2-0 on Thursday in La Liga to continue their perfect start to the season.
The Catalan giants eased to a solid victory over their Basque visitors in their first game of the season at the partially-rebuilt Camp Nou, with new arrival Rodri coming on for his Barca debut.
Raphinha rounded the goalkeeper and slid home in the 37th minute to give Barca the lead, and Lopez netted after 82 minutes to secure the points, with the Catalans missing several chances for more goals and twice hitting the woodwork.
"Very happy to play my first game, happy with the victory, we've got two from two," Rodri told DAZN.
"It's important to keep building up rhythm and adapting to this great team. My first minutes and (I had some) good feelings."
Barca coach Hansi Flick made three changes to the team that thrashed Elche 5-0 last weekend, handing Anthony Gordon his first start for the club, while bringing Pedri Gonzalez into midfield and picking Pau Cubarsi in defence.
The German kept Raphinha playing up front as a makeshift number nine, after the departures of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres.
Barca have fruitlessly tried to pry Julian Alvarez away from Atletico Madrid, who will not negotiate with the Spanish champions for the Argentina forward.
However, Raphinha netted twice from his striker's role against Elche and was on target again for Barca at Camp Nou, giving them a deserved lead at half-time.
"It doesn't matter which position Rapha plays, as a captain he's shown total commitment to this team, to this club," Flick told reporters.
"You can see the supporters are connected with him and it's really good."
The Brazilian nodded against the post from Xavi Espart's cross midway through the first half and Lamine Yamal's follow-up effort was deflected wide, with Barca controlling the game.
Eventually, they took the lead when Pedri slipped Raphinha through on goal, with the Brazilian rounding Unai Simon and rolling home.
Teenage star Yamal should have doubled Barca's lead before the interval but Simon made a fine save to deny him, while Gordon complained that he would have had an open goal if the Spain international had knocked the ball across to him.
Gordon arrowed a shot narrowly over early in the second half as Barcelona probed for a second goal.
Yamal, still not at his best level since suffering a hamstring injury in April, hit the crossbar with an effort from the edge of the box. Simon saved twice from Lopez, who netted a brace in the opener.
Flick sent on former Manchester City midfielder Rodri for his debut in midfield, leaving 10 Spaniards and Gordon on the pitch for Barca.
Securing the points
The champions were in the ascendency but Athletic threatened on a rare venture forward, with Oihan Sancet drilling against the post.
Barcelona eventually found their second after a mistake from Athletic defender Aymeric Laporte, clumsily nudging Barca substitute Karim Adeyemi's cross past Simon, for Lopez to tuck into an empty net.
Adeyemi should have netted a third late on when Yamal picked him out at the back post but Simon denied the German from point-blank range.
Yamal's second half performance was an improvement on a disappointing opening 45 minutes and his struggles against Elche, and Rodri said that the forward is improving.
"Maybe Lamine came from a moment where he was a bit down and today we tried to help him get back up and saw his best version, even though he didn't score," added Rodri, Spain's World Cup winning captain.
"The goals will come because the talent is there."
Athletic Bilbao have started their season with two defeats under new coach Edin Terzic.
"I'm not a constant winner, I'm a constant trier," said former Borussia Dortmund coach Terzic.
"I'm fully of belief and trust when I see how we worked in these two games and in the training ground, sooner or later we'll get what we deserve and turn results in our favour."

items.author: AFP
items.content:
Arsenal are out to inflict more damage on a wounded Aston Villa, while Tottenham are desperate to see some return for their £300 million ($408 million) investment in new signings when Newcastle visit north London.
New Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola also makes his home bow at Anfield against Nottingham Forest and Manchester United badly need to bounce back from an opening weekend shocker at Hull when Ipswich visit Old Trafford.
AFP Sports looks at the pick of the Premier League action.
Villa torn apart
Ezri Konsa could make his Arsenal debut to a frosty reception on his return to Villa Park.
The England international is just one of a series of departures from Villa in recent months which has torn apart the side that won the Europa League and finished fourth in the Premier League last season.
Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea for £117 million, while Youri Tielemans moved to Manchester United and Lucas Digne departed for Paris Saint-Germain.
Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez appear set to join the exodus before the transfer window shuts.
A depleted Villa found themselves 4-0 down to Brighton inside 31 minutes last weekend.
Worse could be to come against an Arsenal side brimming with the confidence of champions.
Mikel Arteta's men have swatted aside Manchester City and Coventry 3-0 to pick up the Community Shield and make a perfect start to their title defence.
The depth of options available to the Gunners means Konsa may even have to wait for his chance to shine despite the absence of William Saliba to a long-term back injury.
But Villa captain John McGinn remains hopeful they can still have a successful season as long as Unai Emery remains in charge.
"I'm still positive about the season but we need to make sure we keep hold of the manager," McGinn told the Stick to Football podcast. "If we lose him, it's a different story."
De Zerbi sets Savio target
Spurs have fans have been waiting years for their club to be the Premier League's big spenders, but were brought back down to earth with a 3-0 pummelling by Brentford last weekend.
Since then Savio and Omar Marmoush have joined from Manchester City for combined fees that could reach nearly £150 million.
Savio's £75 million price tag has attracted astonishment from some after failing to make the grade in two years at City, but Roberto De Zerbi is confident the Brazilian can help transform Spurs' fortunes after two 17th-placed finishes in the Premier League.
"I think his biggest step and biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals because as qualities, I think he is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals," said De Zerbi after Savio scored on his debut against Charlton in the League Cup on Wednesday.
"Last season we suffered too much because also the number of goals were not enough to compete for nothing more than that (17th) position."
Anfield awaits Iraola
Liverpool needed a 99th-minute penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai to salvage a point in Iraola's first game in charge from a 2-2 draw at Newcastle.
The growing pains of a change in style to Iraola's high-energy pressing game were obvious as twice Liverpool were cut open by Newcastle counter-attacks to score.
Forest have won at Anfield in each of the past two seasons, but Iraola is hoping to have an afternoon to savour in his first competitive game at home.
"I think it's going to be emotional and I think it has to be like this. It is a special place," said the Spaniard. 
"I've had to fight a lot to arrive to this place and I hope everything goes well and I can enjoy also the game."

items.content:
By Folarin Kehinde
The Federal Government has warned that 915 communities across 19 states and the Federal Capital Territory are at critical risk of flooding between August 27 and September 9, 2026, urging residents in the affected areas to take immediate precautionary measures and prepare for possible evacuation.
The National Flood Early Warning Systems Centre classified 915 communities across the affected areas as being at critical flood risk, requiring immediate watch, preparedness and protective action.
Another 429 communities in seven states were classified as high risk, while 656 communities across 13 states were placed on moderate-risk watch.
The critical-risk states are Kogi, Benue, Rivers, Edo, Delta, Cross River, Bayelsa, Akwa Ibom, Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu, Imo, Ekiti, Lagos, Ogun, Ondo, Osun and Oyo.
Major cities and communities listed include Lokoja, Makurdi, Port Harcourt, Benin City, Asaba, Calabar, Yenagoa, Uyo, Aba, Onitsha, Enugu, Owerri, Lagos, Abeokuta, Akure, Osogbo and Ibadan.
The federal government  attributed the projected flood risk to a combination of high soil moisture, rainfall, rapid surface runoff, drainage surcharge and rising river levels.
In the advisory signed by the Director, Erosion, Flood and Coastal Zone Management Department, Usman Abdullahi Bokani, the government urged residents in critical-risk areas to maintain immediate flood watch and verify evacuation routes.
It also advised residents to protect vulnerable households and essential property, and to avoid settlement, parking, trading, or storage activities within floodplains, wetlands, riverbanks, and low-lying drainage corridors.
The government directed state emergency management agencies, environmental officers and community flood focal persons to intensify surveillance around rivers, streams, culverts, bridges, drains, estuaries, reservoirs and erosion-prone corridors.
Communities classified as high risk in Benue, Kogi, Kwara, Niger, Adamawa, Taraba and Kebbi states were advised to intensify drainage clearance and monitor culverts and watercourses.
The Federal Capital Territory and communities in Nasarawa, Plateau, Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Yobe, Zamfara, Sokoto, Katsina, Kano and Kaduna were among those placed on the moderate-risk watchlist.
The Federal government warned that prolonged or consecutive rainfall could rapidly increase flood risk in communities currently classified as moderate.
Residents were urged to comply with evacuation instructions from competent authorities, keep children away from floodwater and avoid driving or walking through flowing water.
They were also advised to disconnect electricity where inundation was imminent and safeguard medicines, important documents, food and potable water.
The government stressed that the forecast should be interpreted alongside real-time local observations, drainage conditions, river levels and official emergency directives.
It added that feedback from state governments, stakeholders and community focal persons would support field validation and continuous updating of the national flood-risk database.

items.author: Nwafor
items.content:
…Minister demands refund of contract money
….Fumes over vandalism on Second Niger Bridge
By Egufe Yafugborhi & Ochuko Akuopha
ASABA — Minister of Works, Senator David Umahi, on Wednesday ordered the arrest of the Managing Director of Hartland Nigeria Ltd over the alleged non-performance of an 11-kilometre road contract for which the company reportedly received about N14 billion.
Umahi gave the directive during an inspection of road infrastructure along the Agbor-Asaba-Onitsha corridor in Delta State, expressing anger that the contractor had completed only about 40 per cent of the work despite receiving the funds.
The minister said the contract covered the 11-kilometre stretch from Summit Junction to the head bridge, including channelisation and hydraulic structures.
He disclosed that he had previously contacted the company’s managing director to discuss its return to the site, but said the contractor had failed to meet its obligations.
“I’ve called the MD to discuss their return to the site. I am going to look for him and have him arrested. I’m going to arrest him,” Umahi declared.
Turning to the ministry’s Controller, he ordered: “Controller, look for the MD of Hartland and arrest him.”
Umahi also directed ministry officials to begin moves to recover the money paid to the contractor.
“Engineer Musa, tell the Directors of C&R to call up the APG immediately. You have to write to the banks to refund that money to us,” he ordered.
The minister said the agreement with the contractor was for the completion of the entire 11-kilometre stretch, alongside the channelisation and hydraulic structures.
“When I paid them that money, we reached an agreement: they were to finish 11 kilometres from Summit Junction to this head bridge with that money, as well as handle the channelisation and hydraulic structures. That was the agreement,” he said.
“Today, they have only completed about 40 per cent of what was agreed upon,” he added.
Umahi described the contractor’s performance as unacceptable, saying: “Look at the kind of mess we are dealing with! Failing to do even simple filling on the road is pure wickedness.”
He directed that both sides of the bridge approach be filled immediately.
“By tomorrow morning, both sides of this head bridge must be filled,” he ordered.
The minister further ordered an audit of Hartland’s payment records and certificates across all its projects, warning that the company would face sanctions if found wanting.
“They must submit all their payment records and certificates. Execute this instruction and report back to me. This is very important. Audit every one of their certificates across all jobs—we are going to sanction Hartland,” he said.
Anger over Second Niger Bridge vandalism
Umahi also expressed outrage over the vandalism of critical infrastructure on the Second Niger Bridge, disclosing that bolts, steel members and expansion joints had been removed.
“We are not mad dogs. We can’t be suffering to fix these things while the public is busy removing them. It’s not possible. Where is the money to fix it?” he queried.
He warned that continued vandalism could compromise the safety of the bridge and lead to a catastrophic incident.
“The Ministry does not have an emergency fund to attend to this, and if this is not attended to, it can result in a catastrophic situation. I am visibly very angry about this situation, and it is unacceptable,” Umahi said.
He consequently directed the immediate repair of the damaged components, alongside enhanced security surveillance on the bridge.
The minister also ordered the installation of solar-powered lighting and closed-circuit television cameras, with access to the CCTV feeds to be granted to designated ministry officials and security agencies.
He further inspected erosion damage around the Second Niger Bridge and directed that remedial work commence immediately.

items.title: Iran’s parliament speaker hits back at US Treasury secretary on foreign spending

items.content:
12MW Independent Power Plant to Enhance Electricity Supply Across Ogba, Acme Road, Wemco Road and Environs
Sahara Power Enterprise Group (SPEG), Africa’s largest private power business, has commenced construction of a 12MW Independent Power Plant (IPP) at the Ogba Undertaking of Ikeja Electric Plc, Lagos, reinforcing efforts to strengthen electricity infrastructure and improve power supply reliability.
The US$12 million project, scheduled for completion in the first quarter of 2027, will comprise six 2MW gas-fired generating units and provide reliable, cost-effective electricity to industrial clusters, businesses, residential communities and public institutions across Ogba, Acme Road, Wemco Road and surrounding areas.
Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony, Kola Adesina, Group Managing Director, Sahara Power Enterprise Group, said the project demonstrates Sahara’s commitment to delivering practical solutions that support Nigeria’s energy future.
“This initiative is about much more than breaking ground for a new power plant. It represents a bold commitment to Nigeria’s energy future and our determination to deliver dependable, efficient, and sustainable electricity to businesses and communities. Improving the availability and reliability of power will enhance productivity, growth, and value creation,” he said.
Adesina noted that the facility will deploy modern gas-powered generating technology aligned with established environmental, operational and safety standards. He also commended the Federal Government, Lagos State Government, Lagos State Electricity Regulatory Commission (LASERC), Ikeja Electric, Cummins and other stakeholders for supporting the project.
Ogochukwu Onyelucheya, Acting Chief Executive Officer, Ikeja Electric Plc, said the IPP represents an important step towards improving the quality, reliability, and sustainability of electricity supply to customers.
She described the project as a strategic investment that will provide a more dependable and cost-effective source of electricity while supporting business growth and economic development within the designated areas.
“At Ikeja Electric, our priority is to partner with forward-looking investors and developers such as SPEG to deliver innovative solutions that improve customer experience and reliable electricity supply across our network. SPEG’s investment in this IPP demonstrates the value of strategic collaboration in creating sustainable energy solutions for our customers,” she said.
Also speaking, Abdul-Ganiyu Obasa, Executive Chairman, Agege Local Government, said improved electricity supply would create an enabling environment for businesses, attract investment, and generate employment opportunities within the community.
Construction of the power plant will be undertaken by Cummins West Africa Limited.
Mark Oni-Okeke, Managing Director, Cummins West Africa Limited, said the company was delighted to partner with Sahara Power to accelerate socio-economic development through reliable and sustainable energy solutions.
Traditional ruler of Ogbaland, HRM Oba Egbeyemi Latif Oladimeji, expressed appreciation to Sahara Power for locating the project within the community and pledged the support of the palace and residents.
“You have the support of the Palace and good people of Ogba and its environs. We are eagerly looking forward to the commissioning of the Plant and the positive impact on our community,” he said.
The Ogba IPP forms part of Sahara Power Enterprise Group’s broader efforts to deploy innovative solutions across Nigeria’s electricity value chain, strengthen energy infrastructure and contribute to closing the country’s power supply gap.

items.content:
By Chioma Obinna
The Federal Government has launched a new five-year national alcohol policy aimed at reducing alcohol-related harm, tightening regulation and curbing the growing illicit alcohol market in Nigeria.
The Nigeria Alcohol Policy and Multisectoral Implementation Plan 2026–2030, launched yesterday in Abuja, provides a unified framework for government agencies and other stakeholders to address the health, social and economic consequences of alcohol consumption.
Under the policy, government will strengthen public education, responsible alcohol marketing, age and access controls, screening, treatment and rehabilitation, while improving safety, quality and traceability across the alcohol value chain.
Speaking at the launch, the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Pate, represented by the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry, Daju Kachollom, said alcohol-related harm could no longer be treated as the responsibility of the health sector alone.
Pate said the issue had implications for public health, economic development and good governance, requiring coordinated action across government.
He said: “Nigeria cannot address alcohol-related harm through fragmented interventions. We need coordination across sectors, clear responsibilities and accountability for results.”
The policy is built around four pillars: harm reduction and health promotion; industrial and economic development; multisectoral coordination and governance; and monitoring, evaluation and accountability.
Pate cited latest available World Health Organisation data showing that Nigeria’s total alcohol consumption stood at 3.2 litres of pure alcohol per person aged 15 and above in 2024.
He also linked alcohol-related risks to road safety, citing Federal Road Safety Corps figures which recorded 9,570 road traffic crashes and 5,421 deaths nationwide in 2024.
According to him, driving under the influence remains a recognised contributor to road traffic crashes, underscoring the need for stronger prevention and enforcement measures.
The minister also raised concern over the scale of illicit alcohol trading, citing industry estimates from the Spirits and Wines Association of Nigeria based on a 2024 Euromonitor survey.
He said illicit spirits and wines accounted for about 40 per cent of the market, representing an estimated annual government revenue loss of more than N428 billion.
The development adds an economic dimension to the government’s renewed push for stronger alcohol regulation, as authorities seek to protect public health while safeguarding legitimate businesses and government revenue.
In a welcome address delivered by the Director, Food and Drugs Services, Dr Olufowubi-Yusuf Adeola, the Permanent Secretary described the launch as a major milestone in the government’s efforts to strengthen alcohol governance.
She urged stakeholders to move beyond policy commitments and translate the objectives into measurable action.
The ministry also called on traditional and religious leaders, civil society organisations and the media to support implementation through public education, advocacy and community engagement.
The Director-General of the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, Professor Mojisola Adeyeye, commended the Federal Government for providing what she described as an unambiguous policy direction on alcohol control.
Adeyeye reaffirmed NAFDAC’s commitment to science-based regulation, monitoring, surveillance and stakeholder engagement.
She also restated the agency’s position on the restriction of small-volume alcohol products.
Adeyeye said NAFDAC remained committed to the ban on the sale of alcohol in sachets and containers below 200 millilitres.
The launch brought together representatives of the Federal Ministries of Finance; Industry, Trade and Investment; Nigerian Correctional Service; Nigeria Customs Service; Federal Road Safety Corps; National Drug Law Enforcement Agency; Association of Local Governments of Nigeria and other stakeholders.
The stakeholders pledged to work together in implementing the 2026–2030 plan.
The Federal Government said the policy aligns with President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, the Nigeria Health Sector Renewal Investment Initiative and international commitments under the African Union Agenda 2063, Sustainable Development Goals and relevant WHO frameworks.
The Ministry of Health and Social Welfare said it would work with government agencies, industry and civil society to ensure that the policy moves from a national framework to concrete and measurable results.
